(p-1) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-An'am

Its purpose is to provide evidence for what the Book called for in the preceding surah concerning monotheism, namely that He encompasses all perfections: bringing into existence and annihilating, power over resurrection, and other things. Among the things mentioned in it, the livestock (al-an'am) are the most fitting for this purpose, because permission regarding them, as will come, is caused by what has been established for Him of splitting (the seed and the grain) and of sole creation. The rest of its mention includes the nullification of what they took as religion from matters concerning them, since He did not permit it and did not permit anyone along with Him, because He is the One uniquely deserving of divinity, with no partner. The restriction of forbidden foods, which are most of what is forbidden in this religion and others, indicates the comprehensiveness of His knowledge. In the surah of Ta Ha will come the clear proof that the comprehensiveness of knowledge necessarily entails the all-inclusiveness of power and of the other perfections, and that is the very purpose of this surah. It has been transmitted through several chains, as I have explained in my book Masa'id al-Nazar: (p-2) that it was sent down all at once, escorted by seventy thousand angels, who have a chanting sound with glorification. In another report, its descent was at night, and the earth shook at its descent. All of it concerns the argumentation against the polytheists and others, including the innovators, the Qadariyya, and the people of deviant creeds, and upon it is built the foundations of the religion, since it contains monotheism, justice, prophethood, the return, and the refutation of the doctrines of the atheists. Its descent in this form indicates that the foundations of the religion are of the highest dignity, and that learning them is obligatory immediately, because it was sent down all at once, unlike the rulings, which are sent down in parts according to the interests involved. Its descent at night is evidence of the utmost blessing, because it is a time of intimacy, with His descent to the lowest heaven. It also shows that the secrets of this knowledge are reached only by the perceptive, awake from the sleep of heedlessness, the people of intellect who dwell in solitude, and the spirits dominant over the bodies, and they are few.

"In the name of Allah" who has shown the proofs of His unity, that He is the One who combines the attributes of perfection; "the Most Gracious" who bestowed upon all existing things from His mercy, through bringing into existence and annihilating, what perplexed understandings by its generality, so that imaginations were constricted by it; "the Most Merciful" who granted the people of faith the light of insights, until existence became speaking to them, informing them that He is the Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Source of Peace.

﴿Praise﴾, that is, the comprehensive encompassing of the attributes of perfection, ﴿belongs to Allah﴾.

When He, glorified be He, concluded the previous surah with the praise of Jesus, peace be upon him, for His majesty on that day in that gathering, and then with the praise of His holy Self through the all-inclusiveness of dominion and power, (p-3) He opened this surah, glorified and exalted be He, with the information that this praise and other praises are due to Him, a firm and perpetual entitlement, before the creation was brought into existence and after its bringing into existence, whether His servants thank Him or deny Him, because of what He possesses of attributes of majesty and perfection, as has been indicated in al-Fatiha. He begins with this nominal sentence, opened with the word "praise," which is the universal, comprehensive term that encompasses all its types, indicating totality. This is either because the definite article (al-) is for totality according to the majority, or because it is for the genus, as is the view of al-Zamakhshari, which comes back to the view of the majority, since if the genus is exclusively His, no individual of it can belong to another, for the genus exists only within its individuals; so whenever an individual of it belongs to another, the genus would be present in that other, and the genus would then not be exclusive to Him. We have said it is exclusive. This praise became, by its description, an individual of the praise of al-Fatiha, confirming that it is the Mother (of the Book). He, glorified be He, followed it with the evidence of observation, in accordance with what He concluded that surah with regarding the description of the all-inclusiveness of power, by His saying: ﴿Who created﴾.

Since the multiplicity of the heavens is evident through the stars in their courses and their movements in speed and slowness, and the concealing of some by others at eclipses, and other things (p-4) which are established among its people, He gathered them and said: ﴿the heavens﴾, that is, in their loftiness and firmness, [He placed them first because of what was mentioned just before], ﴿and the earth﴾, that is, in its adornment with benefits and its arrangement.

Since in "making" there is a meaning of containment, so that what is made does not stand by itself, He said: ﴿and made﴾, that is, brought into being and originated for your interests, ﴿the darknesses﴾, that is, the dense bodies, as previously mentioned, ﴿and the light﴾. He used the plural for the first as an alert that the ways of evil and destruction are many and revolve around desire. By this what He opened the surah with has been established, because whoever uniquely originates things is the one specially deserving of all praises, and whoever is specially deserving of all praises has no other god, and has no partner, neither a second of two nor a third of three, nor anything else. How excellent is its conclusion, after pointing to these purposes that keep far away from disbelieving in Him or equating anything with Him, with His saying: ﴿Then those who disbelieve﴾, that is, who concealed what their intellects guided them to of the evidences of His oneness, which are not hidden from anyone who strips himself of desire and treats its ailments with the most beneficial remedy, because He encompasses all the attributes of perfection. He increased the matter in ugliness against them by replacing what the original speech would have had as a pronoun with His saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to them, the One from whom they have seen no good except from Him, ﴿equate﴾, that is, they make others, who have no power over anything, equal to Him, although they know that He is the One who originated things, (p-5) disbelieving in His blessing and distant from His mercy. Some of them equated with Him some of the substances of His creation from heaven, like the stars, or from earth, like idols, or some of what arises from some of His creation of accidents, which He created, like light and darkness, while their fluctuations indicate, on the slightest reflection, two matters: the first is their distance from being fit for divinity, because of their change, ﴿He said: I do not love the setting ones﴾ [al-An'am: 76]; and the second is the power of their Creator and Changer over resurrection, by bringing each of them into being after its annihilation, as is the case with resurrection, along with other secrets that are too subtle for thoughts. The placing of darkness first suits the context of those who equate. The expression with "then" serves as an alert to what ought to have been for everyone who transgresses in this manner, that he should keep far from disbelief, since it is far from the truth. It has thus become clear that the purpose of the surah is to provide evidence for what the Book called for, which has been shown to be the guidance regarding the unity of Allah, unity in following it, and fulfilling its covenants, namely that He, glorified be He, alone is the Creator, the Possessor of all perfections, including power over resurrection and other things. How fitting this is with the conclusion of al-Ma'ida, with the mention of the Day of Gathering and that to His kingdom belongs all dominion, and He is over all things powerful. This surah is the first of the four surahs indicating all the blessings that fall under the four blessings contained in al-Fatiha, and each surah among them points to one of the four blessings. So His saying: ﴿He created the heavens and the earth﴾, the verse, then ﴿He created you from clay﴾ [al-An'am: 2], then ﴿and there is no creature on the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 38], the verse, is responsible for detailing the blessing of the first origination of all the worlds from the heavens and the earth and what is between them and what is in them, of humans and others, which is referred to in al-Fatiha by "Lord of the worlds," as previously mentioned.

Since the earlier surahs were responsible for refuting the polytheists of the Arabs, the Jews, and the Christians, along with pointing to the nullification of all kinds of polytheism, the purpose of this surah was driven into methods responsible for refuting the remaining sects: the Dualists among the Magians, who say there are two gods and two principles, light and darkness, and who acknowledge the prophethood of Abraham, peace be upon him, only; and the Sabians, who worship celestial idols and earthly idols, intermediating through them to the Lord of lords, and who deny the messengership in human form; and the people of spirituality, meaning those who manage the stars and spheres, who claim affiliation with the religion of Abraham, peace be upon him, and claim that he was one of them, while Allah has preserved him from that; and the Samanids, who say that the sun is divine. Along with emphasizing the refutation of the aforementioned sects, all their groups agree on regarding the stars, as this becomes clear to whoever looks into the books on the conquests of the lands of Persia in the days of al-Siddiq and al-Faruq, may Allah be pleased with them both. Tankalusha the Babylonian said at the beginning of his book (p-7) on the rulings of the celestial degrees: The ancient Kaldanians (Chaldeans) devised the subtle secrets of the heavens, and they had the most honored of sciences, and they did not reveal the science of the heavens to all people, but concealed most of it from their common folk, giving them of it only what suited them, and studied the rest among themselves, hidden among their scholars and sages. Then he mentioned their division of the degrees of the sphere into three hundred and sixty, then said: They divided the degrees into many divisions, until they said that some of them are male and some female, some auspicious and some inauspicious. Then he said: They intended by all of that to indicate through them what it indicates in our world and in our conditions, until they made for every degree a world and a separate creation in its own duration, and that that world and creation are effaced and another arises after them, along with other statements that return to the belief in the influence of the stars by themselves. Exalted is Allah above having a partner or having an equal.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 2 (part 1 of 2):

When He, glorified is He, established that it is He who created the heavens and the earth, from which and in which are the idols, the stars and the celestial bodies from which come light and darkness, His existence was thereby confirmed in the state He is in, of encompassing the attributes of perfection that praise affirms, and so all their doctrines were nullified. He then marveled at them for equating others with Him. He followed this with His exclusive creation of this human species. Along with the evidences it contains for His exclusivity in praise, this is (p. 8) a refutation of those who extol ('Isa, peace be upon him), who was created from clay, by the creation of their father Adam, peace be upon him, and it confirms the invalidation of the doctrine of the Thanawiyya (Dualists). That is because they say that fire is the creator of good, and darkness is the creator of evil. Once it is established that He is the creator of the species of the sons of Adam, among whom are both good and evil, from one and the same thing, which is the clay from which the seminal fluid (al-mani') was born, from which He made the various organs differing in color, form and shape, such as the heart and the other simple organs like bones, cartilage, ligaments and tendons, it is established that the creator of their attributes of good and evil is one, All-Powerful and All-Knowing. This is because the production of differing attributes from a similar substance can only be by an originator who is one and chooses, not two. He is the One who created the earth from which their origin came, and He is Allah, who is exclusive in praise. So He said: ﴿He it is who created you﴾. Since they considered resurrection (al-ba'th) unlikely, because the dead turn to dust and the dust of all of them mixes with one another and with the dust of the earth, making distinction difficult, and since distinguishing clay is harder than distinguishing dust, owing to the intense mixing of its parts with water, He said: ﴿from clay﴾, meaning: He distinguished the clay of each of you, (p. 9) even though among you are the black and the white and other colors, and the strong and the weak, from the clay of the other, after He made it thick water with the force of its gushing, and He caused it to grow to whatever size He willed.

Since it is known that what came from one and the same thing has one and the same duration of life, He alerted, by the particle of delay (thumma), to the perfection of His power and His choice in differentiating the terms, and He said: ﴿Then He decreed a term﴾, meaning: He judged a complete judgment, decided and brought into being ﴿a term﴾, meaning: a specified time for the expiry of life and the cutting off of delay for each of you, whether good or wicked, strong or weak, from the root "ajala, ya'jalu, ujūlan", meaning to be delayed. He made those terms, although they differ, close to one another, so that none of you has a distinction by one attribute over another with a different attribute. The agent of this cannot be other than one agent acting by choice. Since He mentioned the first term, which is the originating from clay, as an indication of what was derived from it of differing terms, He mentioned the other term, which encompasses all, because mention of the beginning requires mention of the end. So He said, indicating its magnitude by the resumption and the indefinite form: ﴿And a term named﴾, meaning: a great term ﴿named﴾, meaning: for all of you together, for the ending of the intermediate state (al-barzakh), for the resurrection, which, in the course of your habits, is easier than the beginning, for the recompense and the judgment between you, which is the locus of His wisdom and the manifestation of His blessing and His punishment, at one time in which all are equal, and He concealed its knowledge from all, as He indicated by the indefinite form. This cannot be true except for one, not for many, for otherwise the measures and the wills would differ, and every thing decreed would split into a category it could not exceed, and some would tower over others and the secrets of some would be exposed by others. Glory be to Allah, exalted above what they describe. He changed the context to the nominal form, to indicate His exclusive knowledge and that it is established without doubt. This is reinforced by affirming His saying ﴿with Him﴾ in this sentence, while omitting it in the first, here and in His saying ﴿Then He raises you up therein, that a term named may be fulfilled﴾ [al-An'am: 60]. He placed the subject first despite its indefiniteness, though the original order is to place it later, to convey its magnification.

Since this explanation contains His oneness and the completeness of His power, especially over the resurrection, which is the aim of His wisdom, and that which makes doubt about the return remote, He indicated it with the particle of delay and the form of ifti'al, and He said: ﴿Yet you doubt﴾, meaning: you burden yourselves with doubt about both the oneness and the return, which in the course of your habits is easier than the beginning, by imitating your fathers, inclining to mere desire, and turning away from the proofs [which] are more evident than the brightest light. This verse is similar to the verse of al-Rum: ﴿Have they not reflected within themselves?﴾ [al-Rum: 8], meaning: how Allah created them from clay, and gave some power over others by injustice and aggression, and made for them terms, distinguishing between them, and in that equalized between the root and the branch. The conclusion of this is that Allah did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth, meaning: by means of establishing justice in all that occurs among you of disagreement, as is the matter for every owner with his slaves. ﴿And a term named﴾, the verse.

Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When He, glorified and exalted is He, explained the state of the earlier people, which is the straight path, and clarified what reveals the caution on both sides of taking and abandoning it, and explained the state of those who deviated from it among those who had been near to it, (p. 11) namely the Jews and the Christians, and that they did not commit themselves to fulfilling it and deviated from what was made clear to them, and the matter of the two groups concluded in blaming their state and explaining their breaking of it and warning the pious lest what befell them should befall them, and He concluded that with an explanation of the state of the certain ones on the Day of Resurrection, the day on which the truthful benefit from their truthfulness. Along with that, the mention of the polytheist Arabs had been dragged in, and their deafness to the caller and their blindness to the signs, so that they were more like animals than human beings. He, exalted is He, followed that with an indication of a group who inclined to contemplation and reflection, but who were not granted success in reaching the truth and fell short of being illuminated by the lights of guidance. They are not among those who return to a law that has been distorted and changed; rather they are in the form of one who intended to be guided by the guidance of the natural disposition (fitra) and to draw evidence from what Allah, exalted is He, spread out in creation, but who did not look carefully, was not granted success, and went astray. They are the Magians and the rest of the dualists, whose ultimate matter was attributing action to light and darkness. No mention of them had preceded, nor any report of their state. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. He began, exalted is He, by mentioning the creation of the heavens and the earth, from which light and darkness came into being, since darkness is the shadows of these bodies, and light comes from luminous bodies carried within them, [namely] the sun, the moon and the stars. So the meaning was: Praise be to Allah, who made the matter clear to whoever reflects and perceives insight, so that he knows that the existence of light and darkness depends, by the law of causation which He willed, on the existence of the bodies of the heavens and the earth (p. 12) and what is deposited in them. Along with the clarification of the matter in that, whoever became blind to insight swerved from it: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He it is who created you from clay﴾ adds further clarity to this meaning, for He mentioned our origin and the substance from which He brought us into being, just as He mentioned for light and darkness what is like the substance, namely the existence of the heavens and the earth. The word "ja'l" (made/placed) indicated that existence depends, according to His will, on what was mentioned. It has been said: What difference is there between the existence of light and darkness from the existence of the heavens and the earth, and between your existence from clay, that there should be doubt about attributing the bringing into being to light and darkness, when they did not come into being except after a substance or cause, as occurred in your coming into being? The matter in that is the clearest thing: ﴿Yet you doubt﴾. Then the surah, from its beginning to its end, passed by alerting to the unfolding of the proofs in existing things, along with an alert that this does not reach the harvesting of its benefit except for one who is prepared according to prior destiny (al-sabiqa). So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Only those who hear respond﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. Then He said, exalted is He: ﴿As for the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. This is, and Allah knows best, of the same pattern as ﴿Is he who was dead and We gave him life﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. It was stated briefly here and then explained later in the same surah. The meaning is that among creation is one whom Allah made a hearer, obedient, alert, and taking lesson at the first instant. He, glorified is He, showed the example of that in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in His saying: ﴿And thus We showed Ibrahim the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 75]. It is as if He is saying to His pious servants: Come, follow the path of reflection, the religion of your father Ibrahim, (p. 13) how he looked, peace be upon him, with the look of the hearer who is alert! In his first look he did not dwell on what the cause of its existence is clear, so that he would need to seek a purpose in the stars, the moon and the sun. Rather he looked at that from which the light proceeds, not at the light itself. When night covered him, he saw a star. Consider that he, peace be upon him, did not prolong looking at the light's appearance, and then returned to considering the body from which the light comes. Rather, when he saw light coming from heavenly bodies, he contemplated those bodies and the attributes subsisting in them, and he saw their setting, rising, moving and turning, and said: This does not befit Lordship, for these are attributes of created things. Then he raised his look to the moon and the sun and saw that same judgment operating in them, and he concluded that behind them is a governor who transcends movement, absence and setting. So he said: ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 79]. Peace be upon him, He specified mention of these two because they carry the bodies of light and are the cause of darkness' existence. Then consider this look of his, peace be upon him, and how he singled out for consideration the most noble and highest of the two existents. In that there are two aspects of wisdom. The first is the loftiness of the look and the penetration of insight in considering the most noble, for when the matter becomes clear from it, it is clearer regarding what is other than it. Thus he combined nearness of grasp with loftiness of ascent. The second aspect is the correspondence between the state of the one looking and what he looks at, and the grasping and following of the lofty natural disposition. This is of the kind of «our Prophet ﷺ took the milk when milk and wine were presented to him, and he chose the milk, so it was said to him: You have chosen the fitra» (p. 14). It has been said: This look and reflection is by inspiration, not the look of one who clung to the earth and so chose light and darkness. It should be relied upon in the story of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, in this reflection, that he ﷺ, in His saying ﴿This is my Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 76], intended only to cut off the argument of one who worships any of these, since it was the religion of his people. So he laid out for them the reflection and the proof, and began to present what is far too exalted to be inclined toward. He is like the debater who says to his opponent: Suppose this is as you say.

He intends by this the submission of his opponent and summoning him to reflection, so that he is not one who argues against him over what he does not believe, in order that he may build his aim upon that, so that his opponent may desist while he is certain of his matter. This is what should be relied upon here regarding the words of Yusuf, peace be upon him, ﴿It was not for us to associate anything with Allah﴾ [Yusuf: 38]. Thus protection (ʿiṣmah, divine preservation from error) surrounded them against what the falsifiers imagine and what the fabricators invent. What we have said is confirmed by the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people﴾ [al-An'am: 83]. This is the state of one whose rank is elevated among those who listen. Among creation there is one whom Allah made to hear at the very first instant, and this is a sufficient example of that. Among them is the dead, and the dead are of two kinds: among them is one who is roused from his ignorance and blindness, and among them is one who remains in his darkness, dead, without movement. Allah the Exalted's words explain this: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people like one who is in darkness and will never emerge from it?﴾ [al-An'am: 122]

Since the surah contains the aspects of reflection (iʿtibar, considering signs as lessons), stirs toward contemplation, and makes clear from the totality of its verses that the one who reflects and ponders, even if he is not awake at the first instant, nor hears the first stimulus, nor responds to the first hearer, may yet move from his stillness and heedlessness until he hears and joins those who awaken at the first instant, it was fitting that the stirring of the servants and their being commanded to reflect should be accompanied, at the beginning of the surah, by a reference to two states: the state of those who hear at the first instant, and the state of those who hear in a second state. So it is said: ﴿Only those who hear will respond, and the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. Here there is no reference to the third category, although it is known, namely the one who remains in his stillness and death, of those whom no admonisher, no preacher, and no reflection has stirred. Moreover, if this kind were mentioned here, there would be in it something that would make lazy the one whose resolve is weak, and his initial state would return. So it is said: ﴿And the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36], and it is stated in general terms so that all might act upon this raising from ignorance and from waking from the slumber of heedlessness, just as He called all with one call, so it is said: ﴿O mankind, worship your Lord﴾ [al-Baqarah: 21]. Then they differed in responding to the caller according to their precedence. The return of this to ﴿And the dead, Allah will raise them﴾ [al-An'am: 36] is for the hearing of all, and in the form of equality there is a fitness for the call, so that the proof may be established against the servants. Then, when the evidences are spread out, the breasts are expanded to receive them, the souls take hold and are attached according to what has been decreed, and those who are worthy of good attain it, Allah the Exalted said after some verses: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. It had been said to one who moved from the state of death and saw the measure of Allah's blessing upon him in giving him life: Does your present state, radiant with what you have been given when you reflected, resemble your state of lifelessness? So thank your Lord and humble yourself before Him, seeking increase, and take warning from the state of the one who clung to his state of death, so that the signs did not benefit him. He is the one indicated by His words, ﴿like one who is in darkness and will never emerge from it﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. ﴿We have placed coverings upon their hearts so that they do not understand it﴾ [al-Kahf: 57]. ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered everything before them, they would not have believed unless Allah willed﴾ [al-An'am: 111].

﴿It is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them; they will not believe﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6]. It seems that the earlier category, which hears at the first instant, would not have had its mention here, from the viewpoint of intending to show them the measure of this blessing and the rescue of the one characterized by it from the bewilderment of doubt about its occurrence, in what came before in His words, ﴿Only those who hear will respond﴾ [al-An'am: 36]. So here He mentions what actually happens in showing the measure of the blessing of rescue and deliverance from the blindness of ignorance. This is the state of the one who moved by Allah's grace, and the state of the one who remained in his death. Or the two kinds may be included in His words, ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life﴾ [al-An'am: 122]. As for the second, namely the one in whom the form of transmission (naql, i.e. being transmitted from death to life) is established, his matter is clear from the verse. As for the first kind, the one who hears at the first instant, who is sufficed in his burden, protected by the shield of preservation from the assaults of ignorance and doubts, his entering under the requirement of this wording is because his protection, or his hearing at the first instant, is not from himself, nor by what preceded, nor was it imposed upon him, but by the bestowal of mercy and the presentation of blessing. Had He left it to him, or entrusted him to himself, it would not have been so: ﴿And whatever blessing you have is from Allah﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. By this consideration, the verse has perhaps included the three categories, and this is more apt. As for the omission of the third category from His words, ﴿Only those who hear will respond﴾ [al-An'am: 36], it is for what has preceded. And Allah knows best what He intended.

When this noble surah has included, in extensive detail, the aspects of reflection and the presentation of the directions of contemplation, such that whoever ponders it knows that the proof of Allah is established over the servants, and that the sending of the Messengers is mercy, blessing, grace and kindness; and when the evidences are spread out, the created things are witnessed and eloquent, and the indication of contemplation through hearing, sight and hearts is present, how can any intelligent person hesitate about the magnitude of His mercy, the Exalted, in sending the Messengers! Thus the proof is confirmed and the demonstrations support one another. So when creation came to know, because of the establishment of the proof against them by the two ways of listening to the caller and reflecting upon the craftsmanship, Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: To Allah belongs the conclusive proof﴾ [al-An'am: 149], ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 157]. What excuse then remains for the one making excuses after this? Do you want the veil lifted and the matter seen with your own eyes? Had you insight, you would have obtained what you were given.

﴿Do they await only that the angels come to them, or your Lord comes, or some of the signs of your Lord come?﴾ [al-An'am: 158]. Then the surah was concluded with submission and entrusting, with what is beneficial, along with His words, ﴿Had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾ [al-An'am: 149]. And from the four surahs there results an explanation of the people of the Straight Path, their levels in following it, what is incumbent upon them to adhere to or to abandon, and an explanation of the state of those who deviate from its course among the Jews, Christians, idol-worshippers and Magians. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 3:

Since knowledge of all the states of the created being indicates that knowledge of them belongs to its Creator, and that whoever claims that its Creator is incapable of controlling His dominion, or of uncovering its defects for others, or of knowing what He Himself does not know of it, then He is not a god; and since the God is the One who alone encompasses all knowledge, for whom it is not difficult to distinguish dust from dust; and since he (ﷺ) would inform them about God from the unseen secrets and hidden news of their inner lives, of things that they related with wonder and from which they knew the all-encompassing nature of His knowledge, to the point that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb said on the day of the Conquest: "If this pebble could speak, it would tell of me," the Exalted said, linking with ﴿He is the One who﴾ [al-An'am: 2], indicating Divine Oneness through the comprehensiveness of knowledge, after the proof of complete power and free choice has been established; because their denial of the Return was for two reasons: one of them is their assumption that the cause acting upon bodies is the mixture of natural elements, and their denial that the cause is a capable, choosing agent; and the second is that He, even on the assumption of choice, does not know particulars, so He cannot distinguish the body of Zayd from the parts of the body of 'Amr. So when the proof has been established of (p-19) the perfection of His power, His choice, and the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all that is known, universals and particulars, all doubts vanish: ﴿And He is Allah﴾, that is, the One who has this name that gathers all the most beautiful names and the highest attributes, the one called upon with it in devout worship, submission and servitude; and He connected with this meaning His saying: ﴿in the heavens﴾ [because whoever is in a thing acts within it].

Since the address is to the deniers of resurrection, He emphasized, saying: ﴿and on the earth﴾, that is, this is His attribute always [upon this meaning, that He, glorified is He, is established with this name which He alone possesses in the sense of worship and servitude in both directions, above and below. No one of sound intellect understands from it what the apparent sense requires, that He is contained, for everything contained is bounded and in need of its container and confiner, weak in acting upon what is beyond it; and whoever has a need of any kind unfit for divinity and sovereign will... as in the hadith of the slave-girl: "Where is Allah?" She said: "In the heaven." And it is refuted by the hadith: "You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You," for its apparent sense contradicts the apparent sense of the first; and the apparent sense of this is supported by decisive transmission that He is not in need, and it is supported by sound transmission: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11], that is, neither in His essence, nor His attributes, nor any of His affairs; and "Allah was, and there was nothing with Him"; and the hadith "There is nothing above you" - narrated by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah in the Supplications, and Abu Dawud in the Adab, from Abu Hurayrah - may Allah be pleased with him. And Allah is the Granter of success.]

Since the aim is to establish that His knowledge, exalted is He, encompasses equally both the hidden and the manifest, and since the context here concerns the hidden, for it is in explaining the creation of man and the wondrous making of him, with what He created in him of the perception of meanings and prepared for him before he could express them, then enabled him to do so, He placed the hidden first, saying, explaining that nothing is absent from Him: ﴿He knows your secret﴾.

Since there is no necessary connection between knowing the secret and knowing the open, for in the open there may be a word so loud that it prevents the mixing of voices from the one who knows it, he stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿and your public speech﴾; and the relation of each of them to Him is on an equal footing, and neither is described as nearer or farther from Him. And since secret and open speech are common in sayings, and sayings relate to hearing, he mentioned what includes both, which is common in deeds relating to sight, saying: ﴿and He knows what you earn﴾, and thereby conveyed the attributes of hearing and sight along with the establishment of knowledge.

Then, when the proofs became manifest and the arguments were mutually reinforcing, while they turned away from them, he connected to that, in a circumstantial clause (jumlah hāliyyah), His saying, turning away from them to signal that they deserve intense anger: ﴿And there does not come to them﴾, that is, these people who are deserving of being turned away from, ﴿any sign﴾ — and he went to the utmost in negation with His saying ﴿any sign﴾, that is, any indication of the truth of what their Messenger ﷺ called them to. He made it partial with His saying ﴿of the signs of their Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to them by establishing proofs, bestowing intellects, and sending the Messenger, ﴿except that they were turning away from it﴾, that is, this is their characteristic always, intentionally out of obstinacy, so that the argument would not be binding upon them. It is also permissible that this (p-21) be conjoined (ma'tūf) to (yaʿdilūn).

Since their turning away from considering (the signs) was a cause of their denial, and denial leads to their punishment, He said: ﴿So they have denied﴾, that is, they have brought about the denial of the Truthful One, ﴿the truth﴾, that is, because of the matter that is established and perfect in all its firmness. This is because all the signs are equal in indicating what any one of them indicates. ﴿When it came to them﴾, that is, they did not hesitate at all upon its arrival, neither to consider it nor to do anything else, and this is the strongest indication of obstinacy.

Since turning away from a thing in this manner is the act of the denier who mocks, one who has carried his denial to its utmost extreme, which is mockery, He said: ﴿There will come to them the news﴾, that is, with a true promise that admits no failure, when the punishment descends upon them, even if its coming is delayed. ﴿of what they used to﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿mock﴾, that is, they renew their mockery of it with the utmost eagerness to seek it, though it is the furthest thing from mockery. The word "naba'" means a great report, the kind that carries recompense with it. And the fronting of the adverbial phrase conveys that they did not mock anything other than the perfect Truth, as you see many of the affluent who are not amazed by what is truly amazing yet are amazed by what is not amazing. Or it may be that he regarded their mockery of anything else, in comparison with their mockery of it, as nothing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 6:

When He had informed of their denial in this manner and threatened them with the certainty of their punishment, He followed it with what serves as admonition and advice. He marvelled at their persistence, despite their knowledge (p-22) of the destruction of those who were stronger than them in power, greater in number, and who had gathered abundant blessings, yet did not take heed from it. Added to this was their certain knowledge of the reports and their witnessing of the traces of those peoples and their wondrous craftsmanship in their buildings and dwellings. Thereby He provided evidence for the establishment of what preceded it, namely the threat concerning mockery. So He said, affirming, rebuking, censuring and expressing wonder: ﴿Have they not seen﴾. He indicated the abundance of those spoken of, to magnify the report, by His saying: ﴿how many We destroyed﴾.

Since the intended ones were specific people who did not encompass the whole of the past, namely those possessing greater capacity, such as the people of Noah, Hud and Salih, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿before them﴾. He specified "kam" (كَمّ, "how many") by His saying: ﴿generations﴾, i.e., groups united in a single time, and they are the people of every hundred years, as the al-Qamus (al-Qamus, the lexicon) has confirmed, "due to the saying of the Prophet ﷺ to a boy: (Live a qarn), so he lived a hundred years." This is the end of the qarn. The closer view is that it is not fixed; rather, when most of the people of an age have passed away, it is said: the qarn has ended. He indicated what they witnessed of their traces by His saying: ﴿We had established them﴾, i.e., We made them firm by strengthening the means: expansion in bodies, strength in physiques, and abundance in wealth, ﴿on the earth﴾, i.e., with strength, health and leisure, that which We had not established for you. We had established for them through fertility, expansiveness and abundance ﴿what We had not established﴾, i.e., an establishment that We did not make ﴿for you﴾, i.e., We do not single you out with it. Thus the verse belongs to ihtibak (احتباك, a rhetorical device in which two corresponding elements are each omitted from one part and retained in the other) or something similar. And the iltifat (التفات, shift of grammatical person) from the third person to the second person is so that the situation is not confused, for the pronoun of the absent can apply to both the inferior and the superior. The past tense in His saying ﴿And We sent the sky﴾ does not leave confusion; i.e., the rain, by naming the thing after its cause, or: the clouds, ﴿upon them﴾. Since the intended meaning is rain, the implied sense is: while it was ﴿in abundant showers﴾, i.e., with a copious, continuous flow, because it is an intensive form (sifah mubalaghah) from the root "darr" (درّ, to flow abundantly). They said: it is used the same for masculine and feminine.

When He mentioned their benefit from the water of the sky, which was not constant, He followed it with the water of the earth, because of its permanence and its constant presence in gardens and meadows. So He said: ﴿And We made the rivers flow﴾. Since the generality of water in the earth and its depth prevent complete benefit from it, He indicated its nearness and that the earth is not entirely encompassed by it, by means of the preposition, saying: ﴿beneath them﴾, i.e., on the surface of the earth, and We placed it in its depths, so that when it is dug, water springs forth from it [min] in such quantity that it flows as a river.

Since it is known that every living thing is made of water, and it is among the most evident of things that He planted their vegetation, and their plains and mountains turned green, so their crops and fruits multiplied, their conditions expanded, their wealth increased, and their hopes were facilitated, Allah, glorified is He, made known that all of this was nothing but a respite for their humiliation, by His saying, as a consequence of that: ﴿So We destroyed them﴾, i.e., by Our greatness, ﴿for their sins﴾, i.e., which resulted from their insolence regarding the blessing (p-24), and We did not care for them, and their blessings did not avail them.

Since a person may sometimes spare his servant or companion out of fear of needing someone like him, He made clear that He, glorified is He, has no need of anything. So He said: ﴿And We brought into being﴾. Since He, glorified is He, did not grant immortality to anyone, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after them﴾, i.e., in what they had been in, ﴿another generation﴾. This indicates that He left none of those destroyed, and that this second generation does not trace back to them by lineage, by His saying: ﴿others﴾. And He did not diminish Our dominion in anything. So beware lest We do to you as We did to them. This verse is like the verse of al-Rum: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth?﴾ [al-Rum: 9] to the end of the verse. Thus the establishment of them is what is meant by the "strength" there, the establishing for them is what is meant by "cultivation," and the destruction by sins is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And Allah was not to wrong them﴾ [al-Rum: 9] to the end of the two verses.

When the summary of what came before was: "Then they ascribe equals to their Lord" and "they deny you concerning the truth you have brought, despite the proofs you have made clear and the evidences you have set up," and since he (ﷺ) was extremely eager for their faith, the situation called for the tongue of the state (lisan al-hal, the implicit meaning conveyed by the circumstances) to say: "O Lord, send down to them something by which they may move from reflective consideration to direct sight, as they have proposed to me." So He informed him that they would not believe in that. This is connected by conjunction (atf) to "and no sign comes to them" (Qur'an 6:4), as confirmation for him and a depiction of the course of events: "Even if We had sent down to you ﴿a book﴾," that is, through what We have of greatness, "﴿a book﴾," that is, written, "from the sky" (p-٢٥) "﴿on parchment﴾," that is, on paper, in response to what the Jews had suggested to them as a proposal. Then He affirmed that the matter was evident, not imaginary, and without any kind of confusion, by His saying: "﴿and they touched it﴾," that is, beyond seeing. He added to the confirmation, the depiction, and the removal of metaphorical usage by His saying: "﴿with their hands, the disbelievers would say﴾." He stated it explicitly and did not use a pronoun, to attach the ruling to the description and to alert that among those present there would be some who stay silent and believe, even after that. So He said: "﴿those who disbelieved﴾," that is, ruling that their disbelief is permanent, concealing the signs out of obstinacy and arrogance. Perhaps He omitted "of them" to indicate the generality of his call, that is, from among the Arabs and from others among the nation of your call, especially the Jews, whose stubbornness and lying are indicated by His saying: "﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the sky﴾" (Qur'an 4:153). "﴿If﴾," that is, "﴿this is nothing but magic﴾," that is, deception and imagination with no reality, and they increased in audacity and said: "﴿clear﴾," that is, evident and manifest. The author of Kitab al-Zina (Kitab al-Zina, a work on the meanings of words) said: the meaning of sihr (magic) in the speech of the Arabs is to create a pretext for a thing, to defend by it, and to deceive with something that has no substance. It is said: "sahara him," when one gives him a false pretext, deceives him, and confuses him so that he does not know from where to approach and is turned away from his direction. Thus the magicians give people false pretexts, make falsehood resemble truth, and turn it away from its proper course.

(p. 26) When he had explained what follows from the response, he turned to the point he had hinted at: the Jews proposed that a revelation be sent down. He informed them that they also proposed the appearance of an angel [to them], and he explained its implications. They said: "If God sent a messenger, he would have to be an angel, so that he would have more knowledge, greater power, and a more distinct separation from humans. Then doubt about his mission would be less. A wise one who wants to achieve an important aim should prefer to achieve it by the means that delivers it most quickly." So He said: ﴿And they say, "Why not (lawla)?"﴾, meaning: why not, and why is it not the case, ﴿that an angel is sent down to him?﴾, meaning from the sky, visibly to us, speaking to us and we speaking to him, and not veiled from us.

When he had mentioned their saying, pointing to their doubt, he refuted it by His saying: ﴿And if⦆ (meaning: while the situation is that if) ﴿We had sent down⦆ and he dropped the particle of elevation ('alā, "upon") because there was no need, in returning their words, to mention it. And so that it should not contain a consolation for them regarding what they hinted at, namely their denial that an angel would descend upon him with revelation, ﴿an angel﴾, meaning as they proposed. Then it is either that he is in his own form or not. If he were in the form in which he was created, they would not be able to bear seeing him, and if that were so, ﴿the matter would have been decided⦆, meaning by their destruction. He built the verb in the passive (lukhiya, "it was decided") as an indication, in the manner of the speech of those who have power, of the extreme speed, because of the ease of the matter and the lightness of its burden. For none of them looks upon him without being struck senseless. And even if We gave them a strength by which they could endure looking at him, it would certainly be a decision of the matter and a resolution of the dispute from another aspect, namely that this would be an uncovering of the veil and the loss of faith in the unseen. Our custom has been to destroy at that point. So they are destroyed under each of these two suppositions. This is the meaning of His saying, magnifying its rank with the particle of delay (thumma, "then"): ﴿then they would not be reprieved⦆, meaning: in neither of these two states. As for if We make him in a form they can look upon, We will make him in the form of a man, for that is the most perfect of forms. Then the confusion will befall them that befell them through your supplication (to God), and this is the meaning of

And if We had made him (i.e., what they sought) a **malak** (angel), it would be possible, in the ordinary course of things in this world, for them to see him and to remain alive after seeing him, [but] **We would certainly have made him a man** (rajul), i.e., in the form of a man. But He expressed it this way to indicate complete concealment, so that no one who sees him doubts that he is a man. Likewise Jibril (peace be upon him) would descend at times upon the Prophet (ﷺ) in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi. When some of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) saw him, they did not doubt that he was Dihya (may Allah be pleased with him). **"And We would surely have confused them"** (wa-lalabasna 'alayhim ma yalbisun), i.e., by making him a man We would have mixed up for them, and for others, what they themselves mix up in their saying that a message cannot be valid from a human being. For if this one who claims to be a messenger were a messenger, he would have to be an angel. So the confusion falls upon them: since this one who says he is a messenger is a man, they conclude he is not a messenger. It is also possible to establish this in another way, namely that **﴿And if We had sent down﴾** [al-An'am: 7] falls within the scope of **﴿they turned away from it﴾** [al-An'am: 4], i.e., they would have turned away from Us if We had sent it down to you on something other than parchment (qirṭās). And if We had sent down to you from heaven a Book on parchment, and made it available to them to be perceived by sight and touch, they would still have turned away. **And those whose disbelief We have prolonged, out of obstinacy and arrogance, said: "This is nothing but clear magic."** The phrase "and they said" (wa-qālū) may be coordinated with **﴿those who disbelieved would say﴾** [al-An'am: 7], and this saying would come before their making such a demand, as Allah related of them in Surat al-Isra' with His words: **﴿And they said: "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth"﴾** [al-Isra': 90], to the end of that passage. In that case it would be a report of the unseen (ikhbār bi-maghīb).

(p. 28)

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 10:**

When he had cut off hope of guiding those whom He had decreed to wretchedness, and their demand for the sending down of an angel and the like was only in the manner of obstinacy (*ta'annut*) and mockery, and this grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, may Allah be pleased with them, to the utmost degree of hardship, the soul turned toward relief from them and anticipated it, because of the manifestations of greatness that had preceded. So He informed him that He would do that, in a context that undertakes to console him, and that this had always been His *sunnah* (established way) regarding those who did their deed. So He said, conjoining it to His saying ﴿So there will come to them the news﴾ [al-An'am: 5]: ﴿And indeed﴾, i.e., this from them is only mockery of you, ﴿indeed messengers were mocked﴾, i.e., mockery was brought about and occurred from the nations. It was made passive because what is significant is the mockery itself, not that it came from a specific person, and to indicate that this used to happen to them from the high and the low alike, ﴿before you﴾.

Since nearness in time is consoling in a matter such as this, and since each of the mockery and the sending did not encompass the whole time, He brought in the preposition and said: ﴿before you﴾, so We destroyed those who mocked them. This is the meaning of ﴿then there enveloped﴾, i.e., there surrounded (*fa-ahaqa*) ﴿those who mocked them﴾, i.e., of those messengers, ﴿what they used to mock﴾, i.e., of the punishment which they were threatening with, and which was the cause of their mockery.

When Allah, exalted is He, knew that they would answer this with, "This is nothing but the myths of the ancients" [as bracketed in the original], He commanded him ﷺ, after the astonishment expressed at their failure to consider with their hearts or their eyes the places of destruction of those who passed away, in His saying: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them?⟩ [al-An'am: 6], to command them to look upon the places of destruction of those whose knowledge had settled in their hearts that they were destroyed for the same kind of denial, such as the people of Salih, Lot, Shu'ayb and others. This would suffice them from witnessing what they demanded. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: Travel⟩, that is, make travel a means of drawing lessons (i'tibar, reflective lesson-drawing), and do not be deceived by your being given respite and your being established ﴿in the earth⟩, and so on, to the end of the verse. This is like the evidence for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieved said, "This is nothing but clear magic"⟩ [al-An'am: 7].

Since the context is a threat through warning against the like of what befell the earlier nations, and since it has already been established that they will not be brought forward from their appointed terms, He gave them respite in looking, for it is stronger as a threat, more indicative of power, and more conducive to fairness, especially as this surah is among the earliest of the Qur'an in revelation and at the beginning of it in arrangement. So He said: ﴿Then look⟩, and He pointed out that this is a matter worthy of being asked about with His saying: ﴿how was the end of⟩, that is, the final outcome of the affair of (p-30) ﴿the deniers⟩. That is: examine thoroughly, reflect deeply, and prolong your contemplation when you see the traces of those punished on account of their denial of the messengers. For when you witness those traces, your lesson-drawing is completed and your insight grows strong. This is an indication that the matter is at its utmost clarity, so the longer one reflects upon it, the more it is manifested.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 12:

When He, glorified be He, commanded them to travel, He asked them: do they see, in their journeying, their roaming, their wandering and their going about, anything belonging to other than Allah? This was a reminder to them of what He had shown them mercy in through this, by bringing them into being first and facilitating its benefits and repelling its harms second, as an appeal to them to turn towards Him and to turn away from submitting to what is like them or less than them, while it is His dominion and in His grip, and as a condemnation of their eating His provision and worshipping other than Him. So He said, establishing for them the existence of the Creator, prophethood and the return, and rebuking them for their foolishness, their extreme ignorance and their blindness: ﴿Say: To whom belongs﴾ — and the placing of the object first draws attention to the importance of the one worshipped — ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth?﴾

Since they were in a state of obstinacy, in that they did not hasten to submission after the proofs had been established and every impediment removed, He alluded to that by His saying, turning away from waiting for their answer, reproaching them for the lack of fairness which they claim: ﴿Say: Allah﴾, that is, the One who has complete encompassment in power and knowledge and has no equal, not anyone else. Even though they are obstinate, they cannot refute your saying, especially since a person's answer to a question he is asked is only fitting to be given by himself when the matter has reached such clarity that no denier can deny it, and here it is so, because the signs of origination and contingency are manifest upon the pages of the existents. So affirmation of Him was necessary, with no disagreement concerning it.

Since most of what is in this existence consists of benefits, together with being good, delicious, pleasant and appetising, and whatever harms are in it are veiled and kept away from them, so that their reaching them is rare except through their own causing of them, and all of this, moreover, constitutes manifest evidences of His oneness and the completeness of His knowledge and power, and this was worthy of being wondered at because of the generality of this kindness, together with what they are upon of sin and transgression, and the delay of punishment from them despite obstinacy and rebellion, He said, indicating that His mercy preceded His wrath, beginning anew: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ — that is, He promised a promise that is like what is written and sealed, and emphasised with the utmost emphasis; or "prescribed" where He willed, glorified be He.

Since the self is used to express the essence as it is, He said: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, that is, for this reason He has honoured you with this honour through the aspects of bounty, and delayed from you retribution by annihilation. Had He willed, He would have set harms over you and made your living of non-delicious things like dust and some of the filth by which some animals live.

Since that is a source of greed for the oppressor and insolent, and a bewildering and regrettable marvel for the oppressed and broken, He said, warning, welcoming, giving good news, and turning to the mode of direct address because it is more eloquent and more explicit about the intended meaning, indicating the resurrection by what has passed of establishing that the existents belong to Allah; because everything in them is described by attributes which admit of being characterised by their opposites, so the specification of each body with its particular attribute occurs only through the specification of a choosing agent, and thus He is capable of restoration, since the first composition occurred only because its Maker is capable of all possibilities, by being knowing of all knowables, and the characterisation with that is not separable from Him. So He is a King, obeyed, commanding and forbidding, sending one who conveys His commands and prohibitions, to manifest the fruit of kingship in reward and punishment on the Day of Gathering: ﴿He will surely gather you﴾ — that is, by Allah, gathering you gradually, one after another ﴿to the Day of Resurrection﴾, for the justice among all the servants, being ﴿in which there is no doubt﴾, that is, in any respect whatsoever. And that gathering is for the specification of mercy on that day to His friends, and of wrath and vengeance to His enemies, after mercy had encompassed both groups in the day of this world; and He made mercy more manifest with regard to the enemies. [And through this gathering mercy is complete for many of the creation, and were it not for it, control would be lost and confusion would multiply, as was the case in the Jahiliyyah.]

Since that is so, in the absence of doubt, because Allah informed of it through the tongues of His messengers, and because of the proofs for it, since in this creation there are wondrous wisdoms, together with most of the actions of living beings departing from justice, it became known to every person of understanding that the resurrection is the seat of wisdom, for manifesting the adornment with the lofty attributes towards all creation: the wretched and the happy, the near and the far. It was as if it were said: what is the matter with us that we see most people disbelieving in it? So He said, as an answer: ﴿Those who have lost their souls﴾, that is, by destroying them through their denial of it, opposing the primordial nature which guides even the mute, and concealing the sound intellect. ﴿So they﴾, that is, because of their loss of their own souls through neglecting the intellect, employing the senses and being bound by imitation, ﴿do not believe﴾. Thus they became like one who throws himself from a height to die for some corrupt purpose, not because of any obscurity in the matter of the Resurrection nor any confusion regarding the event of our Lord. And the meaning becomes: those who do not believe on this Day are the ones decreed to lose on that Day.

When the proofs shone forth like the sun, and the demonstrations were set up so that no kind of confusion remained at all, he spoke generally about what had preceded, including what they witness and what lies beyond it. He mentioned time after place, and placed it first because it is more manifest. A complete teacher is one who begins with the more manifest and then the more manifest, ascending to the less manifest and then the less manifest. Thus the report about time, the things in time, place, and the things in place was completed. ﴿To Him﴾, meaning Him alone, ﴿belongs whatever dwells﴾, meaning whatever settles, is contained, and comes to be, ﴿in the night and the day﴾, meaning whatever is of such a nature as to dwell in them, even if it is in motion. He expressed it this way, rather than with "moves," because they are the abode of death. Included in this are the light and the darkness, which those who associated partners with God have associated with Him.

When what preceded indicated complete power, and it was divided into the moving and the still (p-34), and power is not complete except with knowledge, he indicated knowledge by His saying: ﴿And He﴾, meaning not other than Him, ﴿is the All-Hearing﴾, meaning the one who reaches the hearing of every moving thing, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, meaning the one whose knowledge is all-encompassing, through sight, hearing, and other means, of every moving thing and every still thing, of your words and your deeds and other things. So do not hope that any part of your recompense will be left aside. Here "the All-Knowing" is more emphatic than "the All-Seeing." This is like what preceded in His saying: ﴿Say: Do you worship, besides God, what has no power to harm or benefit you? And God is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 76]. It is also a rendering of His saying: ﴿He knows your secret and your open, and He knows what you earn﴾ [al-An'am: 3].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 14:

When he had set forth the proofs such that no doubt remained for anyone of insight, the tongue of the situation required that he denounce them for turning away from His presence and neglecting His door. So God, exalted is He, expressed this in the form of a command to him, ﷺ, to denounce it against himself, so that it would be more effective for them and gentler toward them. Also, what preceded indicates the utmost opposition and warns of the evil consequence of hostility. It is as though they said: "Is there any way to agreement?" So it was said: "No, except by your taking My God as a protector (walīy). That, by my life, is your happiness in both abodes, whereas your aspiring to take your equals as protectors is something that will never happen." This is the meaning of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say﴾, that is, explicitly, to them, denying that he would incline toward their equals in any way.

Since the denial was directed at the other being taken (as a protector) and not at taking a protector, [p. 35] he gave priority to the particle ﴿ghayr﴾ [meaning "other than"] over the interrogative hamza [i.e., the particle of interrogation], and said: ﴿Shall I take other than God﴾, that is, the One to whom nothing is comparable in greatness, ﴿as a protector?﴾ [that is], shall I burden myself to act contrary to what the primordial nature (fiṭra) and the reason free of desire call for, as you have done? And ﴿walīy﴾ [protector] means: one whom I worship, because he is in charge of all my affairs. Then He described Him with what establishes His guardianship and turns one away from the guardianship of others, saying: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, their Creator, who originated them without a prior pattern. ﴿And He feeds﴾, that is, while He is the One who provides sustenance to everything other than Himself that has a soul, ﴿but is not fed﴾, that is, no one can, in any way whatsoever, feed Him. The meaning is that benefits come from Him, and benefiting from Him is impossible. Hence, in reason, it is impossible to take anyone other than Him as a protector, because everything else is in need of Him in its essence and in all its attributes, whereas He, glory be to Him, is absolutely self-sufficient.

This is a shift (iltifāt) to His statement, exalted is He: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was only a messenger; messengers had passed away before him, and his mother was a truthful woman; they both used to eat food﴾ [al-Mā'ida: 75]. It is also an allusion (ta'rīḍ) to everything that is worshipped besides God, especially idols, for they used to present food to them, which the animals and birds would then eat. It is therefore known that they neither feed nor are fed.

Al-Dārimī related in the beginning of his Musnad, with a sound chain, from al-A'mash, from Mujāhid, who said: (My master told me that his family sent with him a bowl containing butter and milk to their gods. He said: "I refrained from eating the butter out of fear of them. Then a dog came, ate the butter, drank the milk, and then urinated on the idol.") His master had been a partner of the Prophet ﷺ before Islam. There is a difference of opinion about him: it is said he was Qays ibn al-Sā'ib ibn 'Uwaymir ibn 'Ā'idh ibn 'Imrān ibn Makhzūm. It is said he was his relative al-Sā'ib ibn Abī al-Sā'ib Ṣayfī ibn 'Ā'idh ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Umar ibn Makhrūm. It is also said he was his son 'Abd Allāh ibn al-Sā'ib. God knows best.

He also related from Abū Rajā' (who is al-'Uṭāridī, and he is a mukhaḍram, that is, one who lived through both the Jāhiliyya and Islam), who said: (In the Jāhiliyya, when we found a fine stone, we worshipped it. If we did not find a stone, we gathered a heap of sand, then we brought a milch camel, milked her over the heap until it was saturated, and then we kept worshipping that heap for as long as we remained in that place.)

In this [verse] there is also an indication that just as He created all of you from clay, despite your differences in measures, colors, and characters, and He is free of need of you, so He created the foods, with their differences in forms, tastes, benefits, and colors, from clay, and made them benefits for you, while He is free of need of them. The explicit statement of this will come in His statement: ﴿And He it is who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth thereby the vegetation of every thing﴾ [al-An'ām: 99], which is fully treated in its place, and ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned﴾ [al-An'ām: 118].

The whole verse contains a reference (iltifāt) to His statement at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'ām: 1], and to His statement in the preceding surah: ﴿And had they believed in God and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as protectors﴾ [al-Mā'ida: 81], and similar verses in which there is the turning of the disbelievers to other than their Creator, glory be to Him and exalted is He.

This, even if no command had come from the Creator, sound reasoning would be sufficient to keep one free of it, just as I used to be before prophethood, not turning to your idols nor regarding any of your stone idols as worthy of worship. How much more so now that I have been commanded to this! This is the meaning of His statement: ﴿Say: "I have been commanded"﴾, that is, by the One who holds the command, and there is no command except His, and He is the One about whom it was previously stated that to Him belongs everything, namely God alone, ﴿to be the first to submit﴾, that is, in heart and body, in rank absolutely, and in time in relation to the community.

Since the command to submit (to God) implies a prohibition of associating partners, he did not suffice with it, but stated it explicitly, combining command and prohibition, from this Lord, the Generous, whose beneficence and generosity call to His guardianship, and whose complete sovereignty and might forbid any part of enmity toward Him. In His statement, coordinated with ﴿Say﴾ for emphasis: ﴿And never be among the polytheists﴾, that is, in no way and at no time whatsoever, by following them in any of their aims, and this emphasis is to cut off their hopes regarding him, ﷺ, in their request that he drive away some of his followers so that they would befriend him, and similar things by which they hoped to draw near him, informing [him] that doing any of what they desire is a reason for being attributed to them and being counted among them. ("Whoever imitates a people is one of them.")

Since the act of doing what is forbidden is not always punished for itself, He said, instructing that opposition in this matter is among the gravest forms of opposition, so its perpetrator deserves the greatest retribution, and all of this is to wean them away from hoping for it. He emphasized it for this purpose and for their denial of its content: ﴿Say: "Indeed I"﴾. Since the context called for fear, He placed it first and said: ﴿I fear, if I disobey﴾ — whatever thing of what you want from me, that I should comply with you in it, against what I have been commanded or forbidden from — ﴿my Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to me, ﴿the punishment of a tremendous day﴾. And since the greatness of the container corresponds to the greatness of what it contains, He said: ﴿tremendous﴾.

Since he had earlier mentioned the all-encompassing scope of His mercy, which gave the wicked person hope, and then made him despair of it through what was alluded to regarding the loss, he here stated explicitly what that earlier mention implied. He said, describing that punishment and making clear that mercy on that Day is of a different kind from what is known now, for it is special and not general, and it is lasting in its abundance upon the one who attains it, not something that passes away; likewise the blessing. Such is the nature of that Day: ﴿Whoever is turned away from it﴾, that is, from that punishment. Since the intended meaning is the continuation of the turning away throughout the whole Day, He said: ﴿on that Day﴾, that is, the Day on which the punishment of that Day occurs for him, ﴿then He has had mercy on him﴾, that is, He has dealt with him by bestowing favor upon him in the manner of one who is shown mercy. ﴿And that﴾, that is, nothing else but that, ﴿is the clear triumph﴾, that is, the attainment of what is sought, ﴿the manifest﴾, that is, exceedingly evident. And whoever is not turned away from it, He has humiliated him, and that is the great punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 17:

Since the implied sense was: "If that punishment is turned away from you, then your eye has been comforted," he (al-Biqa'i) followed it with another proof, because it is not permissible by reason to take anyone other than Him as a protector (waliyy). So He said, generalizing the ruling to that punishment and to other than it, making clear that there is no deliverer for one upon whom it befalls: ﴿And if Allah touches you﴾, that is, the Supreme King, for whom there is no equal (kufu'). Since the context is one of intimidation (tarhib), He placed first His saying: ﴿with harm﴾, that is, here or there, ﴿then there is none to remove it﴾ at all, in any way whatsoever, ﴿except Him﴾. That is, because He has no equal; He is able to inflict it, and no one other than Him is able to repel it, for ﴿He is over all things Powerful﴾. ﴿And if He touches you with good﴾, that is, at whatever time He wills.

Since analogy with the first (clause) would require that the consequence be: "then there is none to prevent it," its attribute came from the phrase ﴿so He is over all things﴾, that is, of that and of other than that, ﴿Powerful﴾, and none other than Him can prevent His doing it, alerting to the fact that His mercy, glory be to Him, precedes His wrath.

Since the two sentences were in the arrangement of ihtibak (the rhetorical device of mutual implication, where each part implies what is omitted from the other), they conveyed, by what was stated and by what was indicated by the omitted element, that He, exalted is He, is dominant over His command. Stating this explicitly, He said: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants﴾, that is, the One who carries out all His will and prevents others from achieving their will whenever He wills. He depicted His subjugation and confirmed it, to establish the dominance, by His saying: ﴿over His servants﴾, and everything other than Him is a servant. And since subjugation can include what is blameworthy, He negated that by His saying: ﴿And He is﴾, that is, He alone, ﴿the All-Wise﴾, so that the effect of subjugation is never made to reach the infliction of what is disliked except upon one who deserves it. He completed the meaning by His saying: ﴿the All-Aware﴾, that is, of what each thing deserves. Thus the proofs of the greatness of His sovereignty were complete, and that there is no doer other than Him.

When he had concluded with the two attributes of wisdom and awareness, it was as if it were said: "Why does He not know that we deny you, and so send with you, in His wisdom, someone who bears witness for you to what you say, that He commanded you to be the first to submit and forbade you from associating partners with Him, so that we would believe you? [Such a witness would be] an angel, as our question to you about it has already passed, or a book written on parchment, or something else?" Then He said: "He has done so, and He was not content for me except with His holy testimony." Or it is said: when He had established the proofs of God's oneness and power, and reached the attribute of dominance that announces retribution, nothing remained but to call them to witness, as a notice of the terrible punishment they deserve, and as a warning, lest they say when it befalls them: "No warner came to us." So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O Messenger, to them: ﴿"What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾, that is, greatest and most majestic? If they are fair and say, "Allah," then say: "He is the One who bears witness for me," just as He said in al-Nisa': ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:166]. But He cut off the speech here as an indication of their obstinacy or their silence, or as placing them in the position of the obstinate, or of one who knows a thing yet acts as one ignorant. So He said, commanding him (ﷺ): ﴿Say, "Allah"﴾, that is, the Supreme King, encompassing in knowledge and power, is the greatest in testimony.

(p-41) When they were on the verge of granting this and saying, "It is indeed so, but bring us His testimony!" He said: ﴿He is witness﴾, that is, He is the most eloquent of witnesses who bears witness ﴿between me and you﴾, that is, by this Qur'an, whose being the speech of Allah is established by your inability to produce its like, and by the other signs that you were unable to oppose. When He had established that He is the greatest witness, and had indicated His testimony through all the signs, He drew attention to the greatest of them, because God's making the Qur'an manifest upon the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ) in accordance with his claim is itself a testimony from Allah to his truthfulness. So He said, mentioning its benefit in the context of a warning that encompasses both the establishment of prophethood and the establishment of God's oneness, and placing the first before the second because the first establishes the second and conveys its purpose, linking it to the clause "witness" and using the passive form, drawing attention to the fact that the agent is known through the inimitability (i'jaz). He used the active form in the surah's black ink: ﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me﴾, and He specified the revealed matter and identified it by saying: ﴿this Qur'an﴾. Since it was in the context of a threat, He said, limiting Himself to what suits it: ﴿that I may warn you﴾, that is, I frighten you and caution you against believing any deficiency in the Deity, especially associating partners with Him, ﴿and whoever it reaches﴾, that is, I warn by it every one whom it ﴿reaches﴾, that is, reaches him. Al-Farra' said: the Arabs omit the pronoun in the relative clauses of "alladhi" (who), "man" (whoever), and "ma" (what). Al-Bukhari said at the end of the Sahih, regarding ﴿that I may warn you by it﴾ (p-42): "It means the people of Makkah, and whoever this Qur'an reaches, it is a warner to him." He transmitted it in the form of a categorical statement from Ibn 'Abbas, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it to him with a chain, as our shaykh has noted in his commentary. 'Abd al-Razzaq said in his tafsir: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Convey from Allah; whoever has had a verse of the Book of Allah reach him, then the command of Allah has reached him." Imam Taqi al-Din 'Ali ibn 'Abd al-Kafi al-Subki said in answer to a question received in the year 738 AH about whether the Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to the jinn, and from his own handwriting I quote: "The Book and the Sunnah speak to this, and the consensus (ijma') stands upon it; there is no disagreement among the Muslims about it." Then he attributed the consensus to Abu Talib al-Qada'i, Abu 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Barr in al-Tamhid, Abu Muhammad ibn Hazm in his book al-Fisal, ... and others. Then he said: As for the Book, there are verses, the first of which is ﴿that I may warn you by it and whoever it reaches﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: "Whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is as if he had seen the Prophet (ﷺ)." Ibn 'Abbas said—and he mentioned it—and al-Suddi (p-43) said: "Whoever the Qur'an reaches, it is a warner to him." Ibn Zayd said: "Whoever this Qur'an reaches, I am his warner." All these sayings are agreed in meaning.
