It seems that their speech is sent down according to states in which matters are uncovered for them, one after another, each matter more terrifying than the one before it. The Day of Resurrection, as Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said, has many aspects: at times Allah will not speak to them; at times He will speak to them and they will lie; at times He will ask them about something and they will deny it, and then their limbs will bear witness; and at times they will speak the truth, as in this station, and swear to the truth.

When they acknowledged this under compulsion, after the veil was removed and the opportunity of belief in the unseen had passed, through what they had been denying, their humiliation followed as a consequence. Therefore He said, resuming the speech: ﴿He will say﴾, that is, Allah, causing it as a consequence of their acknowledgment at a time when it does not benefit them, and of their abandonment in the world when it would have benefited them: ﴿"Then taste the punishment"﴾, that is, that with which you were threatened, ﴿"because you used to disbelieve"﴾, that is, because of your persistence in concealing what your reason had pointed you to of the truthfulness of your messenger. There is no doubt that this speech, although it takes this form, contains a kind of kindness, because it is lighter than punishment accompanied by rejection, in the station of ﴿"Be silent therein and do not speak to Me"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 108]. For this reason, [that] was the last of the stations.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 6, verse 31:

Since what has preceded, the report of their loss of their own selves on the Day of Resurrection, has produced this, the listener anticipates its mention, so He said, confirming it, and adding weight to it, for it is from the taste of the punishment: ﴿They have certainly lost﴾. He made explicit the place of the pronoun for generality and to draw attention to what necessitated this for them, so He said: ﴿those who denied the meeting with Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, to whom all command belongs and with whom there is no command for anyone. [They] have lost everything that can be secured of great reward, and their denial persisted, ﴿until, when the Hour came upon them﴾, that is, the Reality, and likewise death, which is its beginning, for whoever dies, his hour has come. He warned them of it by His saying: ﴿suddenly﴾, that is, sudden (bāghitah), or possessing suddenness, or it surprised them by its coming at a time of heedlessness, such that they cannot perceive the exact time at which it comes, except for some kind of awareness. ﴿They will say, "Oh, our regret!"﴾, that is, "Come, O regret, be present with us, you who are befitting for us in this station! For we have no companion other than you." It is a metonymy for the greatness of the regret and an admonition about it, so that a person may refrain from its causes. ﴿for what we neglected﴾, that is, we fell short ﴿concerning it﴾, that is, concerning the Hour, so we missed what would make us happy in it, namely the refinement of character which prepares one for the race, by abandoning the following of the Messengers. This is because Allah created the accountable person and sent to him the rational, holy soul as a resident sent down to the lower world, and bestowed upon him manifest blessings, which are the outward perceptive senses and the organs and bodily instruments, and inward blessings, which are the intellect, the reflection, and others, so that he might use these powers and instruments as a means to attain true knowledge and virtuous character, whose benefits become greater after death. He sent the Prophets, peace be upon them, for guidance, and manifested miracles through them so that they might be believed. But they turned away from what they were called to, namely the purification of the soul, and devoted themselves to employing the faculties and powers in the transient pleasures and desires. Thus the bodily instruments, which are the capital, were lost, and what they supposed to be pleasures, which they counted as profits, perished; so they lost the provision, and did not prepare their souls for guidance. There is therefore neither capital nor profit, and they became in the utmost state of severance and estrangement, and there is no greater loss than this.

Since this was a dreadful matter, He increased its dreadfulness by reporting, in a circumstantial clause, the intensity of their weariness in that station and the weakness of their backs under their sins, as though heavy burdens were upon them. So He said: ﴿while they bear their burdens﴾, that is, while they said that and the state was that they ﴿bear their burdens﴾, that is, the loads of their sins, which by their nature are heavy. He confirmed the matter and depicted it by His saying: ﴿upon their backs﴾, because of the belief that the load is upon them, as one says, "The speech of so-and-so has weighed heavily upon you." It is also permissible that their deeds be embodied as heavy bodies, so that they are burdened with carrying them. And since that load is a matter whose description cannot reach our intellects' full grasp of the reality of its ugliness and heaviness, He pointed to this by His saying, comprehending all blameworthy things: ﴿Evil is what they bear!﴾

When the matter of resurrection had been confirmed to the utmost degree, and no one of sound mind could still hesitate over it, he (God) made explicit what the situation required regarding this worldly abode. He declared its lowliness and marveled at their intense desire to prefer its pleasures, informing them that He had unveiled the reality: what they had inclined toward is an illusion, and what they denied is a firm truth that has no end. This is the reverse of what they used to say: ﴿And what is the worldly life except amusement and diversion?﴾

Since the context concerns loss, and loss is most often connected with play (la'ib), which is the pursuit of what increases the soul's delight in an unlawful manner and whose passing is swift, He placed it first and said: ﴿But the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ [i.e.] for the wretched; and the worldly life is an evil for those who play. Lahw is whatever tends to please the soul, such as singing and the adornments of wealth and women, in a manner not permitted, so that it becomes a cause of heedlessness toward what benefits. [Thus the placing of lahw after la'ib indicates that the ignorant, whenever they slacken in play, which is occupation with base affairs and vain distractions, due to the lowliness of their souls, they stir up their desires through diversions.] The meaning is that from these signs the passing of this world is established, and thus its swiftness is realized, because everything that is coming is near. Then, the worldly life is nothing but an hour of play, over which a person regrets what he neglected within it, just as a player, if he has intellect, regrets missing profits when he sees what the earnest and the people of resolve have gained.

Since the implied sense of the context guided to the meaning, namely: "And the Hereafter is nothing but earnestness, presence and permanence for the God-fearing," He followed it with His emphatic statement: ﴿And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear God.﴾ Since all of them will ultimately return to the Hereafter, He specified: ﴿for those who fear God⦆, i.e., those who bring about taqwa (God-consciousness, the fear of God which moves one to perform acts of obedience and abandon sins, so that it becomes a protection for them from God's wrath). He mentioned the state of this world and omitted its outcome for its people, because the fruit of the Hereafter indicates it; and He omitted mention of the state of the Hereafter because the mention of the state of this world indicates it. This is ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two contrasting elements are mentioned in one part and omitted in the other, each indicating the omitted counterpart). Since it is the nature of intelligent people to turn toward what is good and abandon what is other than it, his statement, in rebuke, followed from their turning toward what is perishable and their abandoning what endures: ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾

When He repeated in this surah His command to dispute with them, extended His exhortation to argue against them, and concluded with what entails their being deprived of reason, while repeatedly informing that those destined to ruin among them will not believe, despite any sign, it was known that while they heard what He commanded him to say, they would not remain silent, because of their great arrogance, the swelling of their pride, and the strength of their audacity. They had no answer but insult and abuse, as is the habit of the stubborn one who has been defeated. That this would grieve him ﷺ, given his innate modesty, nobility, self-respect, and purity, made the situation require consolation. So God, exalted is He, said: ﴿We certainly know﴾. The present tense here denotes the existence of knowledge without reference to a particular time. He turned away from the past tense lest it be thought that the knowledge was restricted to a specific past occurrence. The intended meaning is the establishment of renewal, since knowledge is connected to the renewal of statements. ﴿Indeed, it grieves you﴾, that is, it continually and persistently causes you grief over the states of clarity that have been clouded for you. ﴿What they say﴾, that is, of your denial. We know your compliance with Our commands to recite to them what they dislike of Our transcendence, and We know their rejoinder to you with what does not please you, and We know that it reaches you. So do not grieve, for whoever knows that his Lord is pleased with the one who obeys Him and punishes the one who disobeys Him, and who knows what the obedient one attains through his obedience, should not grieve but rather rejoice. This is like His saying, exalted is He, in Surah Ya-Sin:

﴿So let not their speech grieve you. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they declare.﴾ [Ya-Sin: 76]

There is no doubt that grief at the occurrence of what is displeasing is part of human nature, which cannot be freed from it. Therefore the prohibition against it is a prohibition against what arises from it: continuous dwelling that leads to despair, which leads to lack of patience and forgetting what consoles. This is from the prohibition against the cause in order to emphasize the prohibition against the effect. How fitting is the mention of what causes grief after the affirmation that the worldly life is play and amusement for its people, and that the Hereafter is better for the God-fearing. It is known that these two are opposites, so one is not attained except by the opposite of what belongs to the other. Thus the Hereafter is not attained except by the opposite of what belongs to the people of this world, namely play and amusement. That is the grief arising from piety, which is motivated by fear, as is related in a ḥadīth qudsī (a hadith in which God speaks in the first person): «I am with those whose hearts are broken for My sake.»

When He, glorified is He, informed him of His knowledge of this, He made His saying dependent on it: ﴿For they﴾, that is, so do not let that grieve you, for they ﴿do not deny you﴾. Rather, you are among them the trustworthy one. Let Our knowledge of what you encounter from them be a cause for the removal of your grief, and likewise Our informing you that they do not deny you. Indeed, in reality you are trustworthy among them, not accused. But due to the severity of their obstinacy, their adherence to their interests, and their inability to find an answer that would cool their rage and cure their ailments, they deny the signs of God while knowing their truth. So let him lighten your grief for yourself, for what they violated of the sanctity of the One who sent you.

The verse is of the type called al-iḥtibāk (a rhetorical device in which something is omitted from each of two parts, the omitted element of each being indicated by the other). In the first part, the cause of grief, which is denial, is omitted, in order to show the nobility of the Prophet ﷺ and out of courtesy toward him. This omission is indicated by its mention in the second part. From the second part, the prohibition against the effect is omitted, because it is indicated by the first part.

Al-Ṭabarī related in his tafsīr, from al-Suddī, that on the day of Badr, al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq said to the Banū Zuhrah: "Muḥammad is your maternal nephew, and you are the most entitled to refrain from him. If he is a prophet, you will not fight him today; and if he is a liar, you are the most entitled to refrain from your nephew. Stand here until I meet Abū al-Ḥakam. If Muḥammad prevails, you will return safe; and if Muḥammad is defeated, your people will do nothing to you." That day he was called al-Akhnas, and his name had been Ubayy. Al-Akhnas met Abū Jahl, and al-Akhnas withdrew with him and said: "O Abū al-Ḥakam! Tell me about Muḥammad: is he truthful or a liar? For there is no one here from Quraysh besides you and me who hears our conversation." Abū Jahl said: "Woe to you! By God, Muḥammad is truthful, and Muḥammad has never lied. But when the Banū Qusayy take the banner, the custodianship of the Kaʿbah, the provision of water to pilgrims, and the prophethood, what then will remain for the rest of Quraysh?"

And on the authority of Nājiyah, he said: Abū Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not accuse you, but we accuse what you have brought." So God revealed the verse. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿But it is the wrongdoers﴾, placing "the wrongdoers" in the position of the pronoun, to generalize and to attach the judgment to the attribute. That is, those who were in a state of such darkness ﴿deny the signs of God﴾, that is, by means of the signs of God, that is, the Great Sovereign, to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿they reject﴾.

Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī said at the beginning of his book al-Ḥujjah: "That is, they reject what they knew of your truthfulness and trustworthiness." He connected the prepositional bā' (the "bi-" of ﴿bi-āyāt﴾) to "the wrongdoers," as it is in His saying: ﴿And We gave Thamūd the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged themselves through it﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 59], and similar usages. Ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said in his book al-Afʿāl: "Jaḥada al-shayʾ, jaḥdan wa-juḥūdan: he denied it while knowing it."

This is their intention, except that they have no way to deny the signs except through denial or what leads to it. You know that He who sent you is over all things Powerful, and He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the All-Aware. His power, His dominance, His victory for the people of His allegiance, and His restoration of them have required that a punishment befitting description come upon their enemies. And His wisdom has required that it not be hastened, as an honor to you and to increase your community.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 34:

When He consoled him with His promise of victory, which is grounded in the knowledge of the One who sends (the Messenger) and His power, and with the fact that their denial is in truth directed at Him—glory be to Him—and that He nonetheless bears patiently with them, forbears from them, and even shows them kindness through provision and benefits, He added to this that such is the practice (sunnah) regarding His brother messengers. So He said: ﴿And indeed messengers were denied﴾. Since what is to be emphasized is the denial itself and not who the denier is, the verb was put in the passive form: "﴿were denied﴾."

Since their denial did not extend over a long period of time, and since sharing in something makes it easier to bear, and the nearer the time, the more fitting this is, He introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿before you﴾, in that their people denied what they knew of their truthfulness and trustworthiness, just as was done to you. ﴿So they were patient﴾, meaning: as a consequence of their people's denial of them, they were patient ﴿over what they were denied and harmed﴾, meaning: they were also patient over the harm they suffered. Then He pointed to the promise of victory, on condition of patience, saying: ﴿until﴾, meaning: their patience continued until ﴿Our help reached them﴾. That is: let there be for you in them an example, and in them consolation, so be patient until help comes to you as it came to them. Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would indeed be the ones made victorious, in Our saying: ﴿Indeed, the party of Allah, they are the victorious﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 56]. ﴿And there is no changer of the words of Allah﴾, meaning: because for Him is all greatness, so none is His equal.

He—glory be to Him—indicated the great difficulty of the station of patience by emphasis, saying: ﴿And indeed there came to you﴾, and He indicated the magnitude of what they endured by His saying: ﴿some of the news of the messengers﴾, meaning: their great news in their patience, their forbearance, their obedience, their compliance, their gentleness toward those to whom they were sent, and Our help for them against those who transgressed against them. The coming of their news was previously mentioned in general and in detail. As for the general, it is in such verses as His saying: ﴿And how many a prophet fought, along with him many devoted ones﴾ [Al 'Imran: 146], and ﴿Is it that whenever a messenger came to you with what your souls did not desire...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 87]. As for the detail, it is in the mention of Musa, 'Isa, and others. And in His saying ﴿So they were patient﴾ is the clearest proof of what preceded: that the prohibition against grief is a prohibition against what follows it, which leads to the absence of patience. The expression with "min" (some of) as partitive is an amplification of what they encountered, and thus it is more eloquent in consolation.

When He consoled him with what is most complete in consolation, He informed him that he has no recourse except patience. So He said, linking it to what is implied: "Be consoled and be patient, as they were patient, and let what you encounter from them in the cause of God seem small to you: ﴿And if their turning away is great upon you﴾, i.e., it has become very grievous, ﴿their aversion﴾, i.e., from the signs that come to them from their Lord, about which We have already told you in Our saying: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it﴾ [al-An'am: 4]. And you wished to move, in Our informing you that the proposed signs will not benefit them, ﴿from the knowledge of certainty to the sight of certainty﴾. ﴿So if you are able to seek﴾, i.e., to strive with your effort and utmost capacity, ﴿a tunnel﴾, i.e., an opening, ﴿in the earth﴾ through which you may pass to whatever you can reach, ﴿or a ladder in the sky﴾, i.e., toward the heights, by which you may ascend to whatever you are able to reach, ﴿and bring them a sign﴾, i.e., what they have proposed to you, then do it, so that you may witness that they only increase in aversion when you bring it, as We have informed you. (p-100) This is because God has willed the misguidance of some of them. The purpose of this is to show the intensity of his ﷺ eagerness for their guidance, that if he were able to exert himself to descend beneath the earth or ascend above the sky and bring them what they would believe in, he would have done it."

Since this context might suggest something about power, He negated that, guiding to the understanding of what you have estimated, and so He said: ﴿And if God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾, i.e., He to whom belongs the overwhelming greatness and the complete, dominating power. ﴿He would have gathered them upon guidance﴾, i.e., because His power is all-encompassing, and their faith in itself is possible, but He has willed their separation by misguiding some of them. Since he ﷺ, after God informed him of what He had decreed, that signs do not benefit those who are sealed in disbelief, was still eager to respond to their proposals, hoping to gather them upon guidance, because of the excessive compassion with which he was made, toward a stranger, let alone a relative, together with what God had enjoined upon him on the night of al-Isra' (the Night Journey, the nocturnal journey to Jerusalem) without intermediary, as al-Harali has pointed out, of continuing compassion toward His servants, mercy for them, kindness to them, gentleness with them, and bringing joy to them, so that both his natural disposition and this injunction worked together upon that, until he would not refrain from it except by a decisive command or an emphatic, stern prohibition, he was led by this to His saying: ﴿So never be among the ignorant﴾. He, glorified is He, emphasized the statement so that he ﷺ would know that He had decreed their separation, so that he would be at rest with that (p-101) and turn away from what he was disposed to of intense compassion for them. ﴿Among the ignorant﴾, i.e., you are the most knowledgeable of people absolutely, and you possess complete discernment, penetrating insight, and clear reflection regarding those you have not associated with, so how about those whom you have tested since childhood, youth and maturity! So do not act on the pretext of what God has enjoined on you of patience and forgiveness, and what He has disposed you to of forbearance and clemency in seeking their faith, contrary to what is known of their loss. Do not make yourself hope for what has no prospect, for whatever He wills does not come to be [ghayruhu]. This verse and similar ones, which seem harsh in their outward meaning, indicate the great rank of his ﷺ and are among the subtle praises of the Qur'an for him, as will be explained, God willing, in Surat al-Tawbah at His saying: ﴿May God pardon you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43].

Since this decree of sealing made clear that their state had become that of those who have been sealed by death, so that they cannot be made to hear except by God, and cannot ordinarily respond, He said: ﴿Only those respond who hear﴾, i.e., within the normal course of your customs. ﴿Those who hear﴾, i.e., those who have the capacity for hearing, because they are living, so they then reflect upon what is conveyed to them and thereby benefit from it. These [disbelievers] have become equal to the dead in lacking the capacity to hear, because their faculties are sealed. ﴿And the dead﴾, i.e., all of them, sensorily and in meaning, ﴿God will raise them﴾, i.e., (p-102) the King, encompassing in knowledge and power. He is capable of raising them by bestowing faith upon the unbeliever and restoring the spirit to the one who is lost, so that they then hear. Thus the verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device of mutual omission): from the first part He omitted life, because "the dead" indicates it, and from the second part He omitted hearing, because ﴿they hear﴾ indicates it.

Since He had established that whoever does not believe is like the dead, as an exhortation to faith and an encouragement toward it, and had determined His power to raise, He warned of His assaults by saying: ﴿Then to Him﴾, i.e., to Him alone, ﴿they will be returned﴾, i.e., in meaning in this world, for He is capable of everything He wills concerning them, and nothing of their conditions escapes His will at all, either in meaning or sensorily after death. They will be driven by compulsion to a place of standing where every oppressed person will be separated from his oppressor.

When He consoled him (ﷺ) regarding what I had informed him of their statements, with what expanded his breast and gladdened his heart, and made him know, as a lightening for him, that their affair is only in His hand, He reminded him of some of their words, which lead to denial, following His informing him of the Gathering in which He recompenses each with what he does. So He said, as a continuation of His saying, ﴿And they say, "There is only our life of this world"﴾ [al-An'am: 29] and His saying, ﴿And they say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?"﴾ [al-An'am: 8], expressing wonder at them in another way: ﴿And they say﴾, i.e., through sophistry, obstinacy, or arrogance, ﴿why not﴾, i.e., "Would that", ﴿has been sent down﴾ (p-١٠٣) i.e., gradually, ﴿upon him﴾ i.e., specifically, ﴿a sign﴾ i.e., one single sign that remains established gradually and does not cease. This, from them, is an indication that they do not count the Qur'an as a sign, nor anything else they have seen from him (ﷺ) other than that, such as the splitting of the moon. ﴿from his Lord﴾ i.e., the One who bestows favour upon him, according to what he claims, so that we may infer from it what he says about Tawhid and resurrection.

Since in this, as has preceded, there is an indication from them that he has not brought a sign of this kind, whether by arrogance or by sophistry, He commanded him to answer with His saying, ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the One to whom belongs all the affair, ﴿is Able to﴾. By the intensive form of the verb (tashdid), He indicated the Qur'anic sign which is repeated upon them at all times, calling them to contest and challenging them with exaggeration and the challenge of inability, so He said, ﴿send down﴾. The recitation of Ibn Kathir with the light form (takhfif) indicates that they reached the utmost in impudence, and that if they had said "lawla unzila" (why was it not sent down), i.e., once, it would have been lighter in impudence, [or it indicates that any sign sent down upon them would compel them and force them to it at a single moment, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿If We willed, We could send down upon them a sign from the heaven, so that their necks would remain humbled before it﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 4], but He does not ask that except gradually, as the form of intensification (tafil) in the recitation of others, which is masculine, indicates] (p-١٠٤) that the sign of the Qur'an does not end; rather, whenever any one of them or of others hears it throughout the ages, it is sent down upon him, because it reaches him. Thus it is more eloquent than their request for a sign sent down upon him alone. The summary is that they asked for a sign that is purely lasting, so He hinted to them at a sign which, though specific to him in the honour that he attained, is general to everyone it reaches, lasting throughout time. ﴿a sign﴾, i.e., of what they proposed and of other things, nothing is beyond Him. In every thing He has signs that defy description, and the Great Qur'an suffices as an example of that. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾, i.e., they do not have the capacity for knowledge; they do not reflect upon anything of that which He originates of His creations, so that it would show them that He is over all things Competent. Thus there is no benefit for them in sending down what they request. As for the non-majority, He, glorified is He, turns them back with the sign of the Qur'an or others that they did not propose.

When He marvelled at their saying this, which implies that they had never seen any sign after the particular signs that came to them, signs that filled the horizons, returned hearing to the deaf, and lit sight for the blind, He reminded them of a sign other than the Qur'an. It comprises abundant signs sufficient for their righteousness, and He arranged it, glorified is He, (p. 105) before their asking, as a favour from Him to them. It indicates His manifest power over the resurrection and other things they had requested, and others, and His sole control over all affairs. If they reflected on it truly, it would suffice them for everything that is required of them. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And there is not﴾, i.e., they said this while the situation is that there is not, and it looks most directly at His saying ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ (6:2), i.e., He did that to you. ﴿Any creature on the earth﴾, i.e., one that crawls, i.e., moves by a foot or without a foot, ﴿nor any bird that flies﴾. He affirmed the reality with His saying ﴿on its two wings﴾. This includes all animals, even those in the sea, because their movement in water is either crawling or, metaphorically, flying.

Since the intended sense of "creature" and "bird" is generality, He said: ﴿but they are communities like you﴾, i.e., in that, and in that We created you when you were nothing, and We preserved all their conditions, decreed all their provisions and their terms, and made for you among them rulings that We renewed for you. We made for each of them a term of death which it does not exceed, after We differentiated among them in life. For all of them there is a term in Our knowledge, recorded in the intermediate realm (al-barzakh) before We created them, which will not decrease by an atom nor increase by a mustard seed. We placed in these animals some that are stronger than you and some that are weaker, and We made you stronger than all of them by reason. Had We willed, We would have made it (for it) between the strength of the body and reason. Sometimes We give the weaker power over you, such as locusts, mice and worms, with what your minds cannot withstand. Had We willed, We would have given power over you from the weakest of them in creation, the gnat, which would seize your breaths, deny you rest, remove you from voluntary movements, and destroy you all with the destruction of a single soul. This is among other matters that the intellects fall short of and that the windows of thought cannot reach. All of this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿We have neglected nothing﴾, i.e., We left out and omitted nothing, because of the complete power and comprehensive knowledge We possess, ﴿in the Book﴾, i.e., the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) and the Qur'an. He emphasised the negation with His saying ﴿anything﴾, i.e., so that its mention might be lost, as a necklace whose thread breaks and whose beads scatter. Rather, We have recorded all the states of Our creation, of jinn, humans, angels and others, of every speaking and silent thing, so that they are in the utmost precision. To the extent that the guardian angels (al-hafazah) present what occurs of the deeds of the responsible and others at the end of the day, upon what was recorded in the Mother of the Book (Umm al-Kitab), they find it just as it is, neither increasing nor decreasing, so they increase in faith. We have set forth in this Qur'an the comprehensive matters, so it is an exposition of everything: the rulings, both fundamental and derivative, the indications of all of that, the news of the earlier and later peoples, and every knowledge that the created may need. Whoever desires guidance, He guides him by its subtle secrets, and whoever turns away, He casts into ruin and blinds even to its clear lights. The sign is as He, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ (2:164), until He said: “And He dispersed therein every kind of creature. Are signs for a people who reason.”

؎ In everything there is a sign indicating that He is One.

Will there not be for you in that signs sufficient for you, without needing the sending of messengers, let alone that you should hesitate after their sending and not be satisfied with them except by the supernatural acts you propose?

When he had pointed out what the animals share with humans of the states of life and others, he specified the Gathering, which is the focal point of wisdom, so He said: ﴿Then﴾, i.e., after a long life and dwelling in the barzakh, ﴿to their Lord﴾, i.e., specifically, [and the passive was used following the manner of speech of the powerful, in His saying]: ﴿they will be gathered﴾ [i.e., they will be assembled unwillingly], after He restores them all as He originated them, and gives every oppressed person justice against his oppressor. All of that [is] easy for Him: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only as a single soul﴾ (31:28). All of them are preserved in a Clear Book, despite the differences of their kinds, the divergence of their realities and persons, and their increase in earnestness, so that He may direct the reckoning toward them. Glory be to Him who has encompassed all things in knowledge and enumerated all things by count. Indeed, that is easy for God, and He is capable of all things.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 39:**

(p. 108) Since the preceding reminder, through this verse in which the signs vary, recur, and their indications multiply, implies: "Those who believe are living, hearing Our words, speaking Our praises, and seeing Our deeds," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And those who denied﴾, that is, those who committed denial, ﴿Our signs﴾, that is, in light of the greatness they possess, which requires that they be attributed to Us, whether visible or audible, a repeated denial matching the number of the signs, actually or potentially, even by turning away from them. ﴿Deaf﴾, that is, dead, so they do not hear, ﴿and dumb﴾, who do not speak, ﴿in darkness﴾, that is, blind, who do not see. Therefore they continue stumbling like a blind camel (*khabṭ al-ʿashwāʾ*), striving with all their effort toward ruin, because that is the condition of one who is in darkness, so how much more of one who is in all the darknesses! Perhaps He combined them to indicate that the denier benefits neither from sight nor from insight, since, as they did not benefit from their lives, their hearing, their speech, their eyesight, or their minds, all of that was, in their case, nonexistent.

When He had made clear that the deaf, dumb, and blind cannot be guided, He made clear that this applies only with respect to others than Him, glorified is He, cutting off the expectation of answering them in what they demand of signs. As for Him, glorified is He, He is the Doer of what He wills. So He said, in answer to one who seems to have said, "Guidance for them is only possible if...": ﴿Whomever Allah wills﴾, that is, He to whom the command belongs entirely and to whom no one has any command alongside Him, ﴿He leaves astray﴾, ﴿and whomever He wills﴾ [to be guided], (p. 109) ﴿He places it﴾, and He indicated His empowering him by the particle of elevation (*ʿalā*, "upon"), so He said: ﴿upon a straight path﴾, by creating guidance in his heart. ﴿And whoever Allah guides, there is no misguider for him, and whoever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾, although all of them are His servants and His creatures, moving about in His bounties, going and coming in His kindness and generosity. Indeed, in that is evidence of His oneness and the perfection of His power: ﴿surely there are clear signs in that for a people who reason﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 40:

When this verse, with its explicit statement of denial, was closely bound to His saying ﴿And who is more wrong than one who invents a lie against Allah?﴾ [al-An'am: 21] and His saying ﴿They denied the truth when it came to them, but there will soon come to them the news﴾ [al-An'am: 5], the two verses, he returned with what follows to the summation (fadhlakah) of the previous details, the central thread (wasitat 'iqdiha) and the unique pearl of their string, which is the Tawhid that the proofs had made clear before the two verses. So he said, indicating their belief in the power whose denial was implied by their demand for a sign, and their belief in Tawhid in general while they denied it, as a clarification that they are, in the darknesses, subdued under the hand of the Will, because they do not shy away from contradiction, marveling at them: ﴿Say: Tell me﴾ meaning: inform me, O you who denied the signs and the power out of obstinacy, and who testified that there are other gods with Allah and set up equals to Allah, who knows the secret and the open, and who is with whomever calls upon Him in every heaven and every earth by His care and His help.

Since the literal meaning of ﴿Tell me﴾ is "Have you seen yourselves?", and since this is a question about something known which no one is ignorant of, indicating that a question about anything else that may be hidden of the states of the soul, it was as if it were said: About which states of our souls are we asked? So it was said, alerting them to a state that obliges them to Tawhid or to the obstinacy which, in knowledge of it, becomes like a question about seeing oneself, equally: ﴿If there comes upon you﴾ meaning: before the coming of the Hour, as it came upon those before you, ﴿the punishment of Allah﴾ meaning: the One who combines all the attributes of greatness, so no one can remove what He brings, ﴿or the Hour comes upon you﴾ meaning: the Resurrection with its terrors.

When He marveled at them with what has passed, as has passed, He said, answering the condition, rebuking them and reproaching them for not persisting in calling upon Him and for not holding fast to asking Him and calling on Him, [and it is permissible that the answer to the condition be omitted, its estimate being: Whom do you call upon? Then He added to their rebuke and confounding by His saying]: ﴿Other than Allah﴾ meaning: the King to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿do you call upon﴾ meaning: for a hardship of those hardships, and you do not call upon Allah along with that other, ﴿if you are truthful﴾ meaning: in that other than Allah avails anything such that it deserves divinity. The answer to the condition is omitted, its estimate being: then call upon that other. This is a proof which leaves them no option but acknowledgment, for their custom was consistently that when the matter became severe and the strait pressed, they did not call upon anyone other than Allah nor direct their resolve except to Him. If they follow the path of truthfulness, which they claim and by which they boast, and say: "We do not call upon other than Him," then the proof is binding upon them that nothing is to be set equal to Him and that He has no partner. (p-111) If they are obstinate, the tongue of their state speaks that they are in pure error; and if they remain silent, the address is established against them. This, as you see, is also evidence of what the verse before it reported, that the whole matter belongs to Allah, meaning: all of you share in the clarity of the matter, that there is no recourse except to Him, yet you have divided, so some were truthful and others denied. Had the matter depended only on the clarity of the proof, all would have been upon one course.

Abu Hayyan transmitted from al-Farra' that he said: For the Arabs, in "ara'ayta" there are two usages and two meanings. One: you ask a man "ara'ayta Zaydan," meaning with your eye, and this is hamzated. Second: you say "ara'ayta" while you mean "akhbirni" (tell me), and here you may drop the hamza if you wish, and this is the more common in Arab speech; and the dropping of the hamza indicates the distinction between the two meanings. Then Abu Hayyan said: That "ara'ayta" and "ara'aytaka" mean "akhbirni" is attested by Sibawayh and other imams of the Arabs, and it is an explanation of meaning, not an explanation of grammatical construction; because "akhbirni" is transitive with "'an," whereas "ara'ayta" is transitive to a direct object and to a interrogative clause which stands in the position of the second object. He said, in Surat Yunus, peace be upon him: It has passed in Surat al-An'am that the Arabs make "ara'ayta" carry the meaning of "akhbirni," and that it then is transitive to two objects, and that the second object is most often an interrogative clause, from which and from what precedes it a subject and predicate are formed. The Arabs say: "Ara'ayta Zayda ma sana'a?" meaning: Tell me about Zayd, what he did! And before "ara'ayta" entered, the sentence was: "Zayd, what he did." End. I say: The literal meaning, as already passed, is: Have you seen Zayd? When he asked about seeing him, and the intent is information, not sight, it is known that the question is about some of his states, so it was as if it were said: What is his condition? It was said: What did he do?

When the interrogative of denial carries the sense of negation, it is as though it had been said: "You do not call upon other than Him." So He joined to it His words: ﴿Nay, it is Him alone that you call upon﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿you call upon﴾, that is, at that time. Since calling upon Him sometimes results in answer and at other times in something else, He said: ﴿then He removes﴾, that is, Allah, in this world or in the Hereafter, for nothing is obligatory upon Him and nothing wrong can proceed from Him, ﴿that for which you call upon Him﴾, that is, its removal, ﴿if He wills﴾, that is, He removes it as an act of grace upon you, as is His custom with you in times of your hardships. However, He does not will to remove it in the Hereafter, because "the word is not changed with Him" (Qur'an 50:29), although He is able to do whatever He wills. Had He answered you always, while you called upon none other than Him, that would have been sufficient as an indication of your belief that there is no one capable except Him. How much more so, since He answers you in this world when you call upon Him at times, and answers you at other times (p-113). Yet, despite that, the non-answer does not turn you away from the belief in His power and from persistent turning to Him in such a state, owing to what He placed in sound minds and in the primordial natures (fitar, the innate disposition) that He is the Doer who chooses. This is indicated by His words, joined in conjunction with (you call upon): ﴿and you forget﴾, that is, you abandon, at those times, always, ﴿what you associate﴾, that is, of your false objects of worship, because you know that they avail nothing, as is always your custom at times of hardship, returning to the state of uprightness. Should this not be a deterrent for you from associating partners with Allah in times of ease, out of fear of the return of adversity?

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 42:

When he had established for them, through this verse, the proof of His Oneness, to the point that the paths were made clear in reminding them that supplication (al-tadarru') may remove affliction through it, He informed them that abandoning it brings about wretchedness, as an encouragement to persist in it and a warning against turning away from it. So He said: ﴿And We had certainly sent﴾, meaning: with what We possess of greatness, ﴿to nations﴾, meaning: peoples, some of whom lead others, and who are worthy of being sought out by people because of their abundance and greatness.

Since the intended meaning is some of the nations, namely those whom God willed to bear witness to and whose reports He related, He introduced the preposition, and said: ﴿before you﴾, meaning: messengers, and they opposed them. This omission is made good by the fact that it is understood. ﴿Then We seized them﴾, meaning: our sending to them was the cause for Us to seize them with Our greatness, so that they would turn back from what Satan had made attractive to them toward what the messengers called them to, ﴿with adversity﴾, through the imposition of killing upon them, ﴿and hardship﴾, through the imposition of poverty and pains, ﴿that they might humble themselves﴾, meaning: so that their state would be that of one whose submission and humility are hoped for, in an eloquent manner, which is indicated by the form of the verb (yatadarra'una, with the intensive form, tafa''ala), together with the manifest meaning. And because its purpose is to argue for Oneness, and at the disclosure of the foundations it is fitting to make the worship complete, unlike what comes in al-A'raf.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 6, verse 43:

When what had happened from them was not what the circumstances had made him hope for, the rebuke against them followed from that. So he said, expressing it with the particle of restriction (*adat al-takhsis*), so that together with the negation it conveys that they had no excuse for abandoning humble supplication: ﴿Why then did they not humble themselves when Our punishment came upon them?﴾ That is, "Why did they not do so?" Since the meaning of the rebuke is that [they did not] humble themselves, he said: ﴿But their hearts became hardened﴾, that is, they did not remember their Lord at all. ﴿And Satan made attractive to them﴾, that is, through what entered upon them by way of the desires, ﴿what they were doing﴾, of the great sins and evil deeds, which the reversal (*naks*) brought about by being turned back down to the lowest of the low required.

﴿Then when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, i.e., as a consequence of their abandoning the admonition and of not acting upon its benefit, which is humility and tranquility, as is fitting for them especially in that situation, ﴿We opened for them﴾, i.e., in a manner befitting Our greatness, ﴿the gates of every thing﴾, i.e., of good things, provisions and pleasures, which had been closed to them, and We moved them from hardship to ease. This was a ﻿istidraj (gradual lulling into ruin) for them. We extended their time and prolonged their days. ﴿Until, when they rejoiced﴾, i.e., their joy reached its height ﴿in what they had been given﴾, i.e., turning away from the One who granted them this ease after He had tested them with that (hardship). Thus it is known that they were in the utmost heedlessness, not deterred by being disciplined with the whips of affliction, nor benefiting from the carpet of bounty and ease. Rather, they thought that affliction was merely the custom of the age and that ease was owed to their deserving of gratitude. Thus it is known that their hearts are not hoped to awaken, whether by hot or cold, moist or dry (means). ﴿We seized them﴾ by Our greatness. We seized them in a state of ease so that their regret would be more intense, ﴿suddenly﴾, so We did not give them opportunity to plead humbly at the onset of the matter, nor did We grant them any respite at all. Rather, there descended upon them the heavy weight of punishment, and there fell upon them the burdens of hardships and the vicissitudes of calamities, which bewildered them and occupied them from everything, until they were struck dumb. ﴿Then behold, they were in despair﴾, i.e., as a consequence of that sudden seizure, they were overtaken by silence over what was in their souls, and by despair, out of regret and bewilderment. They remained, after falling silent, until they became still and subdued. Thus, in negating supplication from the earlier nations, after having affirmed it for the polytheists of this community, there is a subtle appeal to compassion. And in mentioning the istidraj of those (earlier peoples) through blessings at the time of forgetting what they had been reminded of, and then their sudden seizure by the devastating vengeance, there is the utmost warning.

When it was customary for the victor among worldly people to miss the last of the armies and its stragglers, owing to the weariness of his companions from pursuit, their exhaustion from toil and fatigue, and their inability to encompass all the objectives, Allah the Exalted informed that His seizing was otherwise, and that His attaining the last was like His attaining the first, on an equal footing. So He said, stating the cause of the aforementioned seizing, and indicating by the passive construction the completeness of power and by *dabir* (the last remnant) the total uprooting: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off﴾, meaning the last of ﴿the people who did wrong﴾, that is, by placing a thing in other than its proper place, like one walking in darkness. They placed harshness where compassion was called for, and they placed rejoicing at blessing where fear of being returned to hardship was called for. Likewise you did wrong by calling upon idols in times of ease, when that was the place for calling upon the One who bestowed those blessings, and you called upon Allah in times of hardship, when that was the place for calling upon the One you worshipped in times of ease. This was so that you would not fall into what your custom had long reproached.

A poet said:
"When a dreadful matter occurs, Judab is called for it,
and when the Hays is being mixed, Jundab is called."

Since their uprooting was among the greatest blessings upon the messengers, peace be upon them, and their followers, may Allah be pleased with them, who were opposed by these people, He alerted to this by the general statement together with what it indicates of the manifest absolute self-sufficiency. So He said: ﴿And praise belongs﴾, meaning their entire affair was cut off, while the encompassing of all attributes of perfection belongs ﴿to Allah﴾, the One singular in the qualities of majesty and beauty, ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, the Originator of all of them. That is, all of that belongs to Him after the annihilation of creation, in whatever state they were, whether of faith or disbelief, just as it belonged to Him before their existence and at their creation, in each of their two conditions. This is what was indicated at the beginning of the surah. It is as if it were said: perfection belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; then those who disbelieve in their Lord ascribe equals to Him. So their last remnant was cut off, and perfection remains His, unchanged, for the existence of any existent does not add to Him, and the non-existence of any non-existent does not diminish Him. Thus He is praised in the state of annihilation and destruction just as He was praised in the state of origination and creation. So do not let your soul go in pursuit of them out of grief. Nothing comes out of their faith or their disbelief outside His will, glorified is He. Therefore it does not matter to you whether they ask for signs or not, for upon you is only the conveying (of the message).

When he had first made a warning through the coming of punishment in general, in every circumstance, and since the coming expressed with the *kāf* (the second-person suffix *kāf al-khiṭāb*, "the kāf of address") there carried emphasis while also indicating a kind of delay, and since he followed this with the point that the seizing of the nations was sudden, he then gave a warning about a specific punishment whose horror, once imagined, makes the limbs tremble, cuts the liver, and fills the hearts with dread, for there is no state more dreadful than being deaf, blind, and mad. So he said, indicating by dropping the *kāf* of address (p-118) while expressing the seizing that is known to mean a sudden overtaking with force and subjugation, pointing to the extreme warning against the speed of the seizing: ﴿Say: Tell me﴾. The reality of what is joined with the *kāf* was: "Have you seen yourselves?" Here, however, it is "Have you seen" in the absolute sense of sight, because of the earlier allusion to hastening the answer out of fear of being suddenly struck by punishment. Although in both places the intended meaning is: inform me, ﴿if God takes away﴾, that is, the One Who is capable of everything and knows everything, ﴿your hearing﴾, and he made it singular because there is little variation in it, for it is the greatest means of perceiving, and the heart, in which there is no greater variation, even for one person in different states, so that this would more clearly show the act by choice. ﴿And your sight﴾, that is, He would make you blind and deaf, both outwardly and inwardly, by taking away benefit. ﴿And seals upon your hearts﴾, so that they cannot understand at all, or cannot benefit from understanding. ﴿Who is a god﴾, that is, a deity worthy of worship; for He has comprehensive knowledge and power. Then he described this report by saying: ﴿other than God﴾, that is, the One who possesses all greatness, ﴿will bring it to you﴾, that is, with that which is the most noble of the meanings of your most noble organs, or with some part of it.

When these verses reached the highest stations of clarity in expounding His oneness and the falsehood of every deity other than Him, he drew attention to the fact that He is upon this, by commanding them to reflect on these verses and on their own state after them, indicating what was said earlier: that suggested signs do not benefit those whom He, glorified be He, wills to be wretched. So He said: ﴿Observe how We vary﴾, [that is]: by what We have of greatness, ﴿the signs﴾, that is, We reveal them to them and to others in every aspect of clarification, with an excellence sufficient to seize minds and bewilder intellects, and sufficient to convey one to the desired goal. And since turning away from such is at the utmost extreme of remoteness, he expressed it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then they﴾, that is, after this clarification, with the core of their inner selves, ﴿turn away﴾, that is, they turn away with an aversion that clings to them as an inseparable attribute.

When He joined the seizing (al-akhdh) with the sudden onset (al-baghtah), sometimes explicitly and sometimes by dropping the kaf, it may have occurred to the listener to ask about the state of the open, visible punishment. So He followed this with a detailed mention of the states that were stated in summary in the two previous verses, and said: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of God came upon you﴾. Since the meaning is "Inform me," and it was as if it was said, "About what?", it was answered: ﴿if the punishment of God comes upon you﴾, meaning the One who has all attributes of perfection, so nothing can overpower Him, ﴿suddenly﴾, meaning in such a way that it is not seen except as it overtakes you, without any sense of it beforehand and without any of its signs appearing,

﴿or openly﴾, meaning in such a way that you see it coming toward you, advancing upon you, ﴿will any be destroyed﴾.

Since what is frightening in itself is the destruction, without regard to identifying the agent, the verb is put in the passive: ﴿be destroyed﴾, meaning in either of the two states, a destruction that is destruction indeed, namely the destruction of wrath. ﴿except the people﴾, meaning those who possess the strength to resist and the severity of fighting, in your own opinion, and opposition, ﴿who are wrongdoers﴾, meaning those who place things in other than their proper places, by giving a thing to one who does not deserve it and withholding from one who deserves what is due to him. As for the one who reforms, he is saved, either in both abodes or in the Hereafter, the abode in which whoever succeeds has no loss (p-120). Abu Hayyan mentioned that since the absolute term "punishment" is suitable for every detail of its terrors that is known and those that are not known, the threat of it is more terrifying. For this reason, the address was emphasized in the two verses by the pronoun together with the particle of address, whereas the threat of the seizing of hearing and what accompanies it, being among the kinds of punishment included in that absolute term, was stripped of the particle of address.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 48:

When all of that was in the contention with those who denied the messengers, and who turned away from what their Lord had sent them of signs, of which there is none but that a human being would believe in its like, and in their demand of what none can bring about except the One who sent them, namely the bringing of signs other than those they had brought, [Allah] made clear to them the reality of the messengership, pointing to their wrongdoing in demanding of the messengers what can only be demanded of God. So He said, in conjunction with ﴿And We have sent messengers to nations before you﴾ [al-An'am: 42], ﴿And We send not the messengers﴾, meaning: by what We have of majesty, ﴿the messengers﴾, meaning: We bring this matter into existence in this time and in every time, past and other than it, ﴿except as bringers of good tidings﴾ to whoever obeys, ﴿and warners﴾ to whoever disobeys, excelling in each of the two attributes, neither responding to what the nations propose, nor punishing those who oppose them. Then He traced to this the ultimate purpose of the messengership in terms of benefit and harm, saying: ﴿So whoever believes and makes amends﴾, meaning: confirming his faith through deeds, ﴿there shall be no fear for them﴾, meaning: neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. As for the Hereafter, it is clear; as for this world (p-121), which is transient, their fear in it increases their security in the Hereafter, which is everlasting, for it is passing to an end and then to a perpetual joy, so it is non-existence. ﴿nor shall they grieve﴾, meaning: a grief that harms their everlasting life.

When He had explained the state of the righteous (al-muslihin), He followed it with the state of the corrupters (al-mufsidin), saying: ﴿And those who denied Our signs﴾, i.e., in spite of the greatness they possess by their attribution to Us, ﴿the punishment will touch them﴾, i.e., the constant, ever-renewed (punishment). He expressed its nearness by giving it the power of touch, as if it were a living, willing being, and so said: ﴿because they used to defiantly disobey﴾, i.e., by disposition and nature, ﴿they used to go out of bounds (yafsuqun)﴾, i.e., they perpetually go out of what should be steadfastly kept, namely faith and what it requires. As for incidental transgression (al-fisq al-ʿaridh), its doer, when he repents from it, is pardoned.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 50:

When He had clarified the function of the messengers and divided those to whom they were sent, He commanded him to deny what their claims entail: that a human being cannot be a messenger, and their demand that he show them signs, based on the assumption that he has power over whatever he wills, or that he would display for them everything he is able to do, or that he is obligated to do so. Some of this they said out of their coarseness or obstinacy, wronging themselves. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, in answer to their saying

"﴿Why has no sign been sent down to him?﴾ [Yunus: 20]" and the like.

Since they had no knowledge that a human being could possess the treasuries and dispose of them as he wishes, and since he had been bringing them signs such as the splitting of the moon (p. 122), the walking of trees, the speech of the lizard and the stone, the gushing of water, the guarding by a flame of fire, the stallion camel, and similar things known from the proofs of prophethood, which perhaps led them to assume that what this entails is his claim that he owns the treasuries, they kept demanding of him signs that show this, [as an obligation upon him] with that aim, intending to deny him. He denied what they supposed his claim necessarily entailed, so He said: ﴿I do not tell you﴾, that is, now or in the future. Since God had given him the keys to the treasuries of the earth, and he refused them out of humility before God, glorified is He, the phrase "to you" was attached, to make clear what he tells the believers of this, so that their faith increases along with their faith. As for the disbelievers, telling them of it would only incite them to make demands in mockery, so there is no benefit in it. ﴿With me are the treasuries of God﴾, that is, the supreme dominion, which holds absolute wealth and perfect might. ﴿Nor do I have knowledge of the unseen﴾, i.e., "So I will bring you what you demand of signs, what you desire of hoards, and what you mock with of punishment," but the treasuries are in His hand, and He does with them what He wills.

Since they knew that some human beings, namely the soothsayers (kuhhan), tell of some of the unseen, and since the soothsayers mix truth with falsehood, and since the Prophet (ﷺ) told them of many unseen matters which always came to pass exactly as he said, with no discrepancy, addition, or deficiency in any of them, they began to think that he knows the unseen. But they (p. 123) regarded this as one of the signs of the soothsayers, until they labelled him a soothsayer. They used to ask him about the time of the punishment he threatened them with and about other things, hoping to catch him in something the soothsayers say that does not come to pass, and then they would hold it against him. He denied what they supposed about him in this context: that he should be attributed to other than its owner, who cannot be shared with another. So He said, denying it from its root and not only as a statement, as in what precedes and follows it, linking it to ﴿I do not tell﴾, not to ﴿with me﴾: ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾, that is, "So I will inform you of the time of the separation between me and you, whether of general punishment or the arrival of the Hour." For these two conditions, owning the treasuries and knowing the unseen, belong only to the rank of divinity. I did not claim the first, as you accuse me, nor did I attribute to myself the second in the way you suppose.

Since they thought that a messenger can only be an angel, they would hold him to his claim of messengerhood as a claim to be an angel, so that they could hold him to what is plainly false. He said: ﴿Nor do I say﴾, that is, the claim of being a messenger. Since he (ﷺ) was the highest of the prophets in purity, the brightest of them in heart, the most illuminating of them in every guidance, and the most free of human deficiencies, and since this was a matter from God to him, the phrase "to you" was attached to make clear that it is not impossible for him to say it. Rather, had he said it, he would have been truthful (p. 124). Many similar expressions occur in their figures of speech and their customary modes [in their discourse]. As for the omission of "to you" in the story of Noah in the surah of Hud, peace be upon them both, it was out of humility on his part, since it is his own statement, without explicitly attributing the matter to God, the Exalted: ﴿I am not an angel﴾, so that I would be able to perform the acts which angels can perform, such as abstaining from food, drink, and other acts of angels.

When what they had charged him with and what they supposed about him, that he is a god or an angel, was denied, the matter was confined to his being a messenger who stops at what his sender has set for him. So He said, as a conclusion: ﴿I follow only﴾, that is, with utmost effort, ﴿what is revealed to me﴾, that is, my rank is nothing but obeying what my Lord commands me in this Qur'an, which, given your inability to produce its like, is the greatest witness for me. Nothing was revealed to me in it to say any of what has been denied above. It was revealed to me so that I might warn you of it in particular, and warn with it everyone it reaches in general. This is not unreasonable to the intellect nor improbable; indeed, sending has occurred to many human beings. Its establishment for me has been proven by clear proofs, established arguments, and decisive demonstrations. If there is permission for me to produce a miracle, I will produce it; if there is information in it about the unseen, I will disclose it; otherwise I will limit myself to delivering (p. 125) with the challenge. He informs them that God, whose word has been established by your inability to match it, bears witness for me to the truth of the message and the veracity of the claim.

Since it has been established by this that they are blind in sight and insight, unable to be guided to what benefits them, and unable to silence an opponent or escape from delusion or blemish, but are rather like one who travels among perils, whose claim to wisdom at the very start shows his falsehood, his lie, and his wickedness, following desire, which is the most harmful of diseases, and that he (ﷺ) is the keenest of the perceptive and the wisest of the wise to those who follow him, the knower of the unseen, and it was the place where it should be said, "What is revealed to you in this context?" He said, as a rebuke to them: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to everyone who hears your words after this clarification, which exceeds human faculties, ﴿Is the blind equal to the seeing?﴾, that is, would they be equal without doubt? If they say "Yes," they contradict the senses. If they say "No," it is said: whoever follows these clear signs is the seeing, and whoever turns away from them is the blind, and whoever equates the Creator with any of His creatures is the most blind of the blind. Then, after denying their equality, He commanded him to rebuke them for the corruption of their reasoning and the blindness of their thinking, saying: ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾, that is, so that your thinking may turn you back from these errors.

When He commanded him to rebuke them, He commanded him, coordinating with His words "Say" (﴿قُلْ﴾), to warn them in a manner that also disgraces them, so He said: ﴿And warn thereby﴾, that is, by what is revealed to you. The intent is not to restrict the warning to those who fear, but to point to their coarseness, their great dullness, and their density in refusing to admit what is possible, which everyone should fear, by His words: ﴿those who fear﴾, that is, by accepting as possible what is possible rationally and customarily.

Since the thing feared is the gathering itself, not restricted to its being from a particular source, His words ﴿to be gathered﴾ are in the passive voice, meaning: to be brought together while they are unwilling, ﴿to their Lord﴾, that is, the One who has shown them kindness by bringing them into being and nurturing them, despite their shortcoming in gratitude, while ﴿they have not﴾ ﴿besides Him﴾. He indicates the belittling of anything other than Him and its lowliness by the prepositional phrase, so He said ﴿besides Him﴾, that is, from any station beneath His station. It is known that everything is under the dominion of His greatness and is diminished before His rank, and they have no ﴿protector﴾ who would manage their affairs and rescue them by force from what they fear, ﴿nor any intercessor﴾ who would rescue them through his good mediation and great rank, ﴿so that they may fear God﴾, that is, so that their state becomes that of one who is hoped to place between himself and the punishment of God a shield.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 52:

When He commanded him to call to those who turned away from him and to proclaim the message openly, He commanded him to guard those who followed him and to be gentle with them. So He said: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾, meaning the poor among the Muslims, ﴿their Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to them, in contrast to the disbelievers, who call upon those who possess neither harm nor benefit for them. Then He described their state of constant devotion, which requires sincerity, saying: ﴿morning and evening﴾, that is, at the two ends of the day in general (p-127), or at their two prayers, or it may be a metaphor for constancy. Then He followed this with its outcome, expressing the Essence by the Face, because the face is the most noble part, as we commonly understand it, and remembering it necessitates glorification and produces shame at falling short: ﴿seeking His Face﴾, that is, because if it were show-off, it would have vanished over the passage of time and the alternation of events, through the change of circumstances.

Since the great men among the polytheists and their wealthy ones had promised him ﷺ that they would follow him if he drove away those who followed him from among those whom they disdained to sit with, and had discouraged him from them because of their poverty and because they were not sincere in following him, and had only urged him to that out of need, Allah, exalted is He, made clear to him that he had no stake in driving them away, nor in following those others in this way, except for the sake of this world, from which he was sent to warn. So He said, giving the reason for what preceded or beginning a new statement: ﴿Not on you﴾. He put first what was most important to him, which is bearing it, ﴿for their account﴾, and He went to the extreme in negation, saying: ﴿any [part]﴾, that is, you have nothing but their outward appearance, and nothing of their account is upon you, so that you should deal with them in the way they deserve inwardly by driving them away if they are not sincere. ﴿Nor is any of your account﴾, He again put first what was most important in that regard, ﴿upon them any [part]﴾, that is, nothing of your account is upon them, so that you should fear that they would wrong you in it if they were deceitful, or nothing of your provision is upon them so that they would burden you with it (p-128), nor is any of your provision upon them so that they would be weakened by it because of their poverty. Rather, the Provider of both you and them is Allah. Then He answered the negation by making its consequence explicit, saying: ﴿so that you would drive them away﴾, that is, from one of the two matters follows your driving them away, so that the wealthy would turn toward you and not impose on you what those others were imposing on you, and if you were to impose on them what those others could not bear, they would bear it. The summary is that the meaning of the two sentences ﴿Not on you for their account﴾ through to the end of them may refer back to the verse of the Cave:

﴿And do not let your eyes pass beyond them, desiring the adornment of the worldly life﴾ [al-Kahf: 28]. In that case the meaning concerns provision, that is: your call to Allah revolves around the matter of the Hereafter, so none of these people's provision is upon you such that you would be pressed by them and inclined toward the wealthy, nor is any of your provision upon them such that they would be unable to bear it. The wording, in the language of the lexicographers, admits this meaning. The author of al-Qamus and others said: al-Hisab means sufficiency, and from it comes ﴿a gift in sufficiency﴾ [al-Naba': 36]. And "hasiba fulan fulanan" means he fed him and gave him drink until he was satisfied and quenched. Abu 'Ubayd al-Harawi said: it is said, "I gave him and ahsabtuh," meaning I gave him sufficiency until he said, "Enough for me (hasbi)." His saying, "He provides whom He wills without reckoning" means without restriction or constriction. In the hadith of Simak: "ma hasabu dayfahum" (p-129), meaning they did not honour their guest. Ibn Faris said in al-Mujmal: "ahsabtuhu" means I gave him what pleased him, and "hassabtuhu" likewise, and "ahsabani al-shay'" means it sufficed me.

When He forbade him from driving them away, making clear that this would be harm without benefit, He made the following statement a consequence of this prohibition: ﴿so you would be among the wrongdoers﴾, that is, by placing a thing in other than its proper place. Driving these people away is not a cause of those others' faith, and their guidance lies only with Us. They had asked Us concerning you, when We tested them by singling you out for the message, for what is not hidden from you of their saying: ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him?﴾ [al-An'am: 8] and similar things by which they intended to turn you away. Just as We did not accept them concerning you, do not you accept them concerning Our friends, for We tested them through you until they asked about you what they asked and wished for [what they wished for].

[And thus] i.e., in the same way as We tested them by sending you, [We tested] i.e., We acted as one who tests, forcibly, by the majesty that is Ours, [some of them by means of others] by singling them out with faith, wealth, poverty, and the like, [so that they would say] i.e., in denial, because another's being favoured over them is contempt and belittlement of them, [Are these the ones] i.e., those who are not equal to us, nor even close to us in any one of the qualities of worldly life, [whom God has favoured] i.e., despite His majesty and greatness, [over us, from among us?] i.e., He has guided them to the truth and to what makes them happy with Him, while in our view they are lowly. So the verse refers to what comes later in this surah, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of God﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

[p. 130] Since denial is not appropriate except with complete knowledge of the ranks of those who are preferred, and that the one preferred does not deserve preference in respect of the aspect for which he is preferred, He denied their denial with His saying: ﴿Is not God most knowing of the grateful?﴾ i.e., He to whom belongs the whole command, so there is no objection to Him, [of the grateful] i.e., those who deserve to be preferred because of their gratitude, over others who are preferred for their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 54:

When He (ﷺ) forbade him from driving them away, He taught him how to be gentle with them, saying: [coordinating with what is implied, meaning: "And when those who look down on the weak among My servants come to you, do not concern yourself with them"]: ﴿And when they come to you﴾. He stated the noun in place of the pronoun, to indicate the quality that calls for honouring them, and to generalise the ruling to others. So He said: ﴿who believe﴾, that is, they or others, whether rich or poor. By using the designation of majesty, He indicated that they believed in what is deserving of belief, so He said: ﴿in Our signs﴾, given the greatness they have in relation to Us. ﴿So say﴾, that is, to them, beginning with greeting, as an honour to them and a comfort to their hearts: ﴿Peace be upon you﴾, that is, safety from Me and from God. He made it indefinite (nakira) because of the calamities that befall them in this world. Then He justified this by His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾, that is, the One who is good to you. Then He justified that [by His saying] and resumed with what amounts to this: He knew the deficiency in man, because He created him with the dispositions of loss, except for the one whom He made a recipient of favour. So He said: ﴿that whoever of you does evil﴾, that is, whatever evil it is, (p-131) ﴿in ignorance﴾, that is, through foolishness or a lightness and movement that took him out of the truth and knowledge, to the point that it was as if he knew nothing. ﴿Then repents﴾, that is, returns with remorse and giving up (the sin), even if a long time has passed. For this reason He introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿after it﴾, that is, after that deed. ﴿And amends﴾ by persisting in good. ﴿Then indeed He﴾, that is, your Lord, because of this repentance, ﴿forgives him﴾. For He is always ﴿Oft-Forgiving﴾, that is, of far-reaching concealment and erasure of what was from that. ﴿Most Merciful﴾, who honours whoever repents this repentance by making him like one who did good, after He has made him, through forgiveness, like one who did not sin. As for whoever persists and corrupts, He punishes him, for He is ﴿Almighty, All-Wise﴾. It may be that the verse is referring to what the polytheists slandered them with, of lack of sincerity, and in that case it would be a preparatory indication, since what is meant by reckoning (al-hisab) is being held accountable for sins.

Now, since this surah and what precedes it have presented the wondrous details concerning all conditions, containing clear indications and dazzling, manifest signs, He said, connecting by conjunction to ﴿And thus We test﴾ [al-An'am: 53], a conjunction of opposite to its opposite, for in testing there is a kind of concealment: ﴿And thus﴾, i.e., and like the trials, by presenting some of what is subtle and hidden from certain aspects, ﴿so that We may mislead whom We will﴾, whereby the misguided is distinguished from the guided. ﴿We detail the verses﴾, those whose clarification We intend, so that the way of the righteous becomes clear and is followed, ﴿and that the way of the criminals may become evident﴾, i.e., may appear with clear manifestation, so that it is avoided. He specified this by mention, although the first (the clarification of the way of the righteous) necessarily follows from it, because repelling corruptions (mafasid) is more important.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 56:

(p-132) Since the aim of their request, in asking for the poor to be driven away, was to follow their own desires, God, exalted is He, commanded him to tell them that he is separated from them, after He had made clear to him, by manifest explanation, the evil end of their path, a separation that makes it impossible for them to follow their desires, and this is separation in religion. So He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden﴾, that is, by the One to whom all command belongs, ﴿to worship those whom you invoke﴾, that is, whom you worship, basing this on your own whim and blind imitation (taqlid) in the greatest of the foundations of religion, and [He belittled their affair and] showed how low their rank is by His saying: ﴿besides Allah﴾, that is, the One above whom there is nothing greater. Thus you have abandoned the Greatest, and clung to the lowly, which is below you, in the greatest ignorance, which indicates blindness of the heart together with disbelief in the Benefactor. So my separation from you is founded on severance, so how can you hope for my following you! Then he confirmed this with another matter indicating that they have no excuse in their worship, so He said: ﴿Say: I will not follow your desires﴾, that is, in place of what I am upon of the perfect wisdom, supported by radiant proofs and decisive evidences.

Since it is known that desire does not lead to guidance, but rather to the utmost destruction, He verified what this sentence conveyed by His saying: ﴿Then I would have indeed gone astray﴾, that is, if I followed your desires. Since the one who has strayed may return, He made clear that this is not so, because of their deep-rootedness in error, and He said, expressing it with a nominal sentence which indicates permanence: (p-133) ﴿And I am not among the guided﴾, that is, at that time, possessing any part of guidance, so that I would be counted ﴿among the guided﴾.

Then He reinforced this for those whose hearts had grown in harshness, explaining the grave consequence of other than it, so He said: ﴿Say: If I had what you are hastening for﴾, that is, supposing it were so, ﴿of punishment﴾, that is, of the punishment, ﴿it would have been decided﴾, and He made the verb passive because what is feared is only the destruction itself, not who causes it from a specific person. ﴿The matter would be settled between me and you﴾, that is, I would have destroyed whoever opposed me, out of anger for my Lord because of the arrogance toward Him that had become apparent to me from him. Among them there may be someone written in the register of the fortunate, but the matter was not in my hands, because I do not know the wrongdoer in the sight of God apart from others; so the matter belongs to God alone, for He knows best the fair-minded and so He saves them. ﴿And God﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, ﴿knows best the wrongdoers﴾, that is, those written in the register of the oppressors, so He destroys them.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 59:**
