Then He joined to it the clarification of what they were guided to, as an exhortation to us to give thanks for what He has added to us of His bounty, so He said: ﴿and We guided them﴾, meaning: by what preceded of guidance, ﴿to a straight path﴾. As for the straight path, We singled you out for it and established you upon it, so recognise Our blessing upon you and remember Our preference for you.

Since the phrasing might give the impression of a deficiency in it (the indefinite form), he says, beginning a new sentence to explain its perfection and to magnify its bounty and generosity: ﴿That﴾, i.e., this guidance, great in rank, ﴿is the guidance of God﴾, i.e., the one comprising all attributes of perfection, ﴿He guides by it﴾, i.e., He creates guidance through it, by means of steadfastness upon it, ﴿whomever He wills of His servants﴾, i.e., whether or not he has a father who teaches him, or has someone who first drives him toward error. Having explained the excellence of guidance and specified its foremost people, he threatens whoever abandons it, whoever he may be. He says, manifesting the might of Divinity through absolute self-sufficiency, and exalting Himself above anything in which another is taken into account, even with the slightest regard: ﴿And if they had associated﴾, i.e., these people whom We have mentioned in praise, as you have heard, and whose special favor from Us we have shown, as you have come to know, ﴿anything of partnership [with God]﴾, while God has safeguarded them from that and established through them the crooked paths and lit with them the darkness of the earth in its length and breadth, ﴿then surely would have become worthless from them﴾, i.e., would have been corrupted and fallen away, ﴿what they used to do﴾, i.e., even if it were in the utmost perfection according to the rules of knowledge.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 89:

He added, in warning against slackness in the journey and deviation from the wrong intention, by His saying: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the people of high rank whom We have mentioned before and whom We informed would have their deeds annulled if they associated partners with God, ﴿to whom We gave the Book﴾, that is, the book that gathers every good. Whoever possesses what it contains of sciences and knowledge rules over the inner hearts, because people love it, so they submit to him inwardly. ﴿And the judgment﴾, that is, the act perfected through knowledge, and from it is the enforcement of the word over outward appearances through authority, even if the inner hearts dislike it. ﴿And prophethood﴾, that is, knowledge adorned with judgment, and it is placing everything in its most fitting place. Thus it encompasses the two preceding ranks. Therefore the prophets used to judge the inner hearts by the knowledge they had, and the outward appearances by the miracles that manifested. Then he linked the magnifying of these [gifts] with magnifying them by the fact that they do not perish. He said, consoling [the Prophet] for the affliction of the critics' attacks upon them and the disregard of the ignorant toward them, and giving hope against what necessarily brings despair from the aversion of most of those invited: ﴿If these disbelieve in them﴾, that is, these great things, ﴿these﴾, that is, the people of Makkah among whom you live, to whom We have given them in the most complete, perfect, highest and most beautiful manner, and you call them to be happy through what it contains of guidance, while they turn away from it. Perhaps the indication in this manner is for belittling them. ﴿Then We have entrusted﴾, that is, by virtue of Our greatness in the past, present and future, ﴿with them a people﴾, that is, people possessing strength to carry out affairs by believing in them and guarding their rights, ﴿who are not﴾, and he placed the prepositional phrase first for emphasis, so he said: ﴿disbelievers in them﴾, that is, concealers of anything of the suns of their proofs that have appeared; and they are the prophets and those who followed them. God has spoken truly, and who is more truthful in statement than God! Among this community there have come righteous scholars and firmly grounded rabbis whom none can count except God.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 90:

Since the purpose of their being mentioned in this manner is, God knows best, that each of them, after being guided, hastened to call to God and to be jealous for His majesty against associating partners with Him, neither prosperity nor adversity distracted any one of them from that, whether it was caused by kingship or by other than kingship, from a king or from other than a king. Rather, they clung to guidance and to calling to it in every state. He said, beginning a new sentence to repeat their praise in a way that impels one to adorn oneself with their qualities, and emphasizing the establishment of prophethood: ﴿Those are they﴾, that is, those of elevated ranks, ﴿whom God guided﴾, that is, the King who possesses the ranks of perfection, the complete guidance. Therefore, he made the statement ﴿So follow their guidance﴾ a consequence of praising them, that is, specifically in the obligations of the mission and other matters. He indicated, by the silent-ha (hā' al-sakt), which is the sign of pausing and is present in all the mushafs, that following them required nothing else. Then he explained guidance by its greatest causes, saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to those you call, as they used to say, something that negates the accusation, purifies the advice, and thus obliges following, except for the one who is wretched: ﴿I do not ask you﴾, that is, O you who are called, ﴿for it﴾, that is, for the calling, ﴿any reward﴾, for the motives for coming to the caller and responding to the guide are strengthened by that. Then he began a new sentence: ﴿It is not﴾, that is, this calling with which I call you ﴿except a reminder﴾, that is, an eloquent reminder of everything needed for the livelihood and the return, ﴿to the worlds﴾, that is, to jinn, humankind and angels, perpetually, whose calling never ends and whose summons never ceases. In the expression "follow" (iqtida') there is an allusion to rebuking the disbelievers of the Arabs, in that they followed those among their forefathers who were not fit to be followed, and abandoned the one whom it is obligatory to follow.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 91:

When He confined the call to remembrance (dhikra), and this was a benefit to them and a kindness to them, [saying that] their obedience does not increase anything in God's dominion and their turning away does not diminish anything of His greatness, because all of that is by His will, He made it a circumstantial clause (hal) concerning them, and said, emphasizing the matter of the Message by denouncing those who deny it and by holding them to what they themselves acknowledge: as for the People of the Book, it is by certain knowledge; as for the Arabs, it is by imitation of them; and also because they had entrusted them with knowledge and made them the object of their questions about Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And they did not measure﴾, that is, We said that to them specifically while the situation was that they did not ﴿measure﴾, that is, did not magnify, ﴿God﴾, that is, the One possessing all attributes of perfection, ﴿with the measure due to Him﴾, that is, with the magnification due to Him, in their denial of His remembrance, their turning people away from His good tidings, and their repaying the thanks owed to Him with disbelief toward Him. al-Wahidi said: It is said "qadara al-shay'" when one tests it, estimates it, and wishes to know its measure: yaqduruhu, with a damma, qadran. From this is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «If it is obscured for you, then estimate it (fa-qdurū lahu)», meaning: seek to know it. This is its original meaning in the language. Then it was said of one who knows something: "he measures its measure," and of one who does not know it by its attributes: "he does not measure its measure." ﴿When﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿they said﴾, that is, the Jews. The verse is Medinan, and Quraysh were in accepting their saying; it is possible that it is Meccan, and that their saying was at the time when Quraysh sent to them asking them about him ﷺ concerning the matter of his Message, and arguing against them with the sending of Moses (peace be upon him) and the descent of the Torah upon him: ﴿God has not sent down anything upon a human being﴾, that is, forgetting what He possesses of the attributes of perfection, ﴿upon any human being at all﴾, because whoever attributes to a king of complete dominion that he has not established his commands among his subjects, by what pleases him for them to do and what angers him for them to avoid, has attributed to him a great deficiency; so how much more when that attribution is a lie! Although the one who said this was only some of the worlds, indeed only some of the People of the Book who are some of the worlds, it is ascribed to all of them, because they did not refute its speaker and did not hasten to seize him, as a way of making the matter appear monstrous and magnifying the affair, and to make clear that it is obligatory upon everyone who hears of a sign from the signs of God to strive toward it and learn its matter; then, if he verifies it and someone disparages it, he should restrain his hand with whatever his power reaches, just as he would do if that came from his father or from one of those in whom his pride lies among the sons of this world. In that is the most complete indication that enjoining good and forbidding evil is the pillar of all affairs; whoever neglects it has perished and caused others to perish. al-Wahidi related in Asbab al-Nuzul, without a chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, that the Jews said: "God has not sent down anything upon any human being," so God the Exalted sent down this verse, that is, [this verse]. He said, indicating that the Jews are the ones who say that, and obligating them to acknowledge the lie or to equal the Unlettered (ummiyyin) in holding to desire without a Book, rebuking them, deploring their evil ignorance, their great slander, their severe impudence and their lack of shame: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these fools who have dared to utter this statement without considering its outcome or what follows from it, as a rebuke to them and as a demand that they stand upon the point of their ignorance: ﴿Who sent down the Book﴾, that is, the one that gathers the rulings and admonitions and the good of this world and the Hereafter, ﴿which Moses brought﴾, that is, which you claim to hold to its law, the Book being ﴿a light﴾, that is, possessing a light by which one can take guidance, by placing things in their exact place, ﴿and a guidance for the people﴾, that is, possessing guidance for all of them. As for that time, it is by adhering to it; and as for the descent of the Gospel, it is by acting on what it guided to by following it; and likewise at the descent of the Qur'an. It has thus become clear that it is a guidance in every age, sometimes by calling to what is in it and sometimes by calling to other than it. Then He explained that they concealed from it what is explicit and clear in calling to other than it, out of their following of desire and their adherence to blindness, so He said: ﴿You make it﴾, that is, O Jews, ﴿into pages﴾, that is, scattered sheets, so that you may be able thereby to conceal what you wish, ﴿which you display﴾, that is, you show them to the people, ﴿and conceal much﴾, that is, of them, that by which you intend to alter the religion. This is according to the reading of the group with the second person; according to the reading of Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr with the third person, it is an iltifat indicating intense anger, pointing out that what they said is deserving of being ashamed to mention, so how much more their doing it! Then He turned to them to increase their rebuke, informing them that they are equal to the rest of mankind in the basic natural disposition; rather, the Arabs are purer than them and sounder in understanding. Had Moses (peace be upon him) not brought what he brought, they would not have surpassed them in understanding nor added to them in knowledge. So He said: ﴿And you were taught﴾, that is, O Jews, through the Book that was sent down to Moses, ﴿what you did not know, you﴾, that is, O Jews of this age, ﴿nor your fathers﴾, that is, the earlier ones who were more knowledgeable than you.

Since they had reached, in this statement, a degree of enormous ignorance, He said, pointing to their obstinacy: ﴿Say﴾, that is, you, in answer to this question, without awaiting their reply, for they are the most stubborn and insolent of people, ﴿God﴾, that is, the One who sent down that Book; ﴿then﴾, after you say that, do not listen to them at all, but ﴿leave them in their plunging﴾, that is, their speech and their actions, which are fixed upon ignorance and founded upon their being in the darkness of error, like one wading in water, doing what they do not know, ﴿playing﴾, that is, doing the act of one who plays, which brings them no benefit and averts no harm from them, along with the wasting of time.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 92:

When He—glorified is He—established that it is He who sent down the Torah and the Gospel, as a completion of the proof of the Message through the knowledge of the Jews, as opposed to those who have no Scripture, He followed that with His words, to confirm and affirm its establishment: ﴿And this﴾, that is, the Qur'an, which is now present in all minds, ﴿is a Book﴾, that is, one that gathers the good of both abodes. The context called for saying "God sent down," but He used the plural of majesty (nun al-'azamah), because it is more indicative of His glorification, and so He said: ﴿We have sent it down﴾, that is, it is not from Muhammad ﷺ (p-188) of his own self; rather, it is by Our sending it down to him and Our dispatching him with it. ﴿Blessed﴾, that is, abundant in good and firm in its matter, such that none of creation can deny it because of its inimitability, so that the People of the Book in particular may know its reality by its confirming their Book, because it is ﴿confirming that which is before it﴾, that is, all of it from their books and others, so that they would be more worthy of believing in it; and so that all the people of the earth in general may know that through that and through its inimitability. ﴿And that you may warn﴾, that is, by it, ﴿the Mother of Cities﴾, that is, Mecca, because it is the greatest of cities by virtue of its excellences. ﴿And those around it﴾, from among those who do not believe in the Hereafter—so they do not believe in it—from the people of the whole earth, from all lands and towns, because it is the mother of all of them, and they are heedless in their misguidance. ﴿And those who believe in the Hereafter﴾, that is, among them there is a readiness to believe in it as it is, from the people of the Mother of Cities and those around it, who spread every good ﴿believe in it﴾, that is, in the Book, in actuality, because belief in the Hereafter calls to every good through fear and hope, while disbelief in it drives to every evil.

When the description of the hypocrites with laziness regarding the prayer was repeated, He made preserving it a sign of faith, and so He said: ﴿And they are over their prayer they guard﴾, that is, they preserve it with utmost preservation. So the verse is of the wonderful art of al-ihtibak (interlocking ellipsis): mentioning the warning and the "Mother" first indicates their omission in the second part, and mentioning faith and prayer second is evidence of their negation in the first part.

(p-189) Since their statement, ﴿Allah did not send down anything to a human being﴾ [al-An'am: 91], was plainly a lie and implied the denial of the Messenger (ﷺ), God forbid that it should be said of him (ﷺ), the Jews did this in action and the Quraysh by their approval, and some of the disbelievers claimed that revelation had come to themselves, intending to attack the Qur'an, God the Exalted said, magnifying the matter of lying, especially lying against Him, and especially in the matter of revelation. It is connected to what was said in ﴿Say, "Who sent down...﴾ [al-An'am: 91], nullifying prophethood after establishing the affair of the message and affirming it beyond any doubt. So the proofs of its affirmation were also proofs that prophethood is void and that its claimant is a liar: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who invents against Allah a lie﴾, meaning by action, like the Jews, or by approval, like the Quraysh, ﴿against Allah a lie﴾, meaning any lie whatsoever, let alone denying that anything was sent down to a human being, ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me," while nothing has been revealed to him﴾, meaning, while in fact nothing has been revealed to him. This is a general threat, in keeping with the manner of the glorious Qur'an, and it includes everyone who is characterized by any of that, such as Musaylima, al-Aswad al-'Ansi, and others. Then I saw in the book *Ghayat al-Maqsud fi al-Radd 'ala al-Nasara wa al-Yahud* (The Aim of Intent in Refuting the Christians and the Jews) by Samaw'al ibn Yahya al-Maghribi, who was one of their most eminent scholars around the year five hundred and sixty (AH), and then Allah guided him to Islam, and he had a far-reaching skill in arithmetic, geometry, medicine, and other sciences, that after his Islam he exposed their scandals, (p-190) that the Rabbanites among them claimed that Allah used to reveal to all of them several times every day. Then he said, after dividing them into Qara'in (Karaites) and Rabbaniyyun (Rabbanites), that the Rabbaniyyun are the more numerous, and he said: "They are those who claim that Allah used to address them concerning every matter with what is correct." He said: "This sect is the most hostile of the Jews toward other nations." ﴿And who says, "I will send down"﴾, meaning with a promise that admits no failure, ﴿the like of what Allah has sent down﴾, like al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and others of his kind.

Since the answer is certain for every fair-minded person, that no one is more unjust than him, indeed they are the most unjust of the wrongdoers, it is as if it were said: "If you could see them when the requital of this injustice has befallen them, such as their faces blackened while they are dragged on their faces in chains, and Hell almost bursting apart with rage against them, and they crushed by regret and anguish, and bewildered by grief and perplexity, you would see a matter whose sight is terrifying; how then will its taste and its reality be!" So He followed it with what is nearer to it, saying, as an explanation of that general threat, highlighting the attribute that led them to that instead of their pronoun: ﴿And if you could see﴾, meaning there would be a sight from you of what is lesser than that, ﴿when the wrongdoers﴾, meaning for the sake of injustice in general, so how about what has been mentioned of it! The "al" here is for the genus, which these people enter first and foremost, ﴿in the agonies of death﴾, meaning its hardships, which have overwhelmed them, just as the deep sea overwhelms one who drowns in it, so it lifts him, lowers him, swallows him, and spits him out, and he has no escape from it (p-191), ﴿while the angels﴾, meaning those who asked, out of their ignorance, that some of them be sent down to them in visible form, while We informed them that they do not descend except to decide matters and accomplish what is decreed, ﴿stretch out their hands﴾, meaning toward them with harm, to extract their souls and draw them out complete from their bodies, as a branched iron skewer is drawn out of wet, tangled wool; it is not difficult for them to separate the souls from the body, and nothing of them is hidden from them in any part of it, saying, to terrify them and to depict the violence and severity in the driving, and the insistence and vigor in the taking of life, without any respite or delay, and that they treat them like a relentless creditor who presses and pursues: ﴿Bring forth your souls﴾. It is as if they said: "Why, O messengers of our Lord?" So they said: ﴿Today﴾, meaning this very hour, and it seems they expressed it with "today" to depict the length of the punishment, ﴿you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation﴾, meaning the punishment that combines grievous pain, severe disgrace, and lasting shame, through the extraction, the agonies of death, and what follows it in the barzakh, without any end, ﴿for what you used to say﴾, meaning you would constantly renew the saying, ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning the One to whom belongs all greatness, ﴿other than the truth﴾, meaning other than a saying firmly established to the utmost degree of stability. Had He said "falsehood" instead of it, this meaning would not have been conveyed; had He said "the falsehood," it would have fallen even shorter of the meaning. What benefits here has already passed in al-Ma'idah. When you consider that the context concerns the foundations of religion, the intended meaning becomes even clearer. ﴿And you used to﴾, meaning and because you used to, ﴿be arrogant toward His signs﴾ (p-192), meaning you sought arrogance in order to transgress beyond them. Whoever is arrogant toward a single sign is arrogant toward all of them. That is, if you saw that, you would see a dreadful matter and a monstrous, appalling state. He expressed it with the present tense to depict their state.

When they denied that the dead perceive anything after death or understand speech, and the implied meaning, as the context indicates, was: "Then the angels will take their souls, and no one can prevent them. Then He will say to them: 'You have seen Our angels, of whom We informed you at the beginning of the surah, that when they appear the decree is decisive, the command is final and absolute, with no delay,'" He followed this with His saying, pointing to what was the cause of their arrogance, namely gathering around misguidance and piety with wealth: ﴿And you have indeed come to Us﴾, that is, because of the greatness We possess, through death, which indicates with certainty the comprehensiveness of Our knowledge and the completeness of Our power. The completeness of this greatness, and that the intended meaning is their coming through death, is shown by His saying: ﴿alone﴾, that is, scattered, none of you with anyone else, and each standing alone, separated from everything that prevented you from following Our messengers. ﴿As We created you the first time﴾, that is, with that same greatness by which We caused you to die, in aloneness, weakness and poverty. So where is the group you used to be arrogant about? ﴿And you have left behind what We bestowed upon you﴾, that is, what We made you possess of wealth and enabled you to manage, as a blessing upon you, so that you might reach Our pleasure through it. You thought it belonged to you by right, and you turned away from Us and replaced what indicated Our greatness with its opposite, mocking Our commands. ﴿Behind your backs﴾. So what they used to be arrogant about did not avail them.

When they counted the idols as gods and hoped for their intercession, whether mockingly, or in this world, or in the Hereafter (on the assumption of accepting the validity of resurrection), He said, mocking them and ridiculing their state: ﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors﴾, that is, those about whom you used to say what you said, ﴿whom you claimed﴾, that is, falsely, audaciously and wickedly, ﴿were partners in you﴾, that is, that they had a share with God, so that you worshipped them in times of ease and called upon Him in times of hardship. Show them to us. Perhaps some concealer has hidden them from us, or some barrier has screened them from us. Then He indicated their bewilderment at this awful, terrifying speech, through their confusion, helplessness, astonishment and humiliation, in His saying: ﴿Indeed, [your ties] have been cut﴾, that is, a severing of great extent.

Since mention of "al-bayn" (the between, the space separating things) indicates its nearness in general and its presence even if only in the mind, for one says "between me and such-and-such" and "so-and-so was between us," and similar expressions that indicate presence, He said, alerting to the removal of all of that, even to the point of passing through the mind or occurring to the thought due to intense preoccupation: ﴿between you﴾. He thus attributed the emphatic severing to the "between," and when the "between" is severed, whatever was in it of the causes that used to create connection is also severed, so no one among them retains any connection with another, because what lay between them became like a trench once the "between" itself was cut off, so that reaching one another became impossible. This is according to the reading of the majority (qira'a, a canonical recitation) with the nominative (raf'). This example is the meaning of the reading of Nafi', al-Kisa'i and Hafs from 'Asim with the accusative (nasb) as an adverb of place (zarfiyya, adverbial of place). When the meaning returned to the severing of the connection, He stated the cause of that, which is the disappearance of the support on which they used to rely, saying: ﴿And there has vanished from you﴾, that is, gone away and become void, ﴿what you used to claim﴾, that is, all of those falsehoods.

The Oneness of God, prophethood, and messengership were established, along with some of their proofs. The discourse reached the point where the majesty of God's station became manifest, the veil of wisdom was lifted, and the effect of His Word became evident. The listener was therefore prepared to reflect on it, and his understanding was free to ponder it. So He said, pointing to it and indicating it, making known that what has preceded has produced and manifested it, and will inevitably bring it forth. He reminds of His signs with ﴿Those who believe in the Hereafter﴾ (6:92) and of the argument of Ibrahim (peace be upon him). He varies the proofs of Oneness mentioned at the beginning of the surah in other aspects, informing that the proofs of His majesty exceed the number of the sands, and alerting that the primary aim is knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, through His essence and attributes. ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all the attributes of perfection, is capable of everything He wills. ﴿Splitter of the grain﴾, that is, its originator and the one who splits it open for crops and plants. He expressed it this way because a thing before its existence was nonexistent, and the intellect imagines and supposes from non-existence a continuous darkness. [p. 195] When it emerges from pure non-existence and absolute annihilation, it is as if, in imagination and supposition, it has split that non-existence. ﴿And the date-stone﴾, that is, what lies inside edible fruits such as dates, and which is not intended for its own sake, by splitting it from the trees. In this are wisdoms and secrets too subtle for thoughts, and they indicate the perfection of the Chooser, the One. Imam al-Razi said, in substance: the date-stone and the grain remain in moist earth for a period, and Allah produces in them a split at their top and another at their bottom. A tree rises from the top, growing upward, and another tree descends from the bottom into the depths of the earth, which are the roots. That grain or stone is the connecting cause between the two trees, the ascending and the descending. Sense and reason testify that the nature of the ascending and the descending is opposite. This is not by necessity of nature and property, but by origination, invention, formation, and innovation. There is no doubt that the descending roots are of extreme fineness and delicacy, such that if rubbed with the hand with the slightest force they become like water, yet they are able to penetrate hard earth, into which a needle or a sharp knife cannot penetrate except with great force. The occurrence of this penetration by these subtle bodies is certainly due only to the power of the Chooser who acts by will. This is especially so when you consider the emergence of a tree from a small seed, and then how the tree gathers different natures in its bark, then in what lies beneath it of the substance of the wood, and in the center of the wood's circumference there is a weak substance like carded wool. Then from its trunk its branches are generated, and from the branches its leaves [p. 196], first, then its blossoms and flowers, second, then the fruit, third. Then the fruit may have four kinds of coverings, such as the walnut and the almond: its outer covering is that green substance, beneath it is the covering that is like wood, beneath it is the covering that is like a thin membrane surrounding the kernel, and beneath it is the kernel, which contains a dense substance that is also like a shell, and a subtle substance which is the blossom, and this is the primary aim. Thus the generation of these different bodies in nature, quality, color, shape, and taste, together with the equal influence of natures, stars, elements, and the four seasons, indicates a Powerful Chooser, through the diversity of its fruit. Sometimes the four natures are combined in a single fruit, such as the citron, whose peel is hot and dry and whose pulp is hot and dry. Likewise the grape: its skin and its seed are dry, hot, and moist, yet you find their conditions differ. Some have their kernel inside and their skin outside, like the walnut and the almond. Some have what is sought on the outside and their wood inside, like the peach and the apricot. Some have no kernel in their stones, like the date. Some are wholly desirable, like the fig. The differing of these natures and conditions, these opposing states and mutually repellent properties, even within a single seed, is not from nature but from the One who chooses. Grains differ in colors, shapes, and forms. The shape of wheat is like a half-cone, the shape of barley like two cones joined at their bases, and the shape of chickpea is of another form. He, glory be to Him, deposited in each type of them a property and benefit different from the other. A fruit may be food for one animal and poison for another. This difference, despite the unity of natures and the influence of the stars, indicates that these were produced by the Chooser who acts by will. Furthermore, you find in the leaf of a tree a straight line in its middle, whose relation to that leaf is like the relation of the spinal cord to the human body, from which different threads branch off, and from each of them other threads finer than the first, and it continues in this manner until the threads escape sense and sight, just as many nerves branch from the spinal cord to the right and left in the body, and then from each branch further branches separate, and it continues to become finer until it is too subtle for the senses. He, glory be to Him, did this in the leaf so that the aforementioned powers in the substance of that leaf would be strong enough to draw the subtle earthly particles through those narrow channels. This teaches you that His care, glory be to Him, in creating the whole tree is most perfect. His care in forming the whole of plant life is most perfect. And He created the whole of plant life for the benefit of animals, so His care in creating animals is most perfect. The purpose of creating the whole of animal life is the human being, so His care in creating him is most perfect. He, glory be to Him, created animals and plants in this world only so that they might be food and medicine for the human being according to his body. The purpose of his body is the preservation of its composition for the sake of knowledge, love, and worship. So your way is to look at the leaf of the tree and reflect upon those strings, then ascend from them to the apex of the creation of the tree, and then to what is above it, degree by degree, so that you know that the final purpose of them is the attainment of knowledge and love in human souls. At that point a door of unveilings without end will open for you, and it will become clear to you that the blessings of Allah in your creation are unlimited.

﴿And if you were to count the blessings of Allah, you could not enumerate them﴾ (14:34). And Allah is the Guide.

[p. 198] Since their splitting of the grain and the date-stone from plants is of the kind of giving life, because of the growth in them, He explained and clarified the meaning of splitting, indicating care for it time after time, with His saying: ﴿He brings forth﴾, that is, in a manner of continual renewal and persistence, establishing the matter of resurrection, ﴿the living﴾, that is, like the star, the tree, the bird, and the animal, ﴿from the dead﴾, from the grain, the date-stone, the egg, and the drops of sperm. So how can you deny His power to resurrect? When its meaning was revealed and its purpose made clear through the bringing forth of things from their opposites, lest it be imagined, if He brought forth nothing but its like, that the agent is nature and property, He joined to "Splitter" for further clarification His saying, expressed with the active participle which indicates permanence, since they have no dispute about it, so there was no need to express it with the verb which indicates renewal: ﴿and Bringer-forth of the dead﴾, that is, from the grain and what is with it, ﴿from the living﴾, that is, from the star and what is with it.

When these attributes, for which no one other than Him has any power whatsoever over any of them, were established for Him, glory be to Him, He said, alerting them to their error in associating partners with Him, making known that every partner must be equal to his partner in some respect of the matter in which he is associated, and that there is nothing equal to Him, glory be to Him and exalted, in anything at all, so He has no partner in any way: ﴿That is﴾, that is, the One of exalted ranks, unassailable in His heights, ﴿Allah﴾, that is, the One who unites all the attributes of perfection alone, so divinity is due to none but Him. And since this was the meaning of the discourse [p. 199], He based upon it His saying: ﴿So how are you deluded?﴾, that is, how, and from what direction, ﴿are you turned away?﴾, that is, diverted and turned from what it is fitting to believe.

When He, glorified and exalted be He, described His sacred Self as the Splitter of the grain and the seed, with what necessarily entails His attributes of perfection, and placed it first because it is among the clearest proofs of His power to resurrect, which is the method of this surah, together with the familiarity that comes from its nearness and its constant presence, He followed it with what is similar to it in indicating the giving of life, though it is heavenly in its meanings. This explains what Abraham (peace be upon him) pointed to in his argument with his people, namely the nullification of the divinity of the light, the darkness, and the stars, which are the source of all of these. So He said, elevating the discourse from the lower world to the higher world: ﴿Splitter of the dawn﴾, meaning its Originator. Its literal sense is: the Splitter of the darkness of the night from the morning. But because this usage became common and free from ambiguity, the verb was attributed to the dawn itself, as one says: "the dawn broke" (infajara al-subh) and "the night broke away from it" (infajara 'anhu al-layl). It is also possible that the splitting (al-falq) is meant as uncovering, because it uncovers what was hidden within the split object. Thus the effect, which is manifestation, is expressed by its cause, which is splitting. The dawn is expressed in this form, which is described as "the entrance into the morning" (al-madkhul fi al-subh), so that it can convey the meaning of splitting the stillness by light or other means from the activity that follows upon entering the morning. This indicates that the One who makes the dawn an activity is the One who makes the night a cessation (sadl al-layl). ﴿And He made the night﴾ by what occurs from its darkening ﴿a stillness (sakan)﴾, in which and toward which people rest and find repose. Thus the verse is an instance of ihtibak (a figure in which something is omitted from each of two parallel parts and indicated by the other). It omits the activity (haraka) from the first part and indicates it by the stillness (sakan) in the second, and it omits the cessation (sadl) from the second part and indicates it by the splitting (falq) in the first. This splitting is among the greatest proofs of His power, glorified be He, and it contains two indications. The dawn includes both the false dawn (al-fajr al-kadhib) and the true dawn (al-fajr al-sadiq). The first is stronger in indication, because when the center of the sun reaches the circle of midnight, the place for which that circle is the horizon sees the sun rise from its east. The light then illuminates in that place half of the globe of the earth, so that light occurs in the eastern quarter of your town. That light spreads and disperses throughout the whole atmosphere, and it must strengthen moment by moment. Had the first light come from the disk of the sun, it would have been impossible for it to be a long line. Rather, it would have had to spread across the horizon, dispersing and increasing moment by moment. But it is not so. It appears like a white thread rising upward, to the point that the Arabs likened it to the tail of a wolf (dhanab al-sirhan). Then there follows a pure darkness. Then comes the second, the true dawn, which spreads. Therefore the first is more indicative of power, because it is created by God from the beginning, as a reminder that the lights have no existence except through His origination, and the darknesses have no permanence except through His determination.

When He mentioned the brightness and the darkness, He mentioned their source and joined to it their companion. He said, coordinating with the place (mahall) of "the night," because "jā'il" (making) does not mean only "making bright," so that the annexation would be literal. Rather, what is meant is its continuance through all times: ﴿and the sun﴾, meaning that from which each of the two arises. This one arises from its setting, and that one from its rising. (p-201) ﴿and the moon﴾, meaning the one which is the sign of the night. ﴿as a reckoning (husban)﴾, meaning possessing a reckoning, and a sign by which it is known. The reckoning is known through their cycle and their movement. By means of this, He, glorified be He, arranged the interests of the world into the four seasons, so that from this comes what people need of ripening fruits and the production of crops. He expressed the two by a verbal noun (masdar) built on this eloquent form, indicating that reckoning by them is a great matter, of vast benefit and wide application, together with the worldly benefit it has within the matters of religion. Its greatest benefit is that for which obligation was laid. As if, since the matter is so, that is the reality of the two, by which they are referred to. As for their other benefits, the servants have no part in them.

Since this was a wondrous matter and an overpowering attribute, He pointed to it with the demonstrative of distance and said: ﴿That﴾, meaning this great decree which has preceded, namely the splitting and what follows it, ﴿is the decree of the Almighty (al-'Aziz)﴾, meaning the One whom none can overcome. He is the One who subdued them both in accordance with what He set them in motion to do, and overcame the servants in what He ordained for them through them. If anyone wished to make sleep into wakefulness and wakefulness into sleep, or to make the place of rest into motion or the reverse, or anything else the verse indicates, it would overwhelm him. ﴿the All-Knowing (al-'Alim)﴾, meaning the One who made that by His knowledge upon a path that does not change and a straight balance that does not deviate.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 97:

When he had mentioned that, he followed it with another benefit that encompasses both of them along with others, clarifying what was permitted concerning the knowledge of the stars (ʿilm al-nujūm) and its benefits. So he said: ﴿And He is the One who~﴾, meaning, not anyone else, ﴿who has made~﴾. And since concern for us is greater, he placed first his words: ﴿for you the stars~﴾, meaning all of them, both those that move and those that are fixed, even if your knowledge falls short of all of them, just as it falls short of firm mastery and attainment of the knowledge of the course of the wandering stars (al-sayyāra) from among them, ﴿that you may be guided~﴾, meaning, that you may burden yourselves with the knowledge of guidance ﴿by them~﴾, so that you may know the qibla, the times of the prayers and fasting, and other benefits for your worldly and religious affairs.

Since the earth and water have in themselves nothing but darkness, and the darkness of the night is added to that, He said: ﴿in the darkness of the land~﴾, meaning, the land in which there is no knowledge, even though it has landmarks, since these may be hidden, ﴿and the sea~﴾, for there is no knowledge of it. The attribution to the two (i.e., "darkness of the land and the sea") is for association (al-mulābasa), or it is a comparison of what obscures the paths and other things to darkness. The hafiz Abū Bakr al-Khaṭīb al-Baghdādī narrated in a part (juzʾ) he compiled on the stars, through the chain of Aḥmad ibn Sahl al-Ushnānī, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Learn from the stars what you are guided by in the land and the sea, then stop. And learn from lineages what you connect your kin by, and know what is lawful and unlawful for you regarding women, then stop."

In it also, through the chain of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Imām Aḥmad in his additions (zawāʾid) to the Musnad, from ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O ʿAlī! Perfect the ablution even if it is hard upon you, do not eat charity, do not mate donkeys with horses, and do not sit with the people of the stars."

Also in it, from Abū Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), from ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Do not ask about the stars, do not interpret the Qur'an by your own opinion, and do not revile my Companions, for that is pure faith." And from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) "forbade looking into the stars" — he narrated it through many routes; and from ʿĀʾisha (may Allah be pleased with her) the same, identically. And from Ibn Masʿūd (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When my Companions are mentioned, hold back; when the divine decree (qadar) is mentioned, hold back; and when the stars are mentioned, hold back." He narrated it through several routes.

He also transmitted through a chain from Qatādah his interpretation of the Almighty's words: ﴿and rivers and paths~﴾ [al-Naḥl: 15], he said: "paths"; ﴿and landmarks~﴾ [al-Naḥl: 16], he said: "they are the stars." He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, only created these stars for three purposes: He made them an adornment for the sky, He made them a means of guidance, and He made them missiles against the devils. Whoever pursues anything other than that concerning them has erred in his share, spoken on the basis of his own opinion, wasted his portion, and burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of — in a long, good discourse. [This report from Qatādah was transmitted by al-Bukhārī in his Ṣaḥīḥ.]

The author of Kanz al-Yawāqīt fī Istiʿāb al-Mawāqīt said in the introduction to the book: Know that knowledge is of two kinds: some of it is praiseworthy and some of it is blameworthy, and it is not blamed in itself; it is blamed only with respect to people, for three reasons. The first: that it leads to harm, such as the knowledge of sorcery and talismans (al-ṭalsamāt). This is true, since the Qur'an testified to it and to its being a cause of separation between spouses, and the Prophet (ﷺ) was bewitched and became ill because of it, until Jibrīl (peace be upon him) informed him and removed the sorcery from under a stone at the bottom of a well, as occurs in the authentic hadith. Knowing it as knowledge is not blameworthy, but if it is only fit for harming people, it becomes blameworthy, for the means to evil is itself evil.

The second: that it harms its possessor in most cases, like the second category of the knowledge of the stars, the judicial (al-iḥkāmī) kind, which is used to infer events from causes, like a physician's inference from the pulse about the illness that will arise. This is the knowledge of the paths of Allah's custom and practice in His creation. Yet the Law (al-sharʿ) has condemned it and warned against it for three aspects. One: it harms most people, for when it is said, "this matter is due to the movement of the stars," and this settles in the soul of the weak-minded that it is effective, the remembrance of Allah is erased from his heart, for the weak one restricts his view to intermediaries, unlike the firmly grounded scholar, who perceives the sun, the moon and the stars as subjected [to Allah's command]. There is a great difference between one who stops at causes and one who ascends to the Causer of causes. Then he mentioned what amounts to this: the second reason for forbidding it is that it is conjecture that does not reach certainty; the third is that it has no benefit, so it is an immersion in trivialities (fuḍūl). The third reason among those for which some knowledge is blamed is that it is something the minds of most people cannot reach and cannot independently grasp, and it cannot be denied that a knowledge may be harmful to some individuals, just as the meat of birds harms a suckling infant. End.

Abū Dāwūd and Ibn Mājah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever acquires a branch of knowledge from the stars has acquired a branch of sorcery, increasing it as he increases." [The author of the book al-Zīna said at the end of his book, after mentioning augury (ʿiyāfa), divination by omens (zajr), and the like, and most of it will come from him in surah al-Ṣāffāt: "It has been reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: 'Beware of the stars! For they lead to soothsaying (kihāna).'" He said: All these things have a sound basis. Some of them were from the sciences of the prophets, such as the stars, geomancy (al-khaṭṭ), and other things. Were it not for the prophets who attained the knowledge of the stars and knew the courses of the planets through the zodiacal signs, their direct and retrograde motions, and what has been established and verified of computation in this regard beyond any doubt, people would not have been able to grasp it. All of that came by revelation from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to their prophets (peace be upon them). It has been narrated that Idrīs (peace be upon him) was the first to know the stars, and it is reported about geomancy that it was the knowledge of a prophet from among the prophets; had it not been so, people would not have discovered these subtleties or known them.]

When these verses reached a degree of eloquence that rises beyond the capacity of humans, jinn and angels, because they are an attribute of the Most Merciful, they became a source of honor that calls for drawing attention to them. So He said: ﴿We have detailed~﴾, meaning, We have explained with a healing clarity, in accordance with the greatness that is Ours, ﴿the verses~﴾, one after another, in this impregnable style and this lofty example. And since they are so clear as to need no great reflection, He said: ﴿for a people who know~﴾, meaning, they have the capacity for what is incumbent upon them, and they have the aptitude for knowledge, so that they may infer the unseen from the seen by means of them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 6, verse 98:

When He, glorified is He, mentioned some of this dominion (*malakut*) of the earth and the heavens, He followed it, as had passed at the beginning of the surah, with the singular creation that gathers all of the dominion, namely the human being. This shows His complete power over everything He wills, and it refutes, through the disparity between the first origination and the last of the terms (*ajal*), what they had believed about light, darkness, the sun, the moon and others. For none of these has any choice in anything that proceeds from it. Rather, it is subjected and overpowered, as is sensed and well known. So He said: ﴿And He is﴾, that is, none other than He, ﴿the One who produced you﴾, that is, while you are in the utmost variation in height, stature, color, form and other accidents, which He arranged, glorified is He, according to what His wisdom required, ﴿from a single soul﴾. Then He separated from it its mate, then He multiplied you from the two of them.

Since most people in the life of this world [*al-dunya*] act as one who will not perish and will not pass away, and are not on the verge of passing away as long as there remains in them any remnant [of] life, He said: ﴿So there is a settled place﴾, that is, He made it a consequence of that that among you there is one settled upon the earth. This is according to the recitation of Ibn Kathir and Ibn ʿUmar, with the *qaf* kasra, making it an active participle (*ism fa'il*, a noun of agent). The meaning in the recitation of the rest, with the *qaf* fatha, makes it a noun of place (*ism makan*): ﴿And for you on the earth is a settlement and enjoyment for a time﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 24].

Since those in the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection) have had the veil lifted from them, so they are certain of the Hour and are not acting contrary to that, and likewise those in the loins (*sulb*) and the womb (*rahim*), He expressed by what indicates non-permanence, and He said: ﴿And a temporary dwelling﴾, that is, in the loins, or the wombs, or in the belly of the earth. [The variation in each of the two, together with the fact that all are from a single soul, points to the Capable, the Chooser, who alone can reverse nothing of that.] Everything of this is the content of the two verses at the beginning of the surah. He mentioned the morning and the night and what relates to them first, because they precede in creation. Then He followed it with the creation of man, according to the order that passed at the beginning of the surah. He mentioned here that He made that clay a single soul from which He multiplied all of mankind, despite their variation in what was there and in what is other than it.

Since He mentioned this singular, all-gathering creation and detailed it in these wondrous aspects, it was a place where one would expect that attention be drawn to it. So He said: ﴿We have detailed﴾ [al-Anʿam: 97], that is, by Our majesty, ﴿the signs﴾ [al-Anʿam: 97], that is, We have multiplied their clarification in this singular, all-gathering creature, in the stages of creation and the phases of making: at one time by making a human being from dust, at another by bringing the female out of the male, (p-208) and at another by multiplying from the male and female what cannot be encompassed by counting nor gathered by report, from the drop of semen to birth to old age.

Since the production of people from a single soul and their being turned in those highly varied ways is the most subtle and precise craftsmanship, that required reflection, the use of intelligence and careful examination. So He said: ﴿for a people who understand﴾, that is, for those who have the capacity for understanding (*fiqh*) and intelligence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 99:

When he had mentioned the aspects of the sequential origination (al-ibda' al-tafri'i) from these two worlds, and the causes of their subsistence through what the seasons and other things arise from, he followed this with its nearest cause, which is the water from which He made every living thing. So He said, detailing what He had summarized concerning the grain and the date-stone, bringing it in the manner of kindness toward what preceded it of the proofs. For when the proof is presented in the form of kindness and reminds of blessing, its effect on the heart is great. So whoever is occupied with calling people to faith should follow this path, so that he may hold sway over hearts. ﴿And He is the One who sent down﴾, that is, not other than Him, ﴿from the sky﴾, that is, by His power, knowledge and wisdom, ﴿from the sky﴾, that is, the real sky that you know, as the explicit wording indicates, and what resembles it of the masculine (dhukur) of the animals, which is alluded to by way of indication, ﴿water﴾, that is, pouring forth and gushing.

Since the bringing forth of creation from water is of a degree of greatness that cannot be reached, He drew attention to it by shifting to speech in the mode of majesty, and He said: ﴿So We brought forth﴾, that is, by the greatness We possess, to which none can come close, ﴿by it﴾, that is, by the water, ﴿the growth of every thing﴾, varying in their tastes, colors, scents, natures and benefits, though it is one water. So the cause is one and the effects are many and diverse, whether that growth is real, such as the star and the tree, or figurative, such as the female and the male. Then He grounded the real kind of growth on its clear manifestation, saying, indicating majesty: ﴿So We brought forth from it﴾, that is, from the growth, ﴿green﴾, that is, something green, fresh and tender, which is what branches out from the root of the plant that emerges from the grain. Then He increased the explanation of His greatness by saying: ﴿We bring forth﴾, that is, while We are determining to bring forth ﴿from it﴾, that is, from that green, ﴿grain piled up﴾, that is, in the ear of grain, one part resting upon another, [and guarding it from being picked up by birds, after covering it with a husk and with very fine, rough, needle-like awns,] after its origin had been a single seed in its own form, or scattered in the soil after He had developed it, glorified is He, through several stages. Indeed, the One who does this is capable and chooses.

Since attributing the bringing forth and origination exclusively to Him, glorified is He, in the mode of majesty, both specifically and generally, makes it known that all things come from Him, and the matter has reached a degree of clarity worthy of ensuring that nothing is attributed to another, especially those whom they treat and know to be incapable of originating it, He began with what He had begun with first in the verse of the splitting (al-falaq), namely the grain, and then followed with what comes from the date-stone. So He said, expressing that style: ﴿And from the palm trees﴾. Placing the grain before it here and in what precedes indicates that cultivated crops are superior to it, for it is the staple food in most lands and for most animals, [and food is given precedence over fruit]; for the palm was created from the clay of Adam. Then he substituted for what was summarized from that, saying, explaining: ﴿from its spathe﴾, that is, of the palm, which is the first thing that emerges from it within its sheaths, ﴿are clusters﴾, plural of qinw, which is the cluster (idhq) with the kasr vowel for the stalk, and it is the bunch, and al-'urjun is its stem on which the unripe dates are. ﴿Hanging low﴾, that is, near to reach, even if its root is long, by what He taught you and made easy for you of the craft of reaching it.

Since they did not have in treating grapes and other things what they have in treating palm trees, He joined to (plants) while drawing their attention that these, like the palms, are what He, glorified is He, alone originates, [as has passed], so He said: ﴿And gardens﴾, that is, orchards, ﴿of grapes﴾, and He put it in the plural because of the abundance of its kinds. He began with these two trees because of their merit, as has passed, over others, because their fruit is both fruit and staple food. He put the first (palm) first because they are more familiar with it, even though the grape is the most noble of the kinds of fruit. It is benefited from from its first appearance, for [first] it has fine green threads that are sour and delicious, then it becomes unripe grapes (ḥiṣrim), which is a noble food for the healthy and the sick. From it is made grape must (rubb al-ḥiṣrim) and very pleasant drinks beneficial to people of bile, and from it the most delicious sour dishes are cooked. As grapes themselves, it is the most delicious and the most sweet of fruits. It can be stored as grapes for nearly a year, its raisins are food, and from it come date-syrup (dibs), vinegar and other things. The best thing in it is its seed, and from it are made digestive electuaries (jawarishat), of great benefit to a weak, moist stomach. [And He put the palm first because it is the staple food of the Arabs, and between it and humankind there is a resemblance in many properties that are not found in other plants; therefore it came in a hadith: «Honor your paternal aunt, the palm, for it was created from the clay of Adam, peace be upon him, and of the trees none pollinates other than it.» Narrated by Abu Ya'la, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya, and Abu al-Shaykh from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him.] Then He followed these two with what comes after them in excellence, so He said: ﴿And the olive﴾, [and] He put it first because of the abundance of its benefit, and from it is extracted an oil of great benefit for eating, for light, and for all other uses. ﴿And the pomegranate﴾; He concluded with it because of its goodness and its great benefit. It is composed of four things: its peel, its pulp, its seeds and its juice. The first three are cold, dry, earthy, dense, astringent, and very abundant, while the juice is their opposite, and it is the most pleasant and most refined of drinks, closest to balance and most suited to a balanced nature. In it is strengthening for a weak temperament; it is food in one respect and medicine in another.

When He had mentioned the staple foods of fruits, grains, and oils, and the noblest and most general of fruits, and these were most similar to the human being in their origination, resurrection, agreement and difference, and the resemblance of some of them and the difference of others, while they are watered with one water and in one land, indicated the power and choice (of the Creator), and since the context was to establish the oneness (of God) and deny a partner by establishing perfect power, which is denied of others, it is not valid that He should have a partner, for a partner can only be similar to his partner in perfect resemblance in whatever the partnership consists of, and (the context was also) for the resurrection. So the intent was reflection upon their outward forms and their transformations from non-existence into existence and after existence, and to argue against the People of the Book, who are marked with knowledge and attributed to sharpness of minds, and other sects. The form ifta'ala (Form VIII of the verb) comes for emphasis, which is exaggeration in establishing the root of the act and striving to achieve it and effort, so its attainment, when attained, is most complete. He said, making it a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) of everything previously mentioned: ﴿resembling one another﴾, that is, in the utmost resemblance of some to others, so that it is hardly distinguishable. If the fruits of two trees were cut from it, the fruit of one would not be distinguished from the fruit of the other. Thus the negation of interaction (tafā'ul) does not contradict this, for it is merely the sharing of two or more in the root of an act. So it is known that the intended sense is: "both resembling and not resembling." Then, since the one who holds to the doctrine of natures (al-ṭabā'i') might rely on this expression, He negated what might be thought, namely that these things have an effect in making some of them resemble others, so He said: ﴿and not resembling﴾, that is, not seeking resemblance, although there must be some resemblance. So the verse is an instance of al-iḥtibāk (a rhetorical device in which a term is mentioned in one place and its opposite implied, and vice versa): it affirmed resemblance (ishtibāh) as indicating the negation of its opposite, namely non-resemblance, and because ishtibāh is more emphatic than tashābuh, He tied the command to looking, which is the most reliable of the senses, and as an indication that (p-213) the intended meaning is the outward appearance of that, because it was in indicating resurrection and tawhid, which is the context here. So He said: ﴿Look at its fruit﴾. This is unlike the second term, for it is in the context of refuting the Arabs regarding what they attribute of His creation to their idols, which have no power over anything at all. For this reason, He ended the verse with permission for them to eat from it, to end what they used to forbid for themselves, and with a command to give charity to those to whom charity is to be given. As for the inner meaning, which is eating, it will come later. Then He drew attention to generalizing the looking across all its conditions, saying: ﴿when it bears fruit﴾, that is, when it appears from its sheath weak and of little or no benefit, ﴿and its ripening﴾, that is, and look at its ripening when it has ripened and its picking has come. From this one knows to look at what is between these, for it necessitates observing the beginning and the end, so the impossibility of its colors, measures, tastes, shapes and other of its conditions and states becomes known. It also necessitates looking at its trees, so that the variation of some and the resemblance of others in tallness, shortness, smallness, largeness and other states may be known, just as this exists in dates. So the attribution of these changes and transformations is none other than to the Choosing Agent, because its relation to natures and seasons is equal. If they were attributed to them, they would not change.

When the taking of these things mentioned first, and the difference among their shapes, measures and colors second, indicated perfect power, which necessitates oneness, He indicated His greatness by saying, beginning a new clause and using the distal demonstrative with the plural suffix mīm: ﴿Indeed in that﴾ (p-214), that is, in that matter of great significance and high rank, ﴿are signs﴾, that is, indications of the power and choice of the Maker.

Since signs do not benefit those whose wretchedness is intended, He said: ﴿for a people who believe﴾, that is, it is judged that they, by their cleverness, their vigor, and their strength in what they attempt, renew their faith whenever they reflect on the created works of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, which point to Him and indicate Him in every tongue.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 100:

When the polytheists fell into categories, some of them worshipped a number of idols, which they associated with God in worship but not in creation. Among them was Azar, whom Ibrahim (peace be upon him) debated. Among them were the worshippers of the stars, and they were of two groups. Some of them said that the stars are necessarily existent (wajib al-wujud, that which must exist). Others said that they are contingent (mumkin al-wujud, that which may or may not exist), that God created them and entrusted them with the management of this lower world. These are the ones whom the Friend (al-Khalil) debated concerning the setting (of the stars). Among them were those who said that this whole world has two gods: a doer of good and a doer of evil. They said that God and Iblis are brothers. God is the creator of people, animals and livestock, while Iblis is the creator of predators, snakes, scorpions and evils. They call the zanadiqa (heretics, dualists) by this name, and they are the Majus (Magians, Zoroastrians). The book that Zardusht (Zoroaster) claimed had descended from God was called the Zand, so its adherent is called zindi, and then it was Arabized and said to be zindiq. All of this was in connection with His saying (p-215) ﴿Splitter of the dawn﴾ [al-An'am: 96], as an explanation of the verse ﴿Indeed, Allah is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95], indicating the perfection of power that points to His oneness, in order to point to the resurrection. It is most fitting to return to disparaging the state of the polytheists by expressing amazement at them in a circumstantial clause (jumla haliyya) relating to the pronoun in ﴿splitter﴾ [al-An'am: 95] or to something else that has preceded. So He, exalted is He, said, explaining the matter of this category, because the matter of the others had already been mentioned. Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them) said: this verse was revealed concerning the zanadiqa. ﴿And they set up﴾, that is, He, glory be to Him, did this, which leaves no room for doubt regarding His complete knowledge, power, perfect wisdom and oneness, while the one for whose sake He did that was (made) by them ( جَعَلُوا ). He expressed by the greatest Name and placed it first to magnify the notion of equating anything with Him: ﴿for Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom all command belongs.

Since polytheism is at the extreme of atrocity and ugliness, He placed it first, saying ﴿partners﴾, meaning: it was not fitting that He should have any partner at all. This is because when an attribute is mentioned in an unrestricted way, not applied to any particular thing, the negation connected with it is general to everything that could possess that attribute, and the ruling on denial is the ruling of negation. When the hearer was stirred by this placing forward, for the increase of meaning without increase of wording, he longed to know the type of beings that the partners were from. So He explained them by His saying ﴿the jinn﴾, that is, those who are the most daring of existent beings against them and their enemies to them. So they obeyed them as God is obeyed, and this was worship of them and association (with God). You have seen what clarification there is after the completion (of the matter), which is fine for observers. ﴿While He created them﴾, that is, while they know that God created them, that is, decreed them with knowledge and planning, and therefore His creation of them was perfectly firm. ﴿And they invented﴾, that is, the worshippers ﴿for Him sons﴾, that is, like 'Uzayr and al-Masih, ﴿and daughters﴾, that is, from the angels. So they combined for this ignorances that are the extreme of misguidance: describing the angels with femininity, daring against the station of Lordship by (attributing) need, and specifying Him after that with what they would not accept for themselves in any way. The root (kh-r-q) revolves around penetrating, expansion, release and decree without knowledge or understanding, so that corruption results from it. For this reason, one who does not do work well is called kharq, and a woman is called kharqa'. This means that they lied, disagreed and expanded in this false statement, and by this excessive departure they moved far from its reality, like the expansion of one who travels in a kharq, that is, a wide, empty desert, a hollow vast wilderness with distant horizons, to where no human has preceded him, so that he went astray from the road with a straying in which his guidance is not hoped for except after a great distance, and so he became deserving of destruction. To this returns the meaning of what is read in the irregular reading: wa-harrafu (and they distorted), with an unpointed (ḥ) and a fa.

Since their statement had no root in reality or even a plausible basis, and since kharq means decreeing without knowledge, (p-217) this indicated that, [clearly stating what it implied and confirming it], as a notice of the decisive proof in demolishing their statement from its root. That is because it is a claim with no proof, and matters of the fundamentals of religion are not resorted to except with a decisive (qat'i) proof. That is through an indefinite noun in the context of negation, so He said ﴿without knowledge﴾. Then He declared Himself free of what they say, as a notice of what must be said by everyone who hears that, so He said ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, I glorify Him with a glorification fitting to His majesty that it should be attributed to Him. Since the meaning of tasbih (glorification) is distancing from deficiency, and the context requires that He be in exaltation, He stated this explicitly, saying ﴿and exalted is He﴾, that is, the matter of His elevation is distant to a limit that has no limit or end ﴿above what they describe﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 101:

When he concluded with the declaration of His transcendence above what they ascribe to Him of partners and offspring, he argued for that transcendence by the fact that all of them are His creation, and His knowledge encompasses them, and the made thing cannot be like the maker. So He said: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the one who brings them into being. He possesses the attribute of origination (ibda'), that is, the power of innovation (al-ikhtira') is established for Him. Whoever is like this is free of need for procreation (tawlid). Therefore the expression of wonder is apt in His saying: ﴿How can He have a son?﴾, that is, how, and from what direction? He intensified the wonder with His saying: ﴿when He has had no consort﴾, that is, the situation being that He has had no consort, and the situation being that ﴿He created all things﴾, that is, every possible thing within the scope of power, from every consort that might be supposed, every son that might be imagined, and every partner that might be claimed. So how could the Originator be in need of any of that, by way of procreation or otherwise?

Since power is not complete except with the comprehensiveness of knowledge, He said: ﴿And He is﴾, and did not use a pronoun, as an alert that the generality of knowledge admits no specification as creation does, and so He said: ﴿All-Knowing of everything﴾, meaning: He is over everything Powerful, because the comprehensiveness of knowledge entails the perfection of power, as its proof will come—God willing—in (Ta-Ha). Whoever has a son does not have comprehensive knowledge or power, but rather is in need of procreation.

When it was established that He has no equal, by what He mentioned of His attributes and actions, and He exposed the corruption of the views of the polytheists, presented their doctrines in the best manner, and showed the corruption of each one of them with the firmest proofs, thereby confirming what He had opened the surah with, namely His encompassing of the attributes of perfection, He said, indicating all of that by a subject followed by a series of predicates: ﴿That is﴾, meaning the One exalted in attributes to the utmost degree, who has no need of anything while everything is in need of Him. ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses every perfection. ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning the Originator of you and the Bestower upon you of every kind of bounty. This is a summation (fadhlaka) of what preceded it and its fruit, because whoever is described by these attributes is the Lord of all alone [and the Creator of all, and deserving of worship alone]. Therefore He followed this with His saying: ﴿there is no deity except Him﴾, because the context calls for the tawhid (oneness of God) that necessarily follows from encompassing the attributes of perfection, which are the meaning of the praise (hamd) with which the surah opens. He then introduced His saying: ﴿the Creator of all things﴾, which is the starting point of what follows, in the manner of a causal justification (ta'lil), as proof of this. (p. 219) Having established the proof, He made the command to worship consequent upon it, saying: ﴿so worship Him﴾, meaning Him alone, because whoever associates others with Him has not worshipped Him, since He is absolute self-sufficiency (al-ghina al-mutlaq), and one who has absolute self-sufficiency is not fitting to accept a partner. He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿And He is Guardian over all things﴾. And since the context is the negation of His need for anything, He placed ﴿over all things﴾ first, indicating that a son or a partner is needed only by one who is weak and needy, whereas He is the All-Powerful, and everyone besides Him is powerless; He is the Self-Sufficient, and everyone besides Him is poor. How then would the All-Powerful, [the Self-Sufficient,] need the weak and poor? This is not possible, and it should not occur to conjecture. There is also in this an indication that the worshipper should devote himself to His worship and sever his affairs from other than entrusting them to Him, for He suffices him by His grace over whoever else there is.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 103:

Since every father and every partner must necessarily share some resemblance with his offspring and his partner, He connected to this [verse] the One whose description required what the context demanded of His transcendence, so He said: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, meaning: cannot grasp Him with full comprehension (al-ihata). ﴿Vision﴾, meaning: that whoever you have made His offspring or His partner is grasped by your eyes, like Jesus and Ezra, peace be upon them both, and the idols, the stars, darkness and light. As for the angels and the jinn, if your judgment about them is based on direct observation, then they are like those who preceded them; and if it is based on report, then it comes only from the prophets. Each of them informs that they are servants of God like others, and that He is exalted above partner and offspring. Their books and authentic reports of their traditions bear witness to this. Beyond all of that, they are such that they can be grasped by the eyes in general; their perception is not impossible. As for this Mighty God, He is not grasped by you through sight in the way that others are grasped in complete perception. The one who looks at Him considers Him, weighs Him and assesses Him with discernment of what is in Him of pleasure, anger and other [states], as far as insight (firasa) reveals and keen perception (tawassum) clarifies; for He, glorified is He, is too exalted to be encompassed. This is on the basis that it is a universal negation. If it is a negation of universality, the meaning is that He is Mighty, and not everyone sees Him, but rather the elect see Him when He wills, uncovering the veil for them and creating the means for them. ﴿And He﴾, despite that, perceives you, indeed ﴿perceives﴾ what you do not perceive of yourselves, ﴿the vision﴾, which are the faculties deposited in the optic nerve of the eye so that by them visible things are perceived. ﴿And He is the Subtle﴾ beyond being encompassed by vision, because He prevents causes from producing their effects, and brings into existence the most subtle and strangest causes. Therefore it is not strange for Him to perceive meanings, for He is the One who brought them into existence. ﴿Does He not know who created?﴾ [al-Mulk: 14]. The root of subtlety (al-lutf) is fineness of observation of things. ﴿The All-Aware﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses vision; His encompassing of its possessors is then all the more fitting. The meaning of the two names is realised because the meaning is realised. Al-Harali said in his explanation of the names: subtlety (al-lutf) is concealing the route to a thing by displaying what opposes it, and it is not complete except through experience (khibra); for this reason ﴿the All-Aware﴾ is paired with His name. For He concealed His wisdom within an apparent opposite. So subtlety is testing within wisdom, and by His name the Subtle (al-Latif) He established the affair of His wisdom between this world and the Hereafter. By this He established the affair of the people of His guardianship in this world, since He gathered for them what is of His command within it, so their might appears from behind humiliation, and their humiliation appears while might is beyond it; their might precedes to the hearts while they are humbled in the senses, and what is perceived of them returns to might in the outcome of this world and the swiftness of the Hereafter, with hearts at ease with them.

﴿Indeed my Lord is Subtle in what He wills﴾ [Yusuf: 100]. When He willed to make him ruler of Egypt and made the means of that his being kept hidden, and by the realisation of its meaning through complete experience and wisdom, which is the manifestation of a thing in its opposite, the exclusivity of His attribute of truth becomes clear. He is the One who fed [them] from hunger and secured [them] from fear, the One who made for you fire from the green tree. He, exalted is He, is the Subtle, there is no subtle one but Him. Then he said: experience (al-khibra) is the perception of the hidden and concealed aspects of things, such that no hidden matter appears from Him without the perception of the All-Aware having preceded its appearance. That is not complete except for the One who brings it forth, who ﴿brings out the hidden﴾ in the heavens and the earth. The experience of creation necessarily involves an apparent manifestation that indicates the hidden through observation; otherwise experience would not be valid for them, as it was said: a person's experience is in what appears of his speech and what he displays of his deeds day and night. The True All-Aware is the One who is aware of a thing without an apparent manifestation through which the outward perceives the hidden matter; He is in reality the One for whom there is no all-aware except Him. [End.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 104:

When He had multiplied for them the proofs of His oneness, and concluded them with this sensory proof, the meaning of which is that [every partner and every son reaches his partner and his father, while He is exalted above being reached by anyone, that is, above being encompassed by anyone], it was fitting that He admonish them and praise the proofs, urging them to reflect upon them. He placed this on the tongue of His Prophet (ﷺ) as an indication that he, by the light of his heart, the perfection of his intellect, the purity of his mind, the abundance of his knowledge, the nobility of his character, the uprightness of his dispositions, and the remoteness of his aspiration from being attributed to injustice or accused of obstinacy, is worthy of saying, after establishing them and without hesitation, affirming the matter of his call after the affirmation of the lofty divine demands: ﴿Indeed there has come to you﴾.
