And since the signs, by their strength and majesty, which the verb's feminine form ("taddhkīr al-fi'l") alludes to, necessitate knowledge, and thus become a cause for the unveiling of realities, which is like light in the clarity of sensible things, He said: ﴿insights﴾, that is, lights which for your hearts are in the position of visible illumination for your eyes, ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who bestows upon you every kind of goodness, so that no goodness at all belongs in your sight to anyone else. So ascend from looking with the eyes to considering with the insights, and do not descend into the depths of imitation until you reach a limit at which you understand only what is perceived by the eyes; rather, rise up in the zenith of knowledge to the heavens of independent reasoning, and draw the swords of insight against the highwaymen. For if you are content with the base, you harm only yourselves, and if you compete for the lofty, it is they that you benefit. Therefore, he based on this dazzling light and manifest secret His saying: ﴿So whoever sees﴾, that is, acts upon the proofs, ﴿it is for his own self﴾, that is, the benefit of his sight belongs to himself specifically, because he has saved it from the error that leads to ruin; ﴿and whoever is blind﴾, that is, does not get guided by the proofs, ﴿it is against himself﴾, that is, the harm of his blindness falls specifically upon him, because he goes astray and so perishes.

Since the meaning is that there is nothing of his sight for me or for anyone else that would add anything to me, nor is there anything of his blindness against me or anyone else, the implied sense was: "I am only a bearer of good news and a warner." He followed it with His saying ﴿and I am not﴾, and indicated that the right of the human being is humility and submission of tyranny and force to God, by using the particle of elevation, so He said: ﴿over you﴾. He went to the extreme in negation with His saying: ﴿a guardian﴾, that is, I do not lead you compulsorily to what would save you, nor do I forcibly prevent you from what would destroy you.

The discussion of Quran 6:105 on the Quran's "variation" of verses, as it appears in al-Biqa'i's Nazm al-Durar.

Since the sense requires an address to the majestic Presence (maqam al-'azamah), the wording shifts to the first person plural, to inform that all decree is in His hand, lest any deficiency be supposed in the execution of His word. "So look at what We have varied for you in this surah of verses, and what We have made clear through them of noble indications." He has brought in it wondrous variations and uncovered rare definitions. He follows it with His saying: (p. 224) ﴿And thus﴾, that is, and like this great variation, ﴿We vary﴾, that is, We transfer all the ﴿verses﴾ from state to state in their diverse meanings, pursuing through the aspects of proofs what escapes the powers and defeats the capacities, so that the minds of the apostates are bewildered and the thoughts of the obstructors are obliterated, knowing that they are incapable of producing anything approaching them, [so the proof binds them] ﴿and so that they say﴾, out of transgression and not from a manifest incapacity, ﴿"You have studied"﴾, that is, you have learned this from others among the People of the Book or others, until this arrangement became orderly for you and this completeness was achieved for you. Then they would bring a clear falsehood whose flaw is evident, whose secrets are manifest and whose veils are torn away. It is as if they had said: "You brought it from knowledge, while we are ignorant and know nothing." Every person granted success will know that they did not accept this for themselves, despite claiming truthfulness and competing in distance from the attributes of lying, except from extreme bewilderment, the utmost astonishment, and the lack of a damaging argument.

The summary is that He brought it in this strange method and wondrous style so that some people would be blinded from clear evidence while others see, and they are the ones meant by His saying: ﴿and that We may make it clear﴾, that is, the Quran, since it is what is meant by the verses that are heard, ﴿to a people who know﴾, that is, the purpose of thorough clarification is that the ignorant grow in their ignorance, and that whoever is fit for knowledge be guided. So they will not say "you have studied," but will say: "It is from Allah." This verse is of the device of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which a term omitted from one part is supplied by its counterpart in the other): the affirmation of the claim of studying first indicates its negation (p. 225) second, and the affirmation of knowledge second indicates its absence first. It has the same sense as ﴿He leads many astray by it and guides many by it﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:26].

When this had been made clear in the course of the proofs and within the demonstrations, that the Qur'an is a treasure to which no treasure can be compared, and a might that no might can approach, and that it stands at a summit before which the swift flights of thought fall short and beneath whose brilliance the windows of sight are dazzled, and when it concluded that the intended "clarification" (bayan) is the scholars, it was fitting to draw attention to this, lest their accusation cease, with their saying "You have studied" (darasta) and the like. So He said, specifying the address to him ﷺ to inform that he is the knower in truth:

﴿Follow﴾, i.e., you and those who follow you, ﴿what has been revealed to you﴾, i.e., then persist in acting upon it. Then He affirmed its praise by saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you by this clarification. Then He gave the reason for that by saying: ﴿there is no god but Him﴾, i.e., none other deserves to be followed, and no command is to be obeyed, nor is one to turn to anyone for benefit or harm. ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾, i.e., without delivering the message, for nothing is incumbent upon you beyond it; and your excessive eagerness for their faith does not increase those whose wretchedness is willed except in persisting in their polytheism and in being entangled in the snares of their associating.

Since the Beloved (ﷺ) was most pleased by that which his Beloved (Allah) increases him in, He said, consoling him (ﷺ) regarding their mockery of him and their rejection of his words, and linking it to what its implied sense is: "If Allah had willed, they would not have opposed you, nor would they have uttered a word against you": ﴿And had Allah willed, they would not have associated others with Him﴾, meaning: no association at all actually occurred from them. For He willed for you, regarding their falling into [speaking against] you, what He willed for Himself, so let this be a consolation to you in that.

Since the implied sense is: "Surely He, glorified is He, is Watcher over them," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And We have not made you﴾, meaning: by Our majesty, and He indicated that exaltedness belongs to none but Allah, glorified is He, so He said: ﴿a watcher over them﴾, meaning: you guard their deeds, lest among them be anything that does not please Us, so that you would turn them back from it by compulsion. ﴿Nor are you﴾, and He put first what is more general than the negation of achieving the all-encompassing, overpowering exaltedness, which is specific to God, so He said: ﴿a guardian over them﴾, meaning: so that you would take the right from them by force and deal with them according to what they deserve, good or evil. You are only a conveyor of Our message; then the matter of their guidance and their misguidance rests with Us.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 108:

When the repulsion from what they had taken besides Him as rivals (andad) and daughters had gone on at length, because they are less than that and more contemptible, that might perhaps have served as a call to revile them. So He forbade it, because of a great corruption that reviling would bring about. He said, linking it to His words ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾ [al-An'am: 106], not addressing this to him alone (ﷺ), out of honour for him: ﴿And do not revile﴾. Since the idols do not reason, and the polytheists (p-227) claimed that they possessed reason and knowledge and ascribed actions to them, He let the speech proceed according to their claim, because the matter concerns refraining from reviling them. So He said: ﴿those who call upon﴾, meaning, calling upon them in worship, whether the idols or others, by mentioning what deficiency is in them. Then, to remove the supposition that they were being honoured, He clarified that they are in a low state by His words: ﴿other than Allah﴾, meaning the Supreme King, to whom there is no equal in justice, ﴿out of ignorance on your part of what they have of defects. Rather, they turned away from calling upon anything other than Allah, even from reviling their gods with what they deserve. For We have made their deeds appear fair to them, so they wandered astray, despite the abundance of their intellects, in what no sensible person would approve, and they denied all the signs that necessitate faith. Your reviling them may perhaps lead them, because of the zealotry of the Jahiliyyah (jahiliyya) that they hold, to what is unseemly, ﴿so that they revile﴾, meaning, as a consequence they would revile ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One you call upon, who possesses all the attributes of perfection. He made the object explicit to emphasise this, magnify it, make it terrifying, and repel from it.

When haste is required by the sense of urgency, He indicated it, glory be to Him, by His words: ﴿in enmity﴾, meaning, running towards reviling. Since enmity may occur with knowledge, He said, clarifying that it is meant with haste, that it exceeds the bounds: ﴿without knowledge﴾. Because We have made their deeds appear fair to them, when obedience entails the existence of a great evil, one refrains from it even if the situation leads to abandoning it for a time, so that strength may be gained to repel that evil. Thus the ruling of the verse remains in force and is not abrogated (mansukh).

Since that was severe upon the soul and the breast was constrained by it, the situation required that it be said: Is this adornment specific to these criminals, or was there the like of it for other nations? So it was said: ﴿Thus﴾, meaning, rather it was for others as well, for just as We made such adornment appear fair to these, ﴿We made fair for every nation﴾, meaning every great and intended group, ﴿their deeds﴾, meaning the ugly deeds they undertook without knowledge of what He had placed in their hearts of love for it, as a rejection from Us of them after sound reason, to the lowest of the low, until they saw as good what is not good, so that Our power might be made manifest. In this there is the greatest consolation, solace and comfort. The verse is of the type called ihtibak: the mention of ﴿without knowledge﴾ first indicates its omission second, and the mention of adornment second indicates its omission first.

Since He, glory be to Him, is most patient and of great forbearance, and since respite may sometimes come from the ignorance of the sinner's deed, He negated that by His words: ﴿Then﴾, meaning after a long respite, ﴿to their Lord﴾, meaning the One who does good to them through forbearance towards them, while they strengthen themselves by His blessings in disobedience to Him, and to no other, ﴿is their return﴾, meaning by the Great Gathering, ﴿and He will inform them﴾, meaning He will inform them with a great and eloquent informing, ﴿of what﴾, meaning of all that ﴿they used to do﴾, meaning in a manner of constant renewal and continuance, by what is in their natures of the impulse towards it [even if they claimed that they were acting according to the requirement of knowledge].

(p-229) When He (glory be to Him) set forth these proofs in these clear verses, and concluded them with what He knew of them, namely their haste to revile the One who had done good to them, by bringing them into existence and bringing into existence for them everything in the cosmos, and there is no blessing upon them except that it comes from Him, He marvelled at them regarding their promise to believe, with emphasis, should there come to them what they proposed, informing that this is among what their deeds had made attractive to them. It is a false wish and an oath that is broken. So He said, joining it by conjunction to ﴿And they made for God partners, the jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 100]: ﴿And they swore﴾, that is, the polytheists, ﴿by God﴾, that is, the One than whom there is none greater, ﴿with their most solemn oaths﴾, that is, exerting their utmost effort in them, to the point that it is as though the oaths themselves were striving. He prepared for the oath, saying: ﴿If there came to them a sign﴾, that is, of what they proposed, and He followed the oath with His words: ﴿they would surely believe in it﴾.

Since they were wrongdoers in this respect, because they asked the Messenger for what was not in his power after his coming with miracles that removed their excuses and made following him obligatory for them, He drew attention to this by His words, resuming: ﴿Say﴾, that is, in rejection of their obstinacy: ﴿Signs are only with God﴾, that is, this kind of thing is with God, the One possessing all attributes of perfection, and neither is it in my power nor in the power of anyone else to produce anything of this kind, so that the proposal would yield nothing but His anger.

Since the servant, by reason of his incapacity, has no power over anything at all, it is not valid for him to pass judgment on a thing that has not come about at all, neither by his own actions nor by the actions of others. He said, disapproving of them and turning to address them directly, indicating that they deserve to be confronted with reproach: ﴿And what﴾, that is, and what thing ﴿makes you aware﴾, that is, gives you the least awareness ﴿of what you swore to, of belief, when it comes﴾, such that they could conceive of it even the slightest conception, let alone supposition, let alone certainty, especially in this manner! Then he gave the reason for the interrogative by His words, explaining that there is no benefit in bringing the proposed sign: ﴿That they﴾, with the fath reading of Nafi', Ibn 'Amir, Shu'bah in one narration from him, Hafs, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i, so it is as though it were said: "I reject it for you, because ﴿when it comes they will not believe﴾", with the address form in the reading of Ibn 'Amir and Hamzah, and the shift to the third person in the reading of the others, to inform that they are far from belief, so they are deserving of being turned away from, for what they merited of anger. The reasoning is clear according to the one who read "inna" with a kasra.

Since the sense is: "Indeed We set a seal upon their hearts, and We make their evil deeds seem fair to them," He followed it with His words: ﴿And We turn about﴾, that is, by the greatness We possess, ﴿their hearts﴾, that is, their minds, so that they do not find guidance through them, ﴿and their sight﴾, so that sight does not benefit them through it, and so they do not take heed and do not believe, ﴿just as they did not believe in it﴾, that is, in the like of that, ﴿the first time﴾, that is, when the signs that came before those came, ﴿and We leave them﴾, that is, We abandon them, ﴿in their transgression﴾, that is, their exceeding of the limits, ﴿wandering blindly﴾, that is, they perpetuate bewilderment, even though the situation, by reason of the evidence in it, does not call for bewilderment in any way.

When He had informed that they would not believe at the coming of a sign they had demanded, He generalized in a detailed manner to clarify what preceded it, saying: (p-231)﴿And even if We had sent down﴾, that is, with Our supreme greatness, which the plural of the "nun" forms point to, ﴿to them the angels﴾, that is, all of them, so that they saw them face to face, ﴿and the dead had spoken to them﴾, that is, likewise, ﴿and We had gathered against them﴾, that is, [with what We possess] of greatness, ﴿every thing in front of them﴾. "Qubulan" is the plural of "qabil," which is the plural of "qabila" [in the reading of the one who vowels the qaf and the ba' as in "raghif" and "rughuf"], meaning: all that gathered would come to them tribe by tribe [tribe by tribe], in succession and face to face. ﴿They would not have believed﴾, that is, in any state whatsoever, ﴿unless Allah wills﴾, that is, except in the state of His willing their belief, because He is the Supreme King with whom no one has any command. Therefore, there is no consideration except His will. The verse thus refutes the Ahl al-Qadar (those who deny divine predestination), and no sign or other thing has any role in this. Hence no one should hope for their belief by any other means. In my view, though the reach is far, it is close to the truth that ﴿and they swore﴾ [Al-An'am: 109] is coordinated with His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why has no sign been sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ [Al-An'am: 37]. This is common in the speech of eloquent writers: a person relates a portion of his opponent's speech, then begins to refute it, moving on to many matters required by the context, of varied kinds and very lengthy ramifications. Then he relates another portion and says, marveling at it: "He said such and such," and then proceeds with what is related to it by criticism and rebuttal. What supports this is the unity of their endings. The ending of the first is ﴿but most of them do not know﴾ [Al-An'am: 37], and the ending of this one is ﴿but most of them are ignorant﴾, that is, they are people of ignorance (p-232) immersed in it, who swear to believe at the coming of a demanded sign, and do not realize that what prevents them from believing is only the will (of Allah). Otherwise they would believe in the signs that have come to them, for these are sufficient for prompt belief. All signs are equal in their force in indicating the truthfulness of the one who calls, by breaking habitual custom and by the inability to produce the like of them.

When the content of what preceded was the affirmation of the enmity of the disbelievers toward the Prophet ﷺ, it was as if it were said, as consolation for him and to strengthen his heart: "We have made them enemies to you because you are a knowing one, and the ignorant are enemies to the people of knowledge." ﴿And thus﴾, i.e., just as We have made for you enemies from among the disbelievers of mankind and jinn, ﴿We have made for every prophet﴾, i.e., from among those who were before you. He expressed the plural with the singular, and the intended meaning is the genus, indicating that they are one hand in enmity. So He said: ﴿an enemy﴾, and He clarified that the intended meaning is the genus, and that they are the people of evil, saying by way of substitution: ﴿devils﴾, i.e., the evil ones of ﴿mankind and jinn﴾ who are rebellious among them. Perhaps the devil of the jinn seeks the help of the devil of mankind because his heart is close to him, or because his kind inclines more toward him. He indicated the lowliness of their affair and the evil of their outcome by His saying: ﴿Some of them inspire to others﴾, i.e., some of the devils of both kinds, ﴿to others﴾, i.e., speaking to him in secrecy, ﴿ornamented speech﴾, i.e., its adorned and embellished form.

Since this implies that it, because it has no reality, would not have been said were it not for the ornamentation, He explained it further by His saying: ﴿deception﴾, i.e., so that they may deceive them thereby, meaning they may cheat them, so that they become, by accepting their speech, like the heedless who are not characterized by caution. And deception is that in which benefit is believed to be present while there is no benefit in it.

Since the beginning of the verse informs that this occurred by the will of God and His making, He confirmed and established that at its end by saying that if He had willed, they would not have done it. All of this is out of jealousy for the station of divinity (ulūhiyyah) and to declare God free of any deficiency in the attribute of lordship (rubūbiyyah), lest anything come out of it, which would indicate weakness and would lead inevitably to the belief in incapacity. So He said: ﴿And if your Lord had willed﴾. Since this was in the description of his enemies ﷺ and those empowered over him, He indicated that this is for his honor and exaltation, not for his humiliation. So He said: ﴿your Lord﴾, i.e., with what He has toward you of good nurture and abundant kindness, together with His perfect knowledge and all-encompassing power, that they would not do ﴿what they did﴾, i.e., this which I have informed you of concerning their enmity and what branches from it.

Since He established that this is from the mode of nurture, and its outcome is toward good, He definitively made the consequence of that: ﴿So leave them﴾, i.e., leave them in whatever state they happen to be ﴿and what they fabricate﴾, i.e., what they deliberately lie about and invent. Recall what your Lord has upon you of tenderness, so that you know that He who empowered them over this is in utmost compassion toward you, mercy for you, and good nurture, as is not hidden from you. So trust in Him, and know that He has in this a subtle secret that eludes thought, unlike the coming verses in which He expressed by the Name of Majesty (al-Jalālah), for they are in the great audacity of their boldness against the station of divinity.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 113:

Since the sense (taqdir) is: "Leave them alone, so that the hearts of those who believe in the Hereafter may turn away from it (i.e., from their deception), and may be displeased with it, and so that they may know what they are seeing (mubsirun) and recognize (arifun) it, whereby their ranks will be raised" — he (al-Biqa'i) joined to it His saying: ﴿And that the hearts may incline﴾, i.e., incline with a strong inclination through which they turn away, ﴿toward it﴾, i.e., toward their falsehood and what falls within its scope; ﴿the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, i.e., it is not in their nature to believe in it, because it is unseen, and due to their dullness they remain fixed upon illusion. For this reason the worldly life, which is the root of delusion, has overcome them. ﴿And that they may be pleased with it﴾, i.e., with what has become firmly established through their inclination toward it. ﴿And that they may commit﴾, i.e., may do with their full effort, ﴿what they are committing﴾. These phrases, as Abu Hayyan has pointed out, are of the utmost eloquence, because first there is deception, then inclination, then approval, then the act of committing (the sin), so that each one is caused by what precedes it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 114:

When the preceding discussion included information about the unseen, namely that they would not believe when the demanded signs came, and it was the custom of the Arabs to call their enemies and opponents to a judge who would decide between them, and they would resort in unseen matters to the soothsayers (kuhhan, fortune-tellers), because of what those soothsayers would disclose to them from what their jinn companions cast to them, having stolen it by eavesdropping, so that they would add to it many lies, and then this would not harm them in their estimation because of the little of it that proved true, as we have been tested in this era by the infatuation with those who do the same, from madmen and those who imitate them; and the verses that he had finished with (p-235) had established that taking them as protectors was a delusion, this necessitated the negation of their taking other than God, because of what He is characterized by of inspiring what contradicts their inspiration; so the powers fell short in His informing about the realities of matters in detail, in the best detail, in methods whose like the foremost thoughts fell short of, and whose depths the windows of understanding could not reach; thereby His prophethood was established and His messengership made clear. Their proposal was therefore manifestly a form of obstinacy, because they denied the greatest of signs: the Qur'an. They did not believe in it, and they slandered it with what only increased their disgrace. Thus it was established that there is no benefit in answering them to their proposals. So the response, against what the state of their tongues required of seeking arbitration from their allies, was with a strong rebuke to them [in His saying]: ﴿Shall I seek other than God﴾, i.e., the greatest King, in an extreme of eloquence that cannot be attained. The fa' in it is for causation, and the hamzah of denial preceded it because it has the place of initiation, ﴿as a judge﴾, i.e., one who judges between me and you and decides our dispute. Then he argued for this denial by the detailed explanation of the Book in this miraculous detail, saying: ﴿And He it is﴾, i.e., while the reality is that there is none other than Him, ﴿who has sent down to you﴾, i.e., specifically, as a blessing upon me in the primary sense [and upon you in the secondary sense], ﴿the Book﴾, i.e., the most perfect and miraculous, and it is this Qur'an which is an exposition of everything (p-236) ﴿made detailed﴾, i.e., distinguished within it are the lawful and the unlawful, and all other rulings, together with the subtleties and knowledge that the verse-endings convey, which reveal the realities of beginnings and endings. Great attention has been given in this surah to drawing attention to detail, because people of insight have known in crafts that whoever does not do detail well does not perfect composition.

Since the implied meaning was: "You and all the masters of eloquence know its reality through its detail and the inability to match it," He connected to it His saying: ﴿And those to whom We gave the Book﴾; it may also be a circumstantial clause. ﴿We gave them﴾, i.e., by Our greatness which you know and by which they distinguish truth from falsehood, ﴿the Book﴾, i.e., the known revelation of the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, ﴿know﴾, i.e., because of their foremost familiarity with the divine books, ﴿that it is sent down﴾.

Since the noble Name (Allah) was mentioned earlier in (ḥāqa), its place in the context of judgment, which is only with exclusive perfection, and since this position, in the context of sending down, requires kindness, He did not use a pronoun, but said: ﴿from your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is kind to you by what He singled you out with in this Book of kinds of virtues, ﴿in truth﴾, i.e., the most complete, in that it matches what they have of good tidings in their books, and in its agreement with them in the mention of firm rulings, good admonitions, and frequent remembrance of God in ways that soften hearts, (p-237) draw tears, and split breasts, together with its exceeding of their books in detail, conveying the knowledge of divinity and the Sufi stations within the political rulings, and the miraculous nature of every verse.

Since the People of the Book conceal what they have of knowledge and say to the polytheists that they are better guided in the way, in a manner that may suggest they believe its falsehood, or that the matter is confusing to them, He, glory be to Him, made His statement a consequence of this report, in the manner of stirring and inflaming: ﴿So do not be among the doubters﴾ [i.e., negate most emphatically that you be at any time] ﴿among the doubters﴾, i.e., those acting as doubters regarding what We have informed you of, even if they increase their concealment of it and their display of what suggests the opposite. When you contend with them in this, and you are the most perceptive of people and the most knowing of what the transgressions reveal of hidden secrets, you will realize what we have said, even if they strive to conceal it, as the story of the appeal concerning the adulterers and others has shown. Abu Hayyan said: The polytheists of Quraysh said to the Messenger of God ﷺ: "Make between us and you a judge from the rabbis of the Jews, and if you wish, from the bishops of the Christians, to inform us about you from what is in their Book regarding your matter." So it was revealed.

When he had shown that it is the truth from God through the knowledge of the People of the Book, explicitly, and of the people of eloquence, allusively, he proved it by another, witnessed (*shuhudi*) means: that he (ﷺ) never said anything without it coming to pass exactly as he said it, and that no one could prevent or hinder any of what he reported, not for an hour of a day, nor less nor more. (p. 238) By His saying, may He be exalted, placing the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun, to remind him (ﷺ) of the favour that He, glorified is He, has bestowed upon him, and to alert him to the honour and dignity He intends for him: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ [Hud: 119], meaning: was carried out and realised; ﴿your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who does good to you and manages your affair; ﴿in truth﴾ and ﴿justice﴾ in its state, meaning: no one can bring forth any statement concerning any part of it that contradicts its correspondence with reality.

Since truth is not incompatible with justice, He said: ﴿and justice﴾. And since truth and justice may not be complete with the speaker's intent, nor the command of the one commanding be executed, because a stronger party prevents it, He stated that there is no one who can repel His command or reverse His judgment, explicitly expressing what the opening of the verse implied of completeness, and He placed the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun for generality, blessing and delight, saying: ﴿None can alter His words﴾, meaning: insofar as they are His words, absolutely, without specification to any type, but rather everything they report is certainly going to occur, whether one is pleased or whoever is displeased.

Since the one who changes something only accomplishes what he wants of the change if the one being changed does not know the causes that would make his aim succeed, so that he may control them, nor the obstacles that would hinder it, so that he may nullify them, He said, connecting it to what was implied: He is the Mighty, the Wise. ﴿And He﴾, meaning: not other than Him, ﴿is the All-Hearing﴾, meaning: who reaches the hearing of everything that can be heard of sayings and actions, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾, meaning: who reaches the knowledge of all that. Thus He is the One of complete power, whose command is executed over all causes and obstacles, so He allows no one to change any of them, even if one deceives or makes things appear otherwise.

When al-Biqa'i had answered the doubts of the disbelievers and demonstrated the validity of his prophethood (peace be upon him), he began to urge turning away from the ignorance of the ignorant and turning toward the Majestic One. The implied sense is: "If you obey him in what he has commanded you, you will be guided to the path of Allah, by following which all that He has promised you will be fully realized." He then connected to it His saying: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth﴾. Since most souls are bound by the majority, he indicated that this would not be done except by an ignorant person who clings to imitation (taqlid, following others without evidence), so He said: ﴿most of those on earth﴾, meaning: your obedience to them would be found at any time after you have known that most of them only follow conjecture, and that most of them are defiantly disobedient, not knowing and not giving thanks, ﴿they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾, meaning the one who combines the attributes of perfection. Then He gave the reason for this with His saying: ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture﴾ [i.e., just as these ignorant people conjecture that their forefathers were upon the truth].

Since most of those who state matters with certainty do so on the basis of what their conjecture has prompted them to, and falsely, and since the word "kharis" (one who guesses or conjectures) is applied to the liar and to the one who estimates by guesswork, He said: ﴿And they are only guessing﴾, meaning: in their innermost hearts they state matters with certainty according to what they estimate, and then the matter is revealed to be false, so the difference between you and them becomes known in the completion of [the speech] and its effect like the effect of arrows, or in its failure to reach completion and its recoiling like a blunt sword. Thus no doubt remains concerning the matter of the one who is right and the one who is wrong.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 117:

Since the context calls for knowledge that unveils realities and clarifies what is to be followed and what is to be avoided, he gave the reason for this report, saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who has bestowed favour upon you by sending down this Book, which unveils doubt and guides to what is right, ﴿He﴾, i.e., He alone, ﴿is the most knowing﴾. Since the situation strongly calls for knowledge, he cut the sentence off from what follows so that it would immediately be understood that He is more knowing than anyone who might be supposed to have knowledge absolutely. Then he said: ﴿of who﴾, i.e., He knows who ﴿strays﴾, i.e., who at some time commits error, ﴿from His way﴾, i.e., the way He has made clear by His knowledge, ﴿and He﴾, i.e., He alone, ﴿is most knowing of those who are guided﴾, just as He is most knowing of those who go astray. So whoever commands you to follow him, follow him, and whoever forbids you from him, avoid him. Whoever goes astray, He casts him down, and whoever is guided, He saves him. So hold fast to its causes, out of fear of the severe consequence of His punishment on the day of His reckoning.

When He, glory be to Him, had mentioned what preceded regarding the *sawa'ib* (the animals released for idols) and what accompanied them, and what in *al-Ma'idah* the people of ignorance (*ahl al-jahiliyyah*) observed in eating animals over which polytheism had led them astray, He followed this with a statement that there is no harm to the people of faith from the religion of the people of misguidance when they are guided. He then followed that with what suited it and was strung on the same thread and joined to it, until it became evident that everything belongs to Him and is His dominion, that He has no partner, and that therefore He alone is to be thanked. Yet they, despite this, had denied His blessings, taking partners alongside Him, and this did not suffice them; they assigned to these partners a share of what He had created of tillage and livestock. [p-241] By doing so they were preventing the truth from its rightful people and giving to what does not possess harm or benefit what belongs to Him who has the dominion, and leaving aside some of what its rightful owner had bestowed upon them out of regard for those who have no right and no sanctity. The custom of God, exalted is He, has been established that He mentions His noble self with oneness (*al-wahdaniyyah*). This is evidenced by the creation of the heavens and the earth and what He deposited in them for us of benefits and what He originated of conveniences and workmanship. Then He marvels at the one who associates others with Him. Then He commands eating of what He has created, as a reminder of the blessing, so that this may be a summons for every person of understanding to thank Him. Just as He, exalted is He, said in *al-Baqarah*, after ﴿And your God is one God﴾ [al-Baqarah: 163], ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 164], then He said ﴿And among the people are those who take, besides God, equals (*andad*)﴾ [al-Baqarah: 165], then He said ﴿O mankind, eat from what is on the earth, lawful and good﴾ [al-Baqarah: 168]. He has applied this sublime custom in this *surah* also, saying: ﴿Indeed, God is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95], after ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who originated the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 79], then ﴿And they made for God partners, the jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 100]. It indicates that He has no partner in His dominion or sovereignty, and He concludes that there is no judge besides Him who contends with Him in His judgment or competes with Him in any matter of His command. He explains that among its [signs] is the guidance which He made a condition for the absence of harm that would reach one from the religion of the people of polytheism. So, on the basis of all that I have mentioned, He says: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned﴾, that is, at the time of slaughter, ﴿the name of God﴾, that is, the King to whom belongs the complete encompassing, so to Him belongs everything, ﴿upon it﴾, that is, as if one who says this were speaking, whether it was mentioned in action or not. He departed from the expression "that over which" (*ma*) to what I have made the intended meaning, so that it may be understood that mentioning the name in action is recommended, and so that they will not be among those who built their religion upon following desires and false assumptions. It is as if it were said: follow the one who knows the truth and gives it to its people, for he is guided, not turning aside to others, for he is astray. God knows best the two groups. So be among the guided. Eat, then, of what God has created for you as lawful, thankful for His blessing. He lengthened here, unlike in *al-Baqarah*, the discourse between the clauses, in affirming their meanings and what follows from them and in argumentation for all of that, because this is the *surah* of detailed explanation (*al-tafsil*). He used the mention [of the name] while the intended meaning is the acceptability of the food for the one who eats it, that is: eat of what is acceptable to have the name mentioned over it, according to the prescription that He has legislated. That is what He has made lawful of animals and other things, whether it was something they had designated for their idols or not. This excludes what dies of itself (*hatf anfihi*), or over which the name of other than God has been mentioned, or what is of the forbidden kinds, even if it is slaughtered and the name of God is mentioned over it, for it does not accept being made lawful by mention of the name. Thus the mention of the name is in a place other than its proper place, because the texts have come with its prohibition. And do not follow the polytheists in their prohibiting themselves from the good things God has created for them of tillage and livestock, by their naming it for their gods who have no sufficiency. [That] would be an incitement to mention the name over all lawful food, so the verse is like the verse of *al-Baqarah* [with an addition].

Since this command is not accepted except by one from whose heart the religion of polytheism and all its consequences have departed, He said: ﴿If you are﴾, that is, with what you have of the good natural disposition, ﴿believers in His signs﴾, that is, in general, among which are the signs of what is lawful and unlawful, ﴿believers﴾, that is, firmly rooted in the description of faith,

It has already become clear how well this statement is arranged, through His saying: ﴿And what is [the matter] with you﴾, meaning, what would be the case for you in ﴿not eating of that over which the Name of God has been mentioned﴾, meaning, that which is admissible for the Name of God to be mentioned over, ﴿the One to whom all things belong﴾, meaning, because the mention of the Name stands in place of His permission. ﴿And He has already explained to you﴾, meaning, from before that, while the creation is His creation and the command is His command, ﴿what He has forbidden to you﴾, meaning, that which has not been forbidden, explained in clear detail and manifest proof, ﴿except what you are compelled to﴾, meaning, because necessity removes the detailed ruling concerning it by returning it to what it was before the detailing, so that everything becomes lawful with no detailing concerning it. The intended meaning of this verse differs according to the addressees. As for those who were addressed by it at the time of its revelation, the intended detail is the verse that comes after it, for it was revealed all at once. The same applies to everything similar to it that was revealed in Makkah before this sūrah. It also applies to what the Prophet ﷺ reported in a recited revelation at that time, perhaps whose recitation was abrogated while its ruling remained, or in a non-recited revelation, from all the reports that preceded this sūrah. As for those who were addressed by it after it was arranged in this order, the intended meaning concerning them is [as in] al-Baqarah, al-Mā'idah and the other sūrahs that came before, from the lawful and the unlawful.

Since the sense is: whoever acts upon these commands is guided by what knowledge he has attained, and they are few, He followed it with His saying: ﴿And indeed many﴾, meaning, of the people, ﴿will lead astray﴾ (p. 244), meaning, misguidance occurs from them, so they cause others to go astray by deviating from what God's commands called to and His explanation guided to, and so they are on the brink of ruin, ﴿by their desires﴾, meaning, because of their following of desire (hawa, the inclination of the soul). And since desire may sometimes coincide with what knowledge reached through sound reasoning and clear intellect, He said: ﴿without knowledge﴾, meaning, it calls to that [from one who has knowledge] from an earlier law, from one who has the authority.

Since they were denying this, He affirmed for His noble Self what is accepted by everyone, and as proof of the truth of what He reported, He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, meaning, the One who has been good to you by sending down this Book as a witness for you, attesting to its miraculous nature through confirmation, ﴿He﴾, meaning, alone, ﴿is most knowing﴾. The place called for a pronoun, but it was made explicit for generality and to draw attention to the attribute that necessitated this for them. So He said: ﴿of the transgressors﴾, meaning, those who exceed the limits, striving in that.

Since among the things that are, in general, capable in themselves of having God's name mentioned over them is that which is forbidden because it belongs to another or because it contains doubt, He forbade it in a way that covers other than it, saying, by way of conjunction with (﴿So eat﴾ [al-An'am: 118]): ﴿and abandon﴾, i.e., leave, in whatever state it happens to be, even if you think it is not fit, ﴿the outward sin﴾, i.e., what is known to be forbidden from this and other things, ﴿and its inward﴾, i.e., every matter containing doubt, of sayings, deeds, and beliefs. For God has placed for it a sign in the heart, which is that it becomes agitated in him (p-245) and does not settle, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Sin is that which stirs in the heart and wavers in the breast." It was narrated by Muslim from al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, may Allah be pleased with him. Then he gave the reason for this with His saying: ﴿Indeed those who earn sin﴾, i.e., even by the most hidden kinds of earning, as indicated by the bare form of the verb, which is belief, in the noble Name.

[Since the sensible person is one who fears all recompense, the verb is put in the passive, his saying]: ﴿they will be recompensed﴾, i.e., by a promise that admits no failure, ﴿for what﴾, i.e., because of what, ﴿they were﴾ through their corrupt natures, ﴿committing﴾, i.e., acquiring by an acquisition that brings about separation, which is the greatest fear and removes gentleness. The ifti'al verb form (iftiʿāl, the reflexive-derived pattern) indicates that acts of evil only occur through the self's striving against the original, sound fitra (innate disposition).

When He commanded them to eat of what benefits them and helps them to give thanks to Him, warning against eating what would blind their insight, He followed it with a firm, specific prohibition against eating what harms them in their bodies and their characters. This is what opposes the first, in that it lacks the noble Name, so He said: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned﴾, meaning, that which does not admit of the mention of ﴿the name of God﴾, that is, the One from whom nothing is taken except from Him, because He possesses all perfection, and so He has complete encompassing. By the particle of elevation He indicated sincerity and the negation of association, so He said: ﴿over which﴾, meaning, because God has forbidden it, so it becomes impure in substance; or the meaning is: so it becomes corrupting to the body and the soul, from what is mentioned over it, other than His name, glorified is He, (p-246) by what indicates [from] calling it "fisq" (immorality). The explanation of fisq in another verse is what has been invoked over for other than God, and likewise what is similar to it in meaning, of what died or was unlawful for other reasons. His name, exalted is He, is too exalted to be mentioned over what is not lawful. If it is mentioned over it, it is a mockery, and so it does not purify it. As for what is lawful but over which neither the name of God nor anyone else's has been mentioned, it is lawful, as in the Sahih, from ʿĀ'isha, may God be pleased with her, who said: They said: "O Messenger of God! Indeed there are people near us who are recent converts from polytheism, who bring us meat, and we do not know whether they mention the name of God or not!" He said: "Mention the name of God yourselves and eat." Al-Baghawi said: If saying the basmala were a condition for permissibility, then doubt about its presence would prevent eating it, just as doubt about the act of slaughter itself. End.

Since the implied sense was: "Indeed it is wicked in itself and corrupting," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And indeed it is﴾, meaning, eating from it, or it itself, because it is the cause, ﴿an act of fisq﴾, so He made it the very fisq, which is departing from what is fitting to what is not fitting, because it is very deeply rooted in being its cause for what is firmly established among them of its matter and has spread of its evil. This is evidence for what I have interpreted, because forgetfulness is not a cause of fisq, and the animal over which the basmala was left out through forgetfulness is not fisq, and the one who forgets is not a sinner, as al-Bukhari said. To this the indication is what was narrated from ʿĀ'isha, may God be pleased with her, that a people (p-247) said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed a people bring us meat, and we do not know whether the name of God was mentioned over it or not!" He said: "Mention the name of God over it yourselves and eat it." She said: "And they were recent converts from disbelief." End. All of this indicates that what is meant is only that it is of the kind whose slaughter is lawful, and the intent is not to make saying the basmala a condition in practice.

Since doubts may sometimes shake the firm beliefs, He warned against them, saying: ﴿And indeed the devils﴾, meaning the most wicked of the rebellious ones among the jinn and mankind, who are far from good, prepared for evil, burnt by the curse, from the rebellious jinn and men, ﴿do inspire﴾, meaning they whisper with a forceful and swift whispering, ﴿to their allies﴾, meaning those close to them in nature and prepared to accept their speech, ﴿to dispute with you﴾, meaning to turn you away from what He commanded you, by saying to you: "What God has killed is more deserving of being eaten than what you have killed yourselves and your hunting animals," and similar to that. The people of the Sacred Precinct should not stand in other places, and the stranger should not be equal to them in circumambulating in their garments, and vowing to idols is like vowing to the Kaʿba, and similar to this of their superstitions, by which they founded their affairs on desire, which they themselves acknowledge is misleading and harmful, and they exaggerate in blaming following it and inclining to it. And it suffices, in demolishing all their doubts in general, that the Lord of the religion and the Owner of the dominion has forbidden them.

(p-248) Since the implied sense was: "If you obey them, you abandon guidance and follow desire, and it is known that desire leads to polytheism," He followed this with His saying: ﴿And if you obey them﴾, meaning the polytheists, adopting their religion in what they say about abandoning eating what the name of God has been mentioned over and eating what the name of God has not been mentioned over, or in anything of what they dispute with you about, ﴿indeed you are then polytheists﴾, meaning you and they are equal in associating, just as if you mention other than God over your slaughtered animals in the manner of worship, because whoever follows the command of other than God has associated him with God, as the Prophet ﷺ said in the hadith of ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim, may God be pleased with him, concerning His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides God﴾ [al-Tawba: 31], that their worship of them was their making lawful what they made lawful and their making unlawful what they made unlawful. Thus the Prophet ﷺ alerted by this that names follow meanings. Shaykh al-Islam Muhyi al-Din al-Nawawi al-Shafiʿi said in the chapter on sacrifices of the book al-Rawda: It is reported in al-Shamil and others from the text of al-Shafiʿi that if the People of the Book had a slaughtered animal which they slaughter in the name of other than God, such as the Messiah, it is not lawful. And in the book of the judge Ibn Kajj: if a Jew slaughters for Moses or a Christian for Jesus, peace be upon them both, or for the cross, his slaughter is unlawful, and that if a Muslim slaughters for the Kaʿba or for the Messenger of God ﷺ, it should be said that it is unlawful, because he slaughtered for other than God, exalted is He. He said: (p-249) Abu al-Hasan brought out another opinion, that it is lawful, because the Muslim slaughters for God and does not believe about the Messenger of God ﷺ what the Christian believes about Jesus, peace be upon him.

He said: And if one slaughters for an idol, its slaughter is not eaten, whether the slaughterer is a Muslim or a Christian. In the commentary of Shaykh Ibrahim al-Marwazi: what is slaughtered upon facing the sultan to draw near to him, the people of Bukhara issued a ruling that it is unlawful, because it is of what was invoked for other than God. Know that slaughtering for the worshipped one in his name is equivalent to prostrating to him, and each of them is a kind of the veneration and the particular worship that belongs to God, exalted is He, who is the one deserving of worship. So whoever slaughters for other than Him, of an animal or inanimate thing such as an idol, in the manner of veneration and worship, his slaughter is not lawful, and his act is disbelief, like one who prostrates to other than Him in an act of worship. Likewise if he slaughters for Him and for another in this manner. As for if he slaughters for another not in this manner, such as sacrificing or slaughtering for the Kaʿba in veneration of it because it is the House of God, exalted is He, or for the Messenger of God ﷺ, this does not prevent the lawfulness of the slaughter, and to this meaning returns the saying of one who says: "I have offered it as a gift to the Sacred Precinct or to the Kaʿba." Of this kind is slaughtering upon facing the sultan, for it is an expression of joy at his arrival, equivalent to slaughtering the ʿaqīqa for the birth of a child, and such does not necessitate disbelief. Likewise prostrating to other than God out of humbling oneself and submission. Based on this, if the slaughterer says: "In the name of God and the name of Muhammad," intending: "I slaughter in the name of God and seek blessing through the name of Muhammad," it should not be prohibited. And the saying of one who says: "That is not permissible" may be understood to mean that the expression is disliked, because the disliked may be negated as permissible and in absolute permission. Al-Rafiʿi related that a dispute occurred about this among the people of Qazvin, which led to strife, over whether its slaughter is lawful and whether one disbelieves (p-250) by it! He said: The correct view is what we have explained. Shaykh Muhyi al-Din said: Among what supports what he said, that is, al-Rafiʿi, is what Shaykh Ibrahim al-Marwazi mentioned in his commentary: He said: Sahib al-Taqrib related from al-Shafiʿi, may God have mercy on him, that if a Christian names other than God, such as the Messiah, his slaughter is not lawful. Sahib al-Taqrib said: its meaning is that he slaughters it for him. As for if he mentions the Messiah in the sense of sending blessings on the Messenger of God ﷺ, it is permissible. He said: al-Halimi said: it is lawful absolutely, even if he names the Messiah, and God knows best. Then he said in al-Masa'il al-Mansura: The third: Ibn Kajj said: whoever slaughters a sheep and says: "I slaughter for the pleasure of so-and-so," the animal is lawful, because it is not directed to him, unlike one who draws near by slaughtering to an idol. Al-Ruyani said: whoever slaughters for the jinn and intends by it to draw near to God, exalted is He, so that He may turn away their evil from him, it is lawful, and if he intends to slaughter for them, it is unlawful. And what clarifies to you the secret of this coherence and increases its beauty is that all these verses, from His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed God is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95] to the end of the surah, are an elaboration of His saying, exalted is He, at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Say: Shall I take other than God as a protector, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-An'am: 14]. When He mentioned His originating the heavens and the earth by His saying ﴿Indeed God is the splitter of the grain and the date-stone﴾ [al-An'am: 95] and the like, and denied taking others besides Him by His saying ﴿And they made for God partners, the jinn﴾ [al-An'am: 100] and what goes in that direction, He said ﴿So eat﴾ [al-An'am: 118], as an indication of ﴿And He feeds and is not fed﴾ [al-An'am: 14], and His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead and We gave him life?﴾ [al-An'am: 122], and His saying: ﴿So whomever God wills to guide﴾ [al-An'am: 125] and the like of these two, as an indication of His saying: ﴿Say: I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit﴾ [al-An'am: 14], and His saying: ﴿And the day We gather them all﴾ [al-An'am: 22], and what is similar to it points to: ﴿Indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ [al-An'am: 15].

(p-251) And when the elaboration concluded at His saying "so they will soon know" [al-An'am: 135], He began to elaborate on it a second time with His saying: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle﴾ [al-An'am: 136] to the end of it. The secret in the repetition is that when a matter is affirmed or denied, and proofs are established for the affirmation of what was affirmed and the negation of what was denied, and then that is repeated in another style, it becomes more firmly established in the soul and more adhering to the heart, especially if it is in the second style, as is the custom of the Qur'an, an increase in clarification and an alerting to what was not previously mentioned, especially if the expression is excellent and the words sweet and pleasing. And you should know that all of this is the practice of the Qur'an in its styles of variety. Al-Ghazali said at the beginning of his book "al-Jawahir", in the section in which he discusses the Fatiha's containing eight divisions: His saying a second time ﴿the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾ [al-Fatiha: 3] is an indication of the attribute a second time, and do not think it is repetitive, for there is no repetition in the Qur'an, since the definition of repetition is what does not contain additional benefit, and the mention of mercy after the mention of "the worlds" and before the mention of "the Master of the Day of Judgment" [al-Fatiha: 4] contains two great benefits in detailing the channels of mercy. Then he mentioned what amounts to: one of them turns to the creation of each world among the worlds in its most perfect and best kinds and giving it everything it needs, and the second turns to what follows it, by indicating mercy in the Hereafter on the Day of Recompense when the eternal dominion is bestowed. He said: The explanation of this is lengthy, and the purpose (p-252) is that there is [no] repetition in the Qur'an, and if you see something that appears repeated, look at its precedents and its successors so that the increase in benefit of repeating it will be revealed to you. End. And in that there is another point: "the Most Merciful" indicates what He said in terms of lordship in both the first and the second origination, and "the Especially Merciful" indicates, by its particular quality, what divinity is pleased with, toward the second origination and the second preservation, by the mercy of recompense, and toward what the particularity understands of blessing toward those whom mercy has not particularly included, as the indication to it has already passed in the Fatiha.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 122:

Since the meaning of the warning against obeying the polytheists is that, if you do so, you will have returned yourselves to the darkness of misguidance after being granted the light of guidance, the implied sense becomes: "Is one who is like this the same as one who counsels himself by following the proofs and guarding against doubts?" He follows this with His saying: ﴿Is one who was dead⦅﴾ – that is, drowned in the waves of the darkness of disbelief, having in themselves nothing but inanimateness, or rather non-existence – ﴿then We gave him life⦅﴾ – that is, by Our greatness, through the shining of the lights of faith upon his heart, which, if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt – ﴿and made for him a light⦅﴾ – that is, a guidance to every good – ﴿by which he walks among the people⦅﴾ illuminated by it, so that they recognize his deeds, his character and his words – ﴿like one whose likeness is⦅﴾ – that is, the one by whom he is likened, which is that whose inner spirit and essential state of heart are revealed through the aspect of resemblance – or the meaning may be: his description is that he is ﴿in darknesses⦅﴾ – that is, he has from himself the darkness of ignorance, the darkness of what arises from it of caprice, and the darkness of what caprice gives rise to of disbelief. And when the likeness, which is the higher, is in something, the one likened is deeply rooted in it by way of priority; therefore He said: ﴿not coming out of them⦅﴾ – that is, that likeness does not come out ﴿of them⦅﴾ – that is, the darknesses – because of the evil of his deeds that has been made attractive to him, until they become dearer to him than his own self and wealth. And if the likeness does not come out of something, the one likened does not come out of it either, otherwise there would be no resemblance between them. This is because his deed was made attractive to him. And this refers back to His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Only those who hear respond, while the dead – Allah will raise them⦅﴾ [al-An'am: 36], and His saying: ﴿And those who denied Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darknesses⦅﴾ [al-An'am: 39].

Since the inspiration of the devils to their allies is something that necessitates persistence in blindness and is nothing but making vices appear attractive, and their state is such that wonder at it is intense, it is as if it were said: Were it not for our seeing their state, we would not believe that a rational person would be pleased with what they have done to themselves. Has anyone ever fallen into a state like theirs? It is said: Yes. ﴿Thus⦅﴾ – that is, just as the evil of their deeds was made attractive to them – ﴿the deeds of the disbelievers have been made attractive to them⦅﴾ – that is, all of them – ﴿what they used to do⦅﴾ according to what We had created them upon – so they are forever in darknesses. Thus the verse is of the type of ihtibak (interlocking): it first affirmed their being in darknesses as an indication of its counterpart, and secondly the making-attractive as an indication of its counterpart first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 123:

Since it was known that their enmity toward him (ﷺ), indicated by His saying, ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾ [al-An'am: 112], the verse, is undertaken only by the greatest of people, because of the lofty rank that he (ﷺ) had, the nobility of his tribe, and the abundance of his relatives, and because none persists in it except an ignorant person whose insight is obscured and for whom his ugly deeds are made attractive, He, exalted is He, joined to the making-attractive for the disbelievers His saying: ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: just as We made attractive to the disbelievers the evil of their deeds, so the greatest of the people of Makkah plotted, and others followed their scheming. ﴿We have appointed﴾, meaning: by the greatness We possess in establishing the means for whatever exalts a person's word or makes him of lowly standing. ﴿In every town﴾, meaning: every principal city, [and since greatness varies in its kinds according to the persons of the criminals, he matched with the superlative forms the ones intended by them in the plural in one of the two dialects, and he expressed with the form of the utmost plural to indicate their extreme multiplicity, so he said]: ﴿its greatest criminals﴾, meaning: those who sever what ought to be joined.

Since it is in the nature of a human being to seek means of elevation for himself, and he could not reach that in the abode where effects are bound to causes, by the wisdom of causes, except through scheming, and since the greatest are more capable of carrying out scheming and promoting falsehoods, through what the majority of people strive for by seeking their approval out of greed for what is in their hands, and since a person, whenever he becomes empowered in that, goes deeper into it, and since the great one only attains what has been decreed for him in that by God's decree (p-255) for him; with what has been decreed for him in that, it is as if He created it for him. So He said, expressing it by the term "appointing" because of what it contains of causing and making to be: ﴿That they may scheme therein﴾, meaning: that they may deceive their underlings and incite them with what they dress up for them of matters, until they follow them, and so they become hostile to the party of God for their sake.

Since that was painful, enraging and grieving, He said, belittling their affair and diminishing their matter: ﴿And they scheme not﴾, meaning: while the state is that they [do not] ﴿scheme except against themselves﴾, because their working at scheming is a burden upon them and a ruin for them, and because their scheming against the friends of God is in truth scheming against God, and that is neither achievable nor possible in any way whatsoever. And how could the scheming of one who knows nothing of the unseen be carried out against the One who knows the whole of the unseen! ﴿And they perceive not﴾, meaning: and they have no sort of awareness that their scheming returns upon their own selves; for God, who knows their secret and their open speech, makes their destruction, through what He makes attractive to them, lie within their own planning. He only set His divine custom in this way because of what it contains of signs of prophethood, for the overcoming of a single person, alone or with the following of many among them who are not regarded, with the smallness of number and the weakness of support, against the chiefs and strong men of the people, along with his long stay among them opposing them and calling out against them that your religion will be erased and my religion will prevail, even if you dislike it, is one of the breaking of customary norms and the manifest signs, confirming His saying, exalted is He: ﴿God has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 21], and ﴿And indeed Our host, they are the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 173], and in the like of that.

[p. 256] When he had established this, he followed it with another statement of theirs that indicates their arrogance and self-importance. He said, connecting it to ﴿They swore by God, with the most emphatic of their oaths﴾ [al-An'am: 109], in wonder at their condition regarding the misguidance that had been made attractive to them, and as confirmation of what preceded concerning the information that they will not believe even if every sign comes to them, unless God wills; and as a confirmation of the earlier verse's (mention of) their scheming against others and its turning back upon themselves: ﴿And when a sign comes to them﴾, that is, to the disbelievers, among the great criminals and their followers, ﴿they say﴾, out of envy for the one whom God has singled out with prophethood, because they are great men, ﴿"We will never believe"﴾, emphasizing the negation [because of what the miracles of the prophets, peace be upon them, contain of lessons that compel the belief that even the most obstinate people of disbelief would submit], ﴿never﴾, that is, ever, ﴿"until we are given"﴾, because of the exaltation and greatness that we possess, which require that no one be singled out over us with anything, ﴿"the like of what"﴾

Since their outlook was confined to the world of the senses without looking toward the side of God, since He is unseen, they used the passive form in their saying: ﴿"was given to the messengers of God"﴾. It may be that the intended meaning is: "until revelation is sent down to us," lest they be lesser than us, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Rather, every man among them wants to be given scriptures spread out﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52]. And as has been mentioned earlier at the beginning of the surah, from Abu Jahl, that he said: "We and the sons of 'Abd Manaf competed for honor until, when we were like two horses in a race, they said: 'Among us is a prophet to whom revelation comes from heaven.' (p. 257) Woe to you! When will we attain this? By God, we will never believe in him, ever." It may also be that the intended meaning is that he (ﷺ) would bring signs like those of the earlier (prophets): the splitting of the sea, the hand, the staff, the raising of the dead, and the like. [They called them "descent" and mockery, and they expressed it with the name of Majesty, indicating complete power, so there is no excuse.]

When He mentioned the name of Majesty, announcing the enormity of what they had dared against Him, because of their blindness, by which the darkness of desire had obscured the lights of their hearts, and (because of their blindness) to the grandeur of the messengers, before which the haughty noses bow, He repeated it again to magnify the matter and to draw attention to the great station that lies there. So He said, in response to them, regarding what their saying contained of the claim to have learned wisdom and of objecting to God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿God knows best﴾, that is, with what He possesses of the attributes of perfection, ﴿where﴾, that is, from every one from whom knowledge can be possible, ﴿He places﴾, that is, He determines, through what He causes of matters, ﴿His message﴾, that is, all of it in relation to every individual of creation, for He does not place any part of it according to whim.

When this arrangement revealed that they had dared against Him, and that they persisted in the worst of sins, which is disbelief, not in seeking proof but out of the disease of envy, the soul longed to know what would befall them. So He answered: ﴿Will strike﴾, that is, by a promise that admits no breach, (p. 258) and He stated explicitly the place where a pronoun would have been expected, to generalize and to attach the judgment to the attribute: ﴿those who committed crime﴾, that is, those who severed what should have been connected. ﴿Humiliation﴾, that is, contentment with abasement because there is no helper. And since a thing is magnified by the greatness of its place and of the one from whom it proceeds, He said: ﴿with God﴾, that is, the One who unites the attributes of greatness, ﴿and a punishment﴾, that is, along with the humiliation, ﴿severe﴾, that is, in this world by killing and disgrace, and in the Hereafter by the Fire, ﴿because﴾, that is, because of what ﴿they used to scheme﴾.

Since He, may He be exalted, has already stated that He knows best who has been sealed upon his heart, so that he never turns away from error, and who accepts guidance, whether immediately or in the end, and that the scheming of the criminals is only by His will and His all-pervading power, it is known that the command belongs to Him and that hearts are in His hand. From this His saying follows: ﴿So whomever Allah wills﴾, that is, He who possesses all majesty and honour, ﴿to guide﴾, that is, to create guidance in his heart, whether he is among the greatest of the criminals or others, ﴿He opens his breast﴾, that is, He expands it by making it prepared and receptive to the light, ﴿for Islam.﴾ The Imam Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: It was related that ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah! Does the breast really expand?" He said: "Yes, light enters the heart." He asked: "Is there a sign of that?" He ﷺ said: "Withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning in repentance to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death (comes)." (p-259) In another narration it reads: "before the missing of it [death]." ﴿And whomever He wills﴾, that is, Allah, to be misguided, and He did not manifest here a sign that error follows the requirement of the natural disposition, ﴿to lead astray﴾, that is, to create error and perpetuate it in his heart, ﴿He makes his breast﴾, that is, the seat of his heart, which is the source of lights, ﴿narrow, constricted (ḍayyiqan ḥarajan)﴾, that is, extremely tight, so that it is ﴿murtajis﴾, that is, agitated and disturbed. It was related that ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, summoned a Bedouin from Kinana of the Banu Mudlij and said to him: "What is the ḥarija?" He said: "It is a tree that neither a wild animal nor a grazing animal can reach." Al-Baghawi related the story, and his wording is: He said: "The ḥarija among us is the tree that stands among other trees, which no grazing animal can reach, nor any wild animal, nor anything." Then they agreed, and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Likewise, the heart of the disbeliever, nothing of faith or goodness reaches it." Al-Baghawi added: Sibawayh said: ḥaraj, with a fatḥa, is the verbal noun, meaning "possessing constriction," while with a kasra it is the noun, which is the most intense narrowness. Al-Mahdawi said: Here ḥaraj means the intensely narrow, and this has been discussed before; and he said regarding al-Nisa in His saying: ﴿Then they will not find in themselves any ḥaraj regarding what you have decided﴾ [al-Nisa: 65], that is, constriction. To this meaning returns the saying of Mujahid that it is doubt, and the saying of al-Dahhak that it is sin, as if it were the constriction of doubt or the constriction of sin. (p-260) Al-Nahhas said: ﴿ḥarajan mimmā qaḍayta﴾ [al-Nisa: 65] means doubt and constriction, and the origin of ḥaraj is constriction. End. The verification of this is that the verse here contains, after the emphasis by using the pattern faʿīl rather than fāʿil, another emphasis, either by the verbal noun or by the active participle, which adds intensity beyond the root verb. So with the fatḥa, meaning ḍayyiqan with a kasra on the ḍād and sukūn on the yā' [i.e., ḍayq], and its meaning, if you read (ḥarajan) with a kasra, it means ḍayyiq, by repeating the active participle. The root (ḥ-r-j), in this specific order, revolves around a narrow place abounding in trees, and it implies standing on the surface of the earth, elevation, gathering, prevention, hardship, bewilderment, heat and cold. These five permutations, in any order, are: (ḥ-r-j) (j-ḥ-r) (r-j-ḥ) (ḥ-j-r) (j-r-ḥ), and they revolve around the stone, which is the well-known physical body, and it implies heaviness, prevention, sharpness, standing, and hardness, which is harshness, and harshness implies constriction. Thus ḥaraj returns to hardness in the sense of constriction. A ḥarja is a thicket, a ḥaraj is a necklace of wood beads, ḥurjūj is a strong cold wind, and a ḥurjūj she-camel is one with a fiery heart; and it is possible that it returns to sharpness. Jarḥ is the bier of the dead, because of the constriction of the breast from remembering it, and because it is too narrow for the beds of the living. From it also comes juḥr (the hole of a jerboa or similar), for a hole dug into the ground. Ḥaraj in the sense of sin returns to heaviness, and from that arises the burden that leads to bewilderment; from it comes ḥarajat ʿaynuhu, meaning his eye became bewildered, so it does not blink. Heaviness also implies jurḥ in the sense of a piercing wound that penetrates the body; and from this comes (ijtaraḥa), when one earns wealth, because it is one of its effects. From it comes rujḥān in the sense of heaviness, and a dominant judgment that makes its owner dignified and grave; and from it comes al-ʾurjūḥa (the swing), because each of its two ends outweighs the other. Prevention returns to ḥajar in the sense of intellect, in the sense of protection, and ḥarām, and a female horse, because she may be prevented from being ridden due to pregnancy or a foal; and ḥajr in property, and ḥujra for a nearby region, because when a thing is far from you, even by a fathom, it is withheld from you, and the feminine form in it is for its nearness. Shakhūṣ (standing out, departing) returns to ḥaraj for a long she-camel. Imam Abu al-Fath ibn Jinni, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book al-Muḥtasab fī Tawjīh al-Qirāʾāt al-Shawādhdh, at His saying in this surah (wa-ḥarthun ḥijr) [al-Anʿam: 138], regarding the one who reads with the rāʾ first: all the combinations of this five-letter root converge in their meanings in constriction, hardness and gathering. If you look carefully, leaving aside weariness and impatience, you will find the matter as he said (p-262), Allah knows best: like ḥajar (stone), istaḥjara (the clay hardened), al-ḥujra and its remainder; all of it returns to cohesion and constriction. From it comes ḥaraj for narrowness, and jurḥ similarly; ḥarajah is what intertwines of trees so that it is not possible to enter it; from it comes ḥijr and its derivatives because of its narrowness; from it comes jarḥ, because the iron mixes with the flesh and clings to it. From it comes (rajaḥa al-mīzān), because one of its two sides inclined toward the ground, so it came near it and what had been wide between it and the ground became narrow. If you say: when one of them inclines toward the ground, the other has gone far? It is said: our discussion is about the heavier side, and the heavier is that which is toward the ground; as for the other, it is not called heavier. When this is established, and it is established, then likewise His saying: ﴿wa-ḥarthun ḥijr﴾ [al-Anʿam: 138] has the meaning of ḥijr: their understanding is that it is forbidden and restricted, that none will eat from it except whom they claim they want to feed it to, according to their assertion. End.

Since the possessor of this constricted breast hardly reaches guidance, and if some of it reaches him through the words of a preacher and from the path of a sincere guide, he finds no way, so it recoils; and thus he remains in perpetual agitation and hesitation. His description was His saying: ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾, that is, this person forces himself, in accepting guidance, to ascend ﴿into the sky﴾, in concealment and shame, from attempting what is impossible, as indicated by the reading of the one who assimilated the tāʾ into the ṣād. So whenever his voluntary movement lifts him up, his natural compulsory movement brings him down (p-263), as we see some insects carrying something heavy and climbing with it on a smooth wall; it keeps forcing itself and falls, then forces its climb again, and perhaps reaches its first place and falls, and perhaps falls short of it. This is something that is usually impossible, so he remains murtajis, that is, agitated, and the sources of agitation follow him with what comes after, as will come.

Since what He described the breast of the misguided with is something from which one recoils, and since ruḥs (filth) originally refers to what is considered repulsive, and what is repulsive is shunned, and since this statement may have raised a question, namely: is this—making the misguided person of this description—specific to the people of this age? It was answered with what amounts to: No.

﴿Thus﴾, that is, just as Allah placed filth upon the one whom He wished to be misled among the people of this age, ﴿Allah places﴾, that is, by His complete power and overwhelming greatness, ﴿the filth﴾, that is, agitation and impurity, ﴿upon those who do not believe﴾ among the people of every age, because of His—glory be to Him—will for the perpetuation of their error. So the verse is of the type of iḥtibāk (the omission of parallels): He mentioned error first as evidence of its omission second, and mentioned filth second as evidence of its omission first. The verse is explicit that Allah wills the guidance of the believer and the error of the disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 126:

When he had mentioned what he imposed upon the people of misguidance, in words that are repugnant, it was most fitting to follow it with the Straight Path (al-sirat), for it is among the things that are loved for its uprightness and for its being attributed to the Lord who (p-264) possesses, together with the gathering of all perfections, the attributes of tenderness, goodness and kindness. It is also (attributed) to this Messenger, whom every one who sees him or hears of him loves, in his creation and his character. Better than that and more profound is that the root r-j-s (rijs) revolves around disturbance (idtirab), which necessarily entails crookedness, which necessarily entails misguidance, which prevents faith. So when He, glorified is He, likened the state of the misguided to the state of one in turmoil, and informed that He imposed this turmoil upon everyone who does not believe, He followed it with describing His path as straight, which is the farthest thing from the disturbance that necessarily entails crookedness. The implied sense is: "This is the state of the people of misguidance."
