So He joined to it His saying: ﴿And this﴾, that is, what We have mentioned of the guiding laws in this Qur'an, which We concluded by stating that the One who guides and misguides is God alone, not the bringing of suggested signs, even if every sign came. ﴿is the path﴾, that is, the way ﴿of your Lord﴾, that is, the One who is good to you, this path being ﴿straight﴾, that is, without any crookedness at all. Rather, it is upon the method of the original nature (fitrah), which is in the best of forms, by sound reason that has not been mixed with desire nor with any defect, (recognizing) that the whole matter is in the hand of God, so that man never ceases to fear God and to hope in Him, because He is capable of all things. As for other than Him, they have no power except by His decree, for He created the powers and capacities, according to us and according to the Mu'tazilah. Let the particulars then be likewise, for creation cannot be conceived without knowledge, and no one but God has all-encompassing knowledge. The Imam said: The verse before it is among the muhkamat (clear, decisive verses), so it must be taken according to its apparent meaning, and it is forbidden to alter it by interpretation (ta'wil).

(p-265) And since all that is in this path is upon the method of reason, nothing of it being outside of it, even though there is in it what reason alone cannot grasp, rather it necessarily requires the guidance of the guides, the Messengers who take (their authority) from God, He said, explaining its praise and guiding to its harmony with reason: ﴿We have indeed detailed﴾, that is, to the utmost detail, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿the signs﴾, that is, all of them, distinguished one by one, such that each one is distinguished from the others in a way that admits no confusion, ﴿for a people who remember﴾, that is, who exert themselves to free themselves from the impurities of the obstacles to reason, from desire and other things, even by the least degree of effort, as indicated by the idgham (assimilation of the letters), so that they may be reminded [that He said: there is nothing We have mentioned except that We have placed in their minds a witness to it.

Since remembrance of the signs occurs only among those who have been granted special care on the paths of guidance, He said, encouraging remembrance because it is the cause of the divine outpouring upon hearts prepared for it: ﴿For them﴾, i.e., those who remember, ﴿is the Abode of Peace﴾, i.e., Paradise. He attributed it to Himself, glorified is He, to increase the desire for it. He specified this noble name because no harm, fear, or weariness touches it. Then He increased the encouragement toward it by saying: ﴿with their Lord﴾, i.e., [in] the guarantee of the One who does good to them, and in His presence, through what He prepared for them and made easy for them. ﴿And He is﴾, i.e., alone, ﴿their Protector﴾, i.e., the One who takes charge of their affairs, not leaving them to anyone other than Him. This indicates His nearness to them, and "with" indicates their nearness to Him, because of what He expanded of their breasts with monotheism. Since this might be restricted to remembrance, He clarified that what is meant by it is its conversion into deeds, for deeds are the measure of truthfulness and its balance. So He said: ﴿for what﴾, i.e., because of what ﴿they used to do﴾, i.e., as He had disposed them to do it. That was not except by His bounty, ﴿they used to do﴾.

[p. 267] When Allah, glory be to Him, had detailed the conditions of the two groups and urged reflection, alerting that everything in the Qur'an is something reason guides to, and mentioned the end of those who reflect, He made clear that others are headed to ruin, because they followed their desires, which harm them. It is known that they worship other than their Owner, and that no servant serves other than his master without his master's command except that the master rebukes or punishes him. This is fixed in every sound mind. Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned what precedes that end of terrors in the appointed term (al-ajal al-musamma), which He concealed with Himself and made one of the greatest pillars of this surah. He left it vague at its beginning, and clarified some of its conditions in its course several times, in various modes of expression. That term is the Day of Gathering (yawm al-hashr). Here He, glory be to Him, mentioned some conditions of the heedless, some of what He will say to them on it, and what He will do with them of rebuke and punishment, out of kindness to them and to invite them to repentance. He said, comprehending both groups: ﴿And the day﴾, that is: remember, [p. 267 continued] in your remembrance, the day ﴿when He will gather them﴾, that is: the people of His allegiance and the people of His enmity, ﴿all together﴾, leaving none of them behind. ﴿Then He will say﴾, that is: We will say, through whomever of Our hosts We wish, to the people of Our enmity, as a rebuke and reproach, when they will have no defence at all: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾, that is: the hidden, unsociable ones, the rebellious devils who have power over humankind, whom they see from where you do not see them. ﴿You have indeed taken many﴾, that is: you sought and brought about a great multitude ﴿from mankind﴾, that is: through misleading [the sociable, the manifest ones], until most of them became your followers. [This verse is an instance of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two contrasting elements are each left implicit in one part and expressed in the other): it expressed concealment first, indicating its opposite, which is manifestness, and expressed companionship and tranquillity second, indicating its opposite, which is estrangement and aversion, first.]

﴿And their allies from mankind will say﴾: this is a conjunction with the response of the jinn, concealed [from] the governing element in "O assembly" (yā ma'shar), whose implied sense is, as the verses coming later in the surah indicate in detailing this dialogue: they will say, "Our Lord, they led us astray, for they used to listen to us in their penetration and their hearing of strange reports from us, so they deserve the punishment alone." He omitted the response of the jinn, because, although it is not hidden, being indicated by what is conjoined to it, it suits their condition of concealment together with their fame. He mentioned it in the past tense to indicate that its occurrence is certain, since it is the report of one who does not break a promise. The purpose of this dialogue is a kind of what will be detailed in His saying: ﴿Each group's last said to its first: "Our Lord, these have led us astray"﴾ [al-A'raf: 38], and His saying: ﴿Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant: "Indeed we were your followers"﴾ [Ibrahim: 21]. ﴿Their allies from mankind﴾, that is: the jinn ﴿from mankind﴾, [that is] those who took them as allies through following and obedience in what they called them to of error, acknowledging and pleading: ﴿Our Lord﴾ [O Nurturer who is good to us]. ﴿We have enjoyed one another﴾, that is: sought enjoyment and brought it about, we with them in what they said, and they with us in our obedience to them and our seeking refuge with them. ﴿And we have reached Your term﴾, that is: we and they ﴿which You appointed for us﴾; and they referred the matter to decree, saying: ﴿which You appointed for us﴾, which is death that You decreed upon us and made us equal under the lash of Your subjugation, and drinking the cups of its heat and its cold; then this day, about which we were all jointly in denial, so we all deserve punishment.

When this was complete, it was as if it were said: "What did Allah say to them after this strange dialogue, which is a kind of the speech of the people of inner meaning in this world, a confused and disordered thing with no outcome?" So it was said: ﴿He will say﴾, that is: the one addressing them on Allah's behalf: ﴿The Fire is your abode﴾, that is: your dwelling-place, all of you, with no benefit to you from referring things to decree; ﴿abiding therein﴾, that is: for what has no end, because deeds are by intention, and you were firmly resolved that you would remain upon this disbelief for as long as you lived, even for what has no end. So the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

[p. 268] Since it is established that the sovereignty of one who is under obligation to something, and bound by it in such a way that he cannot be free of it, is not complete, He, glory be to Him, made clear that His sovereignty is not like that; rather, it is in the utmost perfection. Nothing is obligatory upon Him; indeed all His acts are beautiful and all that issues from Him is good. Therefore He made the continuation of their punishment contingent upon His will, saying: ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾. And since the aim of this surah is to manifest greatness out of jealousy for the station of divinity, He expressed it with the greatest Name, saying: ﴿Allah﴾, that is: the One to whom belongs the mantle of greatness, so that no one can object to Him or even intend to do so. Far, far be it! Hopes are cut off beneath that, and the necks of men remain bowed. In His hand is the garment of might; whoever stirs in his heart to lift his bowed neck, He strikes with the maces of humiliation and brings him down into the pits of disgrace. It is established that He, glory be to Him, does not will the cessation of any of this for them in any state, and the Book has affirmed this in explicit statements. And in His stating it in this suspended form, along with what preceded, is an increase in their punishment, by suspending their hope of their affliction ending in a way they have no hope of.

Since the manifestation of majesty in this situation contains, among great terrors, what speech cannot contain, He followed it with gentleness toward the one addressed, ﷺ, saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, that is: the One who is good to you by raising up your allies and lowering your enemies.

Since the context, in such a discourse at the gathering of judgment, pertains to wisdom and knowledge, and since looking at wisdom means placing everything in its greatest station, He placed first the description of [p. 270] it, saying: ﴿is Wise﴾, that is: so He does not punish the sincere one and leave the polytheist, nor punish some of those who associated partners while leaving others. ﴿Knowing﴾, that is: of the subtleties of affairs and their great matters, of both groups, so that no one's deed is hidden from Him, such that He would neglect it for that reason.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 6, verse 129:

When this had become clear, that He had empowered the disbelievers among the wrongdoing jinn over the wrongdoing humans and given them dominion over them, He - exalted is He - informed that this is His practice with every wrongdoer, of whatever kind he may be, whether he is a disbeliever or not. So He said: ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: and like that empowerment by which We empowered the jinn over the humans, with what increased the punishment of both groups, ﴿We make some of the wrongdoers allies of others﴾, meaning: We cause to follow one another at all times and among all creatures, ﴿some of the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: those who are immersed in wrongdoing, ﴿others﴾, meaning: by bringing together their forms in their inward attributes and characteristics, and by empowering some of them over others in misguidance and leading astray, in pains and shackles, ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾, meaning: by their innate natures. They gather and submit to one another because of the common dispositions with which We made them, according to the suitable causes We established for that wrongdoing, which We facilitated for them, until all their deeds became misplaced. So some of them wrong others and destroy others, while they increase only in mutual association, until all of them deserve what We have written for them of punishment.

Al-Tabarani narrated in *al-Awsat*, from Jabir - may Allah be pleased with him - who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

"Indeed Allah - Mighty and Majestic - says: I will take vengeance upon those who [hate Me] through those who hate [Me], then I will return them all to the Fire."

And from Malik ibn Dinar, who said: I found in some of the revealed books of Allah that Allah, exalted is He, says: "I destroy My enemies through My enemies, then I destroy them through My friends."

Or it may be said: We have been informed that Allah - Mighty and Majestic - made the believers rulers because of the goodness of their deeds, and just as He made them rulers in order to honor them, He makes some of the oppressors rulers over others in order to humiliate them, because of what they used to practice of evil deeds, base traits and vile characteristics, leading them to the destruction of pains and terrors. Or it may be said: It has become evident that each of the wrongdoers among the jinn and humans was an ally of the other, and just as We made some of them allies of others in this world, so We will do when We gather them into the Fire, making some of them allies - that is, followers of one another - so that some of them may enjoy the others and help one another if they are able. But far is that from them, far indeed! Weeping, wailing, regret and lamentation will occupy them.

When this dialogue ended, along with the close alliance and neighboring it produced, and its outcome was the alliance with those whose alliance is harmful, Allah, glorified is He, followed it with another dialogue whose outcome is hostility toward those whose hostility is harmful. He said, substituting it for the first address, to complete the rebuke, reproach, and denunciation: ﴿O assembly of jinn﴾. He placed them first because the context concerns demonstrating their dominance. ﴿And mankind﴾. He rebuked them with His words, warning the listeners now and inclining them toward repentance: ﴿Did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ Since the two groups were addressed together as if they were one thing, He said ﴿from among you﴾, even though the messengers were from mankind alone.

Since the focus of this surah is mostly on knowledge, to establish the completeness of power, which is one of its necessary attributes, as shown by ﴿He knows your secret and your open﴾ [al-An'am: 3], ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ [al-An'am: 53], ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen﴾ [al-An'am: 59], and other verses, and for this reason it frequently mentions detail, which only the one with knowledge can provide, qasas (narrating, which is following the trace) was more fitting for this. So He said ﴿they relate to you My verses﴾, by recitation and by explaining the places of the proofs, ﴿following the signs,﴾ meaning they trace, by the signs that deserve, by their majesty and greatness, to be attributed to the places of your doubts, and so they untie them with a definitive solution. ﴿And warn you﴾, meaning they frighten you ﴿of the meeting of this your day﴾, meaning with what they told you, that it pursues you with a swift pursuit, and you are heading toward it in the ships of days and the vessels of sins, while you do not perceive the swift passage. ﴿They will say﴾, making excuses for themselves with humility and submission, ﴿We bear witness﴾ to what You, glorified are You, did to us of good, and what we did of ugliness, ﴿against ourselves﴾, meaning by the coming of the messengers to us and their advice to us, as shown by another verse:

﴿They will say, "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers"﴾ [az-Zumar: 71]. He clarified that their misguidance was in the most wretched and frivolous of ways, the worldly life, such that they were deceived by it despite its lowliness, because it is cut off from the Hereafter, despite the Hereafter's nobility, because it is absent. So He said: ﴿And the worldly life deceived them﴾ (p. 273), meaning they bore this witness while the state was that the worldly life had deceived them, ﴿the worldly life﴾, meaning the present one in their sight at that time, lowly in itself because of its passing, away from following the messengers, like the ignorant man's habit of contentment with the base, and the beast's contentment with the immediate. So their testimony harmed them. But they could not conceal it. Rather, ﴿they bore witness﴾, meaning in this station of the long stations of the Resurrection, ﴿against themselves﴾ also, with what is even more manifestly harmful to them than this, namely ﴿that they had been﴾ by nature and disposition ﴿disbelievers﴾, meaning drowned in disbelief. It is also possible that the deception was that they supposed the conditions of the Hereafter would proceed as they were accustomed to in the world, namely that admitting guilt and speaking the truth may benefit the guilty and restrain the anger of the wrathful, so that he abandons punishment and pardons the offense. Therefore they bore witness to the coming of the messengers to them and to the establishment of the proof against them, and they bore witness against themselves to disbelief. But that only increased them in ruin, grief, and punishment.

When He, glorified is He, had mentioned the establishment of proof against the disbeliever regarding the Return (al-ma'ad) through the messengers, peace be upon them, He gave the reason for sending them. This was as encouragement and urging to follow them during the period of respite after warning, and as admonition and guidance within a piercing warning and discipline. So He said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the matter of great benefit, is that We sent the messengers ﴿because﴾, i.e., for the sake of the fact that ﴿your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly﴾, i.e., the One who is bountiful to you by honoring your people, having established His destroying (them) ﴿while their people were heedless﴾, i.e., they were immersed in heedlessness of what is incumbent upon them, which their intellects cannot independently grasp. That is, (they were heedless) by what was composed in them of appetites and what dominated them of pleasures, so their intellects were held back from penetrating knowledge of what is intended for them. Then We sent messengers to them until they woke them from their sleep and alerted them from their heedlessness. Thus, punishing them after their denial became the binding truth and the correct justice.

It is also permissible that the meaning be: "destroying them as wrongdoers," so that the negated element is injustice, like the negation in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is never unjust to the servants﴾ [Fussilat: 46]. According to the first reading, what is negated is their wrongdoing.

When God, glory be to Him, had explained that one of the two groups has the Abode of Peace and the other has the Abode of Blame, He said, joining both groups and linking to His words ﴿For them is the Abode of Peace with their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 127]: ﴿And for each﴾, that is, for each doer from the two groups, whether righteous or wicked [among the two kinds, the jinn and mankind], in both abodes, ﴿are degrees﴾, meaning God elevates them by them, ﴿according to what they did﴾, meaning because of what they did. And there are also ranks of descent, into which He casts them down, in the same way.

Since it had preceded that He, exalted is He, does not destroy the wrongdoers except after giving them warning, and that this implies granting them respite, and He had concluded their conditions by stating that they are the place where heedlessness is established and persists, He denied that anything of this escapes Him, in a manner in which He affirmed for Himself comprehensive knowledge of all their deeds. So He said: ﴿And your Lord is not﴾, that is, the One who does good to you by elevating your allies and lowering your enemies, ﴿heedless of what they do﴾. He went to the extreme in negation in order to establish greater knowledge, so He said (p-275) ﴿heedless of what they do﴾, that is, of anything any one of the two groups does. Rather, He knows every such thing and what the doer deserves, and He is able to repay him. Thus it does not occur to anyone that the respite is due to the concealment of what is deserved, owing to the concealment of what necessitates it. [So this verse is among the texts concerning the writing down of the righteous among the jinn.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 133:

Since seeking worship for the sake of obedience and abstention may sometimes suggest that Allah needs it, either for some benefit gained from obedience or for some harm that reaches Him, glory be to Him, from disobedience; and since granting respite together with challenge may sometimes be thought to stem from incapacity, He said, encouraging and warning: ﴿And your Lord﴾, that is, the One who bestows favour upon you and upon them by sending you (the Messenger), and He confined the predicate to the subject with His words: ﴿is the Self-Sufficient﴾, that is, He alone is the Absolutely Self-Sufficient, independent of every worshipper and his worship, so let the doer act for the benefit of his own self or its harm. ﴿Full of mercy﴾, that is, He alone (is so) in granting respite and sending (messengers), to draw attention to what He deserves of deeds. Since His exclusive possession of self-sufficiency and mercy means that there is no mercy except from Him and no self-sufficiency except in Him, and since He ordained reward and punishment only out of mercy and generosity from Him, He resumed explaining this, and He informed about this subject through its two attributes, according to those who make them two attributes, expressly stating what it conveys, with His words: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away﴾, that is, all of you, by annihilation, so that no one among you may think that annihilation depends on anything other than His will. Rather, He has decreed that you be granted respite until your appointed terms, out of mercy for you and as an honour to your Prophet ﷺ. Then He said, also confirming His self-sufficiency: ﴿and cause to succeed﴾

Since He has not granted immortality to anyone, He introduced the preposition and said: ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your destruction, ﴿whomever He wills﴾, that is, He will originate others of creation, of your kind [or other than your kind], just as He originated your father Adam from clay, and clay from non-existence, and brought you forth from him. ﴿as He produced you from the offspring﴾, that is, the progeny, ﴿of another people﴾, that is, after He had destroyed them all, namely the people of the Ark, and you were drops of semen in their loins, none of which contained [life].

Since it has been established that He possesses the two attributes that entail power, this produces His statement, in reply to their hasty demand for the punishment in mockery: ﴿Indeed, what you are promised﴾, that is, of the resurrection and other things, ﴿is surely coming﴾, that is, there is no escape from its occurrence, because the one who makes a threat does not have his word changed in his presence, and there is no equal to Him who could oppose Him in it. ﴿And you cannot escape﴾, that is, it is not established for you to bring about anything by which the adversary would be unable to prevail. Thus the matter is made smooth from His side and from your side, owing to the presence of the requisite cause and the absence of any impediment. In this there is an affirmation of the matter of His mercy, because the Mighty, when He wishes vengeance, seizes [the wrongdoer] while he is heedless and does not give warning; and when He wishes mercy, He precedes [the punishment] with a warning, so that the successful may take heed and the losers may submit.

Now that this threat against those who deny the Resurrection has been firmly established and clarified, and it produces in the intelligent person, necessarily, diligence in action, and since most of creation needs the counsel of His command—glory be to Him—He says in counsel: ﴿Say: O my people﴾, that is: O you who are closest of creation to me and dearest to me, and who have those who manage affairs and provide sufficiency in grave matters. ﴿Act﴾. After expressing "people" he indicated greater strength by using the particle of elevation, saying: ﴿according to your station﴾, that is: according to what you have of power to act and capacity before calamities come upon you and sudden disasters overtake you with the approach of the appointed term. In this, along with the counsel, there is a fear more severe than what came before, because a threat directed at someone present through the words of another, together with turning away, is more severe than confronting him directly with a threat. That is: if you do not accept that first threat, you are deserving of turning away and distance.

Since the most indicative thing of sincere counsel is the counselor's hastening to practice what he advises and calls to, he said, beginning a new statement or giving a reason: ﴿Indeed I am acting﴾, that is: according to my station and to the extent of my ability, before the opportunity is lost by the arrival of death. It is possible that this is purely a threat, so the meaning would be: act according to what you are now doing of opposition to me, with the utmost of the power you have; indeed I too am acting in this manner regarding what I have brought.

Since the occurrence of what is threatened is a cause for knowledge of the outcome, [and the context concerns their lack of remembrance, their delusion, and their lack of insight], the retention of the particle fa' in His words was made fitting, [rather than its omission, because the resumption inclines toward a question], so He said: ﴿Then you will come to know﴾, that is: there will happen to you, by a promise without any breach, knowledge. It is as if it were said: What knowledge? So it was said: (p-278) ﴿whose will be the final abode﴾, as a state as though he were created for it, ﴿the ultimate outcome of the abode﴾, that is: between me and you. This is with the retention of the fa', unlike what is in the story of Shu'ayb—peace be upon him—in Surah Hud—peace be upon him—[in its omission]. And since the implied sense was an answer to what had been established from their question—"the final outcome of the abode for the one who acts justly"—He resumed with His words: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾, that is: those who are deeply immersed in wrongdoing, whoever they may be, so for them there will be no final outcome of the abode. The verse is of the type of *ihtibak*: mentioning the outcome first indicates its omission second, and mentioning wrongdoing second [indicates] the omission of justice first.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 136:

When these verses were complete in their demonstration of the ugliness of their way in denying the Resurrection and the excellence of the way of Islam, presented in this wondrous style and this lofty example that is hard to reach, and concluded with the state of the wrongdoer, he began to elaborate on His saying, ﴿Shall I take other than God as a protector, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ [al-An'am: 14], in another style. He began it by explaining their wrongdoing, their ignorance and their falsehoods, as a warning about the feebleness of their minds and as a deterrent from them, through their placing things in other than their proper places, removing them from their rightful owner and attributing them to one who owns nothing, and through the killing of children, the release of cattle and other such things. So he said, linking it to ﴿And they have made the jinn partners with God﴾ [al-An'am: 100]: ﴿And they have made⦆ i.e., the polytheists who equate their Lord with idols, (p-279) ﴿for God⦆ i.e., the King Most High, for whom there is no equal, ﴿of what He has created⦆ i.e., what He has produced, originated and spread, and in whose creation none has shared with Him, ﴿of the tilth and the cattle a share⦆ i.e., and they have made for their partners a share. Since assigning a share is known only through speech, he stated its consequence: ﴿and they say⦆ i.e., with their tongues, after having said it in their hearts, ﴿This is for God⦆ i.e., the King Most High, ﴿by their claim⦆ i.e., their false assertion, and their conduct through the lie of their claim to dedicate it to God. Therefore he dropped the claim from His saying: ﴿and this is for our partners⦆ i.e., they have no authority in this division except their own desires.

Since this was foolishness, by equating one who owns nothing with One who owns everything, he explained from their conduct what is even more foolish than it, by elaborating on what the expression "claim" had hinted at. So he said, stating its consequence and branching from it: ﴿Then what is for their partners⦆ i.e., by their claim that they are partners, ﴿does not reach God⦆ i.e., the One who is the Owner, together with His attributes of majesty and beauty, ﴿and what is for God⦆ i.e., in accordance with His greatness, magnificence, majesty and might, ﴿reaches their partners⦆. So when what they had designated for their partners was lost, or the harvest failed while what was for God increased, they said: "Our gods have no choice but to have provision," and they took from what was for God and spent it on their gods. And when what was for God failed while what was for their gods increased, they said: "If God had willed, He would have increased it," and so they did not return anything to Him from what belonged to the gods.

When this reached the extreme of foolishness, He said: ﴿Evil is what they judge⦆ i.e., this judgment of theirs is the worst of judgments. Imam Abu al-Rabi' Sulayman ibn Salim al-Kala'i mentioned in his sirah (biography of the Prophet), in the delegation of Khawlan, that they had an idol called "Amm Anas." When they came as a delegation to the Prophet (ﷺ), they told him that they used to assign a portion of their livestock and crops to it and a portion to God, by their claim. They said: "We would sow the crop and set aside its middle for it and name it for it, and name another crop a sanctuary for God, Mighty and Majestic. When the wind blew what we had named for God onto what we had designated for Amm Anas, we left it for Amm Anas, and when the wind blew what we had designated for Amm Anas onto what was for God, we did not return it to God." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) told them that God, Mighty and Majestic, had revealed concerning this ﴿And they have made for God⦆ and the verse. They said: "We used to bring our disputes to it and it would speak." So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: (Those are the devils speaking to you). They said: "Then we came in the morning to the Messenger of God, and our hearts knew that it did not harm nor benefit, and that it did not know of its worshippers from those who did not worship it." Ibn Hisham said in the introduction to the sirah that they would make a division for it: whatever entered into the share of Amm Anas from the share of God that they had designated for it, they left for it, and whatever entered into the share of God from the share of Amm Anas, they returned it to it. He said: they were a clan of Khawlan called al-Adim. Abd al-Razzaq said in his tafsir: Ma'mar informed us from Qatadah, who said: They would set aside some of their wealth and say: "This is for God, and this is for our idols." If something from what they had assigned to their partners was lost and became mixed with what they had assigned to God, they returned it. But if something from what they had assigned to God was lost and became mixed with what they had assigned to their partners, they left it. And if a year of drought struck them, they ate from what they had assigned to God and left what they had assigned to their partners. So God, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Evil is what they judge⦆. Al-Baghawi said: They would assign to God a share of their crops, livestock, fruits and all their other wealth, and to the idols a share. Whatever they assigned to God they gave to guests and the needy, and whatever they assigned to the idols they spent on the idols and their attendants. If something of what they had assigned to God fell into the share of the idols, they left it and said: "God is independent of this." But if something of the share of the idols fell into what they had assigned to God, they returned it to the idols and said: "They are in need." If something of what they had assigned to God was lost or diminished, they did not care; but if something of what they had assigned to the idols was lost or diminished, they made it up from what they had assigned to [God].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 137:

Since this (the matter just mentioned) implies that they wasted their own wealth without any benefit, giving it to those who do not deserve it, He (Exalted is He) drew attention to the fact that this was the adornment of those devils who led them astray, from among the guardians of the idols (sadana al-asnam) and others from mankind, and from among the jinn who speak from within the bellies of the idols and others. So He said, alerting to the fact that they made attractive to them something even more evident than that: ﴿And thus﴾, that is: and in the same way as their partners made attractive to all the polytheists the squandering of their wealth and disbelief in their Lord, ﴿their partners made attractive to many of the polytheists﴾.

Since the one who adorns (the act) is by his baseness fit not to have his adornment accepted nor to be paid heed, the obeying of his command was strange, and undertaking the act he adorned was even stranger; so He placed it first, drawing attention to this, and said: ﴿the killing of their children﴾, that is: by burying them alive out of fear of poverty, and by slaughtering them for their gods. How far apart is the one who brings about for them the child and provides for him and the sustenance and creates him, from the one who is only a cause for his annihilation! And since in this there is the utmost strangeness, the soul yearned to know the doer of the adornment, so He said: ﴿their partners﴾, that is: and they are less than them in that they are addressed from within the bellies of the idols, and in that the guardians and the desires (al-ahwiya) embellish for them by means of the idols.

Since this is a wondrous matter, the reading of Ibn 'Amir, who was born in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), who was blessed by that age, who took knowledge from a host of the Companions, who is described as abundant in knowledge, firm in religion, strong in memorization and precision, and a proof in transmission, made the matter more wondrous, by attributing the act to the partners through the attribution of the verbal noun to its doer, and separating the genitive construct from its second term by the object, which is the children, because the occurrence of the killing among them, as mentioned before, is more wondrous.

Since this might have been for some benefit for which this great act was made light, He mentioned that it has no benefit except destruction in this world and in religion, which is destruction in the Hereafter, so that this would be more wondrous, and so He said: ﴿to ruin them﴾, that is: to destroy them with a destruction having no benefit whatsoever. ﴿And to confuse for them their religion﴾, that is: to mix it up and make it resemble, namely the religion of Ibrahim, whom God commanded to sacrifice his son Isma'il (peace be upon them both), so he undertook it only by the command of God; then He ransomed him and did not carry out the slaughter. So these people opposed the command of the partners in both matters together, and thereby combined for them two destructions: of the soul and of the religion. For killing in itself is very great, and its occurrence as an act of piety without any root or doubt is greater still. So none is more astray than one who follows the one who was the cause of destroying his own self and religion.

Since the Arabs claim sharp minds, clear thoughts, correct opinions, and abundant, penetrating intellects, He mentioned this to them by way of causation, mocking them; meaning: they did this for this reason, and they did not perceive them (the partners) nor realize what they intended for you, even though they are stones; so you are lower than them. And since He attributed to the partners an act which is adornment, and had previously negated from them and from all the enemies of the prophets independent power to do it, and had there attached the matter to the attribute of lordship, which requires protection and care (because the context was about the enemies), here, since the discourse concerns specifically the partners, He attached the matter to the Name of the Essence, which indicates perfection that requires greatness, majesty, pride, and all the Most Beautiful Names, in a manner of comprehensiveness and splendour, and so He said: ﴿Had God willed﴾, that is: by His greatness, and His encompassing of all attributes of perfection that require exaltation above rivals and transcendence above partners and offspring, that the polytheists would not do it ﴿they would not have done it﴾, that is: that which was made attractive to them. Rather, that is only by His will and His decree, to guard against the thought that they have power over anything independently, and as consolation to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and as relief, and He emphasized the consolation by His saying: ﴿So leave them and what they fabricate﴾, that is: what they invent of falsehood and deliberately intend.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 6, verse 138:

When He mentioned their audacity regarding what the Sharia (shar', the revealed law) had made abhorrent, and when reason (al-'aql) blamed them for their disapproval of the killing of children, He followed this with their reluctance regarding what the Sharia had deemed good, namely the slaughter of some livestock for their benefit. He also added a group of things that they forbade themselves and adhered to merely out of their own whims. So He said: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, the polytheists, out of folly and ignorance, ﴿"These"﴾, a reference to a portion of their wealth that they had designated for their deities, ﴿"are cattle and tilth, forbidden"﴾, that is, prohibited and placed off-limits, so that no one may partake of them. This is a description that is used identically for the singular and plural, the masculine and feminine, because its ruling is that of nouns rather than adjectives. ﴿"None shall eat of them"﴾, that is, none shall eat from them ﴿"except whom we will"﴾, that is, from among the custodians (al-sadanah) and their like ﴿"by their claim"﴾, that is, by their assertion, based merely on whim, without any authority (sanad) from God, to whom belongs the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth. They are lying in this claim, both regarding the origin of the prohibition and regarding the validity of the restriction. Had God willed that they be eaten, they would have been eaten, and they would not have been able to prevent it. ﴿And cattle﴾

Since their blame was for the mere act of prohibition and not for it being of a specific [animal], the verb of His saying ﴿"Whose backs are forbidden"﴾ is in the passive voice (mabni lil-majhul). That is, the she-camels (al-baha'ir) and what is with them, so they are not ridden. ﴿"And cattle over which they do not mention the name of God"﴾, that is, these who fabricate against God, ﴿"the name of God"﴾, who possesses all greatness, ﴿"over them"﴾, that is, in slaughter or otherwise, ﴿"in fabrication"﴾, that is, deliberately lying ﴿"against Him"﴾.

Since this, given its gravity, involves deliberately lying against the King of kings, it [occupies the position of] arousing the listener's eagerness to know what its consequence will be. So He began a new statement: ﴿"He will repay them"﴾, that is, with a true promise that admits no failure, ﴿"for what"﴾, that is, for the cause of what ﴿"they"﴾ were, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿"used to fabricate"﴾, that is, they deliberately and intentionally lied. As for after the truth has been made manifest, this is clear; and as for before it, it is because it was at the utmost extent of the manifestation of corruption.

When He mentioned from their folly what was pure rashness and what was pure reluctance, He followed it with what is a mixture of both, saying: ﴿And they say﴾, i.e., the polytheists, or some of them, and the rest approved it. ﴿What is in the wombs of these﴾ [a reference to what they set apart for their gods, and which they explained by their saying]: ﴿cattle﴾, i.e., of the embryos, ﴿is exclusively﴾, i.e., an exclusivity with no admixture in it. The feminine form is used in agreement with the sense of "embryos"; or the ta' is for emphasis; or it is a verbal noun like "al-'afiyah," i.e., possessor of exclusivity. ﴿for our males﴾. Since the intended meaning is nobility in every attribute, he used the conjunction waw and said: ﴿and forbidden﴾, and he dropped the ha' either by taking the wording as the basis or for the sake of precision, since what is meant by "exclusive" is emphasis. ﴿upon our wives﴾, i.e., our females. It seems he expressed it with "wives" to clarify the locus of the folly, by making them the equals of the men. This applies if it is born alive. ﴿And if it be﴾, i.e., what is in their wombs, ﴿dead﴾. It seems he affirmed the feminine ta' for emphasis. Abu Ja'far, Ibn 'Amir and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim made the verb feminine, taking the sense of "ma" [what]. Ibn Kathir, Abu Ja'far and Ibn 'Amir read the noun in the nominative as a complete clause, and Ibn Kathir mentioned that the feminine is not real [gender]. The rest read it in the accusative, treating it as a defective predicate with the masculine form, taking the wording of "ma" as the basis. ﴿then they﴾, i.e., their males and their females, ﴿are partners in it﴾, i.e., in that which is in the wombs, ﴿equal partners﴾, i.e., on an equal footing.

Since all of this was a description from them of things placed outside the places that God loves, He said: ﴿He will repay them for their description﴾, i.e., by placing painful punishment in every place they dislike their description to be in, so that it becomes like their description, which they never ceased to follow desire in, until it became a firm disposition for them; so He shows them the grim consequence of it. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿Indeed He is Wise﴾, i.e., He recompenses for nothing except with its like, and places it in the most rightful and most just of its places. ﴿Knowing﴾, i.e., of the equivalence and who deserves it, and in what manner it is done, and in what way it is most complete and perfect. In this there is a most complete indication that these things are at the utmost remove from wisdom, so He is exalted above having legislated them, when they are pure folly that none does except a wrongdoing ignoramus.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 140:

When Allah, exalted is He, had mentioned the details of their foolishness and alluded to their meanings, He gathered them together and stated the outcome of loss they produced, in seven characteristics, each of which is a complete cause for the arising of regret. So He said: ﴿Certainly, those have lost who killed their children out of foolishness﴾. He used the apparent noun in place of the pronoun, to generalize and to attach the ruling to the description, so He said: ﴿those who killed﴾. Ibn 'Amir and Ibn Kathir read it with the intensive form (qattalu, with shaddah), for the sake of indicating multiplicity, while the rest read it with the light form (qatalu). ﴿Their children, out of foolishness﴾, meaning: out of lightness of mind (safah, "lightness, folly") toward the blameworthy act and recklessness, which the devils, who speak through the tongues of the idols or their servants, goad them toward with a strong urging.

Since foolishness is contrary to the sobriety of knowledge, an action arising from which can only come from deliberation, reflection, thought and insight, He stated explicitly what had been implied, saying: ﴿without knowledge﴾, meaning: as for one who kills his child with knowledge, such as when he is an unbeliever, or a murderer, or a married adulterer, his ruling is not like that.

When He had mentioned the grave magnitude of what they undertook, He mentioned the noble side of what they refrained from, saying: ﴿and have forbidden what Allah has provided for them﴾, meaning: which the One who has no sovereign other than Him has provided out of mercy for them, from those livestock and grains, without any legislation and without any benefit in any way, ﴿as a fabrication﴾, meaning: a deliberate lie ﴿against Allah﴾, meaning: to whom belongs all greatness.

Since they had lost three losses while claiming the utmost insight into trade, the loss of the self through killing children, and the loss of wealth through forbidding what Allah had provided for them, and this brought them the loss of religion, its result was His saying: ﴿They have certainly gone astray﴾, meaning: they exceeded bounds, deviated from the truth and transgressed. Since one who is astray may have his straying be an occasional lapse befalling him, while guidance may be a settled quality in him, He alerted that straying is their established description by His saying: ﴿and were not guided﴾, meaning: in any part of this, of any of the morals, ﴿guided﴾, meaning: guidance was not a characteristic of their being; rather, they increased in straying through this.

Al-Bukhari said in (al-Manaqib) of his Sahih: Abu al-Nu'man narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from Abi Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: "If it pleases you to know the ignorance of the Arabs, then recite what is beyond the hundred and thirtieth verse in Surah al-An'am: ﴿Certainly, those have lost who killed their children out of foolishness﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and were not guided﴾." And he has in the Book of Campaigns, in the delegation of Banu Hanifa, from Mahdi ibn Maymun, who said: I heard Abu Raja' al-'Utaridi say: "We used to worship stones. When we found a stone better than it, we would throw away the first and take the other. If we found no stone, we would gather a heap of dust, then bring a sheep and milk over it, then circumambulate it. When the month of Rajab came, we would say: 'The Stripper of Spear-Points,' and we would not leave any spear with iron on it or any arrow with iron on it without pulling it out and casting it away [during the month of Rajab]."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 141:

Since the Qur'an revolves around establishing *tawhid* (the Oneness of God), *nubuwwah* (prophethood) and its corollaries, *ma'ad* (the Return), *qada'* and *qadar* (divine decree and predestination), and action by choice (*al-fi'l bil-ikhtiyar*), and since it perfected the establishment of these foundations, especially in this surah, and came to an end with explaining the states of the blessed and the wretched, and since He, glorified is He, marvelled at those who associated partners with God, denied the Resurrection, and committed the deeds of the polytheists, marvelling after marvelling, and disparaged their way and rebuked them, rebuke upon rebuke, for denying the caller without any proof, and related their false sayings and corrupt claims, together with their claim that they are (p-٢٨٩) the most just of people; and their opposition to the Guide without firm ground or clear evidence, together with their claim that they are the most perceptive of people; and their seeking of signs out of obstinacy, together with their claim that they are the most intelligent of people; and their sincerity in hardship and their association of partners in ease, together with their claim that they are the most thankful of people; and their worship of the jinn and their seeking refuge with them, together with their claim that they are the most courageous of people; up to the point where He marvelled at them for what they legislated for themselves regarding what He had provided them of livestock and produce, and they persisted in it, generation after generation, as a sign of the weakness of their minds and the scantiness of their knowledge, in order to repel people from paying heed to them and from being deceived by their sayings, He said, in the context of the situation:

﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle﴾ [al-An'am: 136], making clear His immense dominion, the all-encompassing scope of His power, His manifest choice and His greatness, as an added marvelling at them for their disposing of His dominion without His permission, [glorified is He], and their legislating what He had not permitted, in a context that secures the establishment of proof for establishing tawhid, returning to the beginning and to the cause after the effect; for this is the greatest axis and the most upright foundation: ﴿And He﴾, that is, none other than Him, ﴿is the One who brought into being﴾, that is, from nothingness, ﴿gardens﴾, that is, of grapes and others, ﴿trellised and untrellised﴾ [i.e., raised above the ground on wood and the like], that is, they cannot thrive except trellised, and if they are not raised above the ground their fruit perishes; ﴿and untrellised﴾, that is, not raised on wood, meaning they cannot thrive except spread on the ground, weighed down by something that secures their reaching it, and if they are lifted from the ground (p-٢٩٠) they perish. So that is not due to nature or anything else; otherwise all the gardens would be alike, since their relation to the sky and the earth is one. Their difference is therefore only due to a single, choosing agent with no partner, who brings about only what He wills.

Having mentioned the comprehensive gardens, He singled out the most excellent of them [and the most indicative of action by choice, and He began with the most familiar of them to those addressed by these verses], so He said: ﴿And the palm-tree﴾, that is, and He brought into being the palm-tree, ﴿and the field-crop﴾, being ﴿of diverse produce﴾, that is, the produce of one of the two kinds, namely its fruit which is eaten, in relation to the other; and the produce of each kind in relation to trees and others in bearing and taste and so on. Indeed, diversity is found even within a single cluster; as for the diversity of size, with one being extremely tall and another extremely short, that is quite evident. ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate﴾

[Since the main aim of this context is the negation of partners and the affirmation of action by choice, the situation did not call for mention of complete resemblance, so it sufficed with the basic act and it was said]: ﴿similar﴾, that is, likewise, ﴿and dissimilar﴾, that is, in colour, taste, spoiling or not spoiling, being eaten as fruit or as staple, oiliness and water, and so on, of other states and qualities which none can comprehend in full except their Creator, glorified is He and exalted is His majesty. Perhaps He combined the first two because each of them is stored for food and does not spoil quickly, despite differing in form, and differing in kind by tree and by stone, and the great disparity in size; and the last two because the first does not spoil at all and the second spoils quickly, and each is stored in a manner other than that in which the other is stored, although both are of trees, close in size, and their fruits differ in shape, measure and other respects.

Since His saying ﴿And He it is who sends down water from the sky﴾ [al-An'am: 99] was in the context of proving that there is no agent but God, He there commanded consideration of the fruit and its ripening, so that their state might be taken as a lesson. This verse, however, was in the context of rebuking those who forbade what God had provided, and of commanding eating of the lawful of what He had bestowed and forbidding abandoning it out of pious pretence. So He, exalted is He, said here: ﴿Eat﴾, and He put first the first [verse], whose evidence establishes the existence of the Originator and His sole disposal of affairs, since belief in that is a spiritual, everlasting felicity. Abu Hayyan said in (*al-Nahr*): Since the occurrence of that verse was in the setting of proof by it for the Creator and His power, for the Gathering and for the return of spirits to bodies after nonexistence, and for the bringing forth of the body and its formation from the decayed [bone], which is the coccyx, He said ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening﴾ [al-An'am: 99], as an indication of its bringing into being [first] and of its end. Here, however, since it was in the setting of favour and the display of kindness through what He created for us, He said: [Eat], and He indicated that provision is more than creation by His saying ﴿of its fruit﴾. And since this command is for permission, not for requirement, He restricted it, lest it imply the production of fruit in every garden at every time, so He said: ﴿when it bears fruit﴾. Thus by the whole of these there is achieved everlasting life and the life of this world, which is swift to end; and sight, which is reflection, was placed before eating for this reason. End of quotation. He expressed it with ﴿when﴾ rather than ﴿if﴾, to affirm people's hope for abundance and to calm their hopes, out of mercy and gentleness towards them, informing them that if drought occurs it will be in one region and not another, and in one kind and not another; and as permission to eat in all states of the fruit, whether ripe or unripe.

Since the verses reporting the doctrines of the unbelievers contain a censure of their setting aside a portion of their wealth for someone by their own whims, He indicated here that He had imposed upon it a right and made for it allocations, by His saying: ﴿and give its due﴾. Since He, glorified is He, had permitted its eating from the outset and to the end, He made clear that He had lightened the obligation for them before the end, so He said: ﴿on the day of its harvest﴾, that is, its cutting, whether gathering it piecemeal or by harvesting. So likewise the first time of the due of the command is wide, and the right is more general than the obligatory and the recommended. If recommendation is meant, it includes the five kinds mentioned before: the grapes indicated by the trellis and what follows it. If obligation is meant, then by the expression "harvest" it is indicated that the principal matter in this is the staple grains, while others follow, their knowledge coming through the explanation of the Prophet (ﷺ), so the term "harvest" is applied to them figuratively.

Since God had commanded eating of its fruit and giving its due, He forbade exceeding the limit in extending or withholding, so He said: ﴿and do not be wasteful﴾. This prohibition includes all instances of wastefulness, so it enters into it: wastefulness in eating the fruit to the point that nothing of it remains for the zakat; and wastefulness in charity to the point of leaving nothing for oneself or one's dependants, (p-٢٩٣) and this is confirmed by ﴿And eat and drink, but do not be wasteful﴾ [al-A'raf: 31] and ﴿Do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched﴾ [al-Isra': 29]. Then He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the wasteful﴾, that is, He does not treat them as one treats a beloved, so He does not honour them. It was said to Hatim al-Ta'i: "There is no good in extravagance," and he replied: "And no extravagance in good."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 142:

Since the context concerns what is eaten of the tillage and the livestock, of lawful and unlawful, and he has finished establishing the matter of the tillage, which he mentioned in the first sentence because it is the material of animals, he said: ﴿And of the livestock﴾, meaning: and He produced from the livestock ﴿burden-bearers﴾, meaning: that which carries loads, ﴿and carpets﴾, meaning: that which is spread out for slaughter or for breeding, and carpets are made from its wool and hair. Since he had completed the two divisions, he commanded eating from all of that in a manner that includes others, in opposition to the disbelievers, saying: ﴿Eat of what Allah has provided you﴾, meaning: because He is the Supreme King, whose gift may not rightly be rejected. ﴿And do not follow﴾ [perhaps he intensified it to indicate pardon for a minor lapse, for when a person is reminded of it he returns and does not persist in his desire] ﴿the steps of Satan﴾, meaning: his path in declaring things lawful and unlawful, as He said in al-Baqarah: ﴿Eat of what is in the earth, lawful and good, and do not follow the steps of Satan﴾ [al-Baqarah: 168]. He expressed it this way because it, along with being from the material of sin, indicates that his laws are laws of effacement; were it not for the extra attention of the wicked in following every step at the moment of its effect, its erasure would hasten toward it, because of its invalidity in itself, so there is no command from Allah that gives it life, nor a Book that preserves it. He omitted here "lawful and good" because it was explained earlier in His saying ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 118], and ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 121], and later in His saying: ﴿Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾ [al-An'am: 145]. Then he gave the reason for the prohibition against following him, saying: ﴿Indeed, he is to you an enemy﴾, meaning: therefore he does not command you to good ﴿clear﴾, meaning: manifest in enmity, because his affair with your father is well known.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 143:

When he refuted the religion of the polytheists and established His own religion, and they had made distinctions regarding prohibition with respect to the males and females of humankind, he obliged them to make the same distinctions regarding the males and females of cattle. So he explained the matter in a style that made clear that their act is weak in strength, flimsy in texture, and far from the law of wisdom; it is therefore a subject for mockery and fit for scorn. He said, as an explanation of ﴿burden-animals and carpets﴾ [al-An'am: 142], ﴿eight pairs﴾, that is, kinds, none of which is complete except with its other. He produced them by the pairing of each of the male and the female with the other, and their naming of a single one as a "pair" (zawj) — on condition that it has another of its own kind — is attached to their naming of the glass a "cup" (ka's) on condition that there is wine in it.

Since the word "zawj" (pair) applies to two and to what has with it another of its own kind, he said, clarifying that this is what is meant and not merely two, specifying these eight: ﴿of the sheep﴾, the plural of ḍā'in and ḍā'inah, like ṣāḥib and ṣaḥb (companion and companions), ﴿two﴾, that is, a male and a female: a ram and a ewe. ﴿And of the goats﴾, the plural of mā'iz and mā'izah, like khādim and khadam (servant and servants) in the reading of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir, and tājir and tajar (merchant and merchants) in the reading of others, ﴿two﴾, that is, two pairs, male and female: a he-goat and a she-goat.

Since it was as if it were said, "What is meant by this distinction?" before they were asked about their religion, he said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to them, interrogating; and since this interrogation carries the meaning of rebuke, scorn and denial, he used in it ﴿am﴾ together with the hamza preceding it, in the sense of "which," so that by it one may inquire about what is known to be established in part while only its specification is sought. He said, interjecting between the enumerated items as an emphasis of the rebuke, because interjections are only introduced for emphasis: ﴿the two males?﴾

Since the one asked about is determined by the word after it and not by what precedes it, he said: ﴿Has forbidden﴾, that is, Allah. If that is the case, it would oblige you to forbid all males ﴿or the two females?﴾, so as to oblige you to forbid all females. He comprehended all that could be supposed among the remaining divisions in His words: ﴿Or what﴾, that is, or has He forbidden what ﴿the wombs of the two females contain﴾, that is, what is combined in and carried by the wombs of the females, of males and females. And if that is the case, it would oblige you to forbid everything, and then you would not be bound by anything that this division requires, so you would not be walking according to any order.

Since he knew that they have no order, and therefore knew that they deserve rebuke, he increased their rebuke and said: ﴿Inform me﴾, that is, tell me what Allah has forbidden of this, a great and magnificent information. And since this described information cannot be about anything in which there is doubt, he said: ﴿with knowledge﴾, that is, with a matter known from Allah, about which there is no reproach, ﴿if you are truthful﴾, that is, if you possess this attribute.

When he distinguished the goats into sheep and goats, that made it unnecessary to specify the camels as one-humped (*ʿirab*) and two-humped (*bukht*), or the cattle as Arabian (*ʿirab*) and water buffalo (*jawamis*). [ - And because these animals interbreed with one another, unlike goats, for neither kind of goat mates with the other - this was transmitted by Shaykh Badr al-Din al-Zarkashi in the *Kitab al-Wasaya* of his commentary on *al-Minhaj*, from *Kitab al-A'dad* by Ibn Suraqa. ] He said: ﴿And of camels, two﴾, meaning a male and a female. ﴿And of cattle, two﴾, meaning likewise. ﴿Say﴾, meaning to these people who invented these claims out of ignorance and foolishness, what has been mentioned of them: ﴿Is it the two males that He has forbidden, or the two females?﴾, meaning of these two kinds. ﴿Or what the wombs of the two females contain?﴾, meaning, that which, according to your claim, is forbidden, [namely] the wombs of the two females, which God has forbidden.

Since the implied meaning is: "Has this come to you from God, whose command is for none other, through the tongue of a prophet?", He balanced it with a rebuke and denunciation of them by saying: ﴿Or were you witnesses﴾, meaning present, ﴿when God enjoined this upon you﴾, meaning God, who has no sovereignty other than His, so that there is no command for anyone besides Him, ﴿this﴾, meaning as you have firmly asserted it, or you have firmly asserted the prohibition of what you have forbidden and the permissibility of what you have made lawful, while there is no one who forbids or makes lawful apart from God. By this you were attributing the ruling to Him. Since the implied meaning, as the context yields, is: "You have indeed lied against God by attributing to Him what you did not take from Him, neither through an intermediary nor without one," He made the following statement a consequence of it. (p-297) Generalizing so that it may be known that when this lying concerns prohibition and permission, lying about the foundations of the religion is even graver, He said: ﴿Who is more unjust﴾, and in place of "from among you" He put, generalizing and attaching the judgment to a description: ﴿than one who fabricates﴾, meaning deliberately ﴿against God﴾, meaning Him than whom there is none greater, because He is the King of kings, ﴿a lie﴾, like ʿAmr ibn Luhayy, who altered the law of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and everyone who does the like of his deed.

Since their legislation in these matters necessarily leads to the misguidance of those who follow them from the straight path, and since they used to claim that they were the most astute of people and the most knowledgeable of the subtleties of matters at their beginnings and their ends and what follows from them, He made the ultimate aim of their deed an intended purpose for them, mocking them, and said: ﴿in order to mislead people﴾. And since misguidance may occur even from a learned guide by error, He said: ﴿without knowledge﴾.

Since this was a matter of wonder regarding one who does this, He exposed it, glorified is He, by saying, as a resumption: ﴿Indeed God﴾, who has no command for anyone besides Him, ﴿does not guide them﴾. This was the original form, but He instead made the statement more general by using a designation broader than their description, so that the judgment against them would apply all the more, and He said: ﴿Indeed God does not guide the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning those who place things in other than their proper places. How then about those who are most unjust! How excellent is this conclusion for their rulings, and how fitting it is for what they were built upon, from His statement: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not prosper﴾ [al-Anʿam: 135].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 145 (part 1 of 2):

When His saying ﴿fabricating against Him﴾ [al-An'am: 138] included "fabricating against Allah," and the expression throughout all of this used the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam, the Supreme Name), this indicated that the prohibition comes only from Allah is a matter known with certainty and is not open to doubt, because He is the Supreme King, and there is no ruling except that of the King. Whoever rules without His command is punished. It was fitting, after refuting their religion [and clarifying that whoever prohibits something by mere whim is misguided and a wrongdoer], that His saying, explaining the correct account of what is lawful and unlawful, should come as an answer to someone who says: "What has He prohibited, glorified is He, and what has He permitted?" ﴿Say﴾, informing that prohibition is not established except by revelation [from] Allah: ﴿I do not find﴾, meaning now or in the future, since (lā, "not") is a particle that does not enter upon the present tense except with the meaning of the future: ﴿in what﴾.

Since what was given to him (ﷺ) had been established as from Allah by their inability to produce its equal, He said in the passive voice: ﴿has been revealed to me﴾, meaning, from the Qur'an and the Sunnah, something of what has preceded, of what you have prohibited, either absolutely or in one state and not another, and for some people and not others: food ﴿forbidden to an eater﴾, meaning an eater, whether male or female, ﴿who eats it﴾, meaning who consumes it, by eating, drinking, as medicine, or otherwise. ﴿Unless it be﴾, meaning that food, ﴿carrion﴾, meaning legally: the legal carrion (maytah) is what does not accept ritual slaughter (tadhkiyah, the lawful slaughter), [and it is whatever has lost its life without lawful slaughter]. ﴿Or blood poured forth﴾, meaning spilled, of a kind that by nature flows and not that which by nature congeals, such as the liver and the spleen.

Since the Christians had taken eating pork as a religion, He specified it, although it falls within His saying "carrion," according to what I have established regarding its meaning, and He said (p-299): ﴿or the flesh of swine﴾, so as to convey its prohibition in every state, whether it is slaughtered or not. Had He said "or a swine" it could have been understood to mean only the prohibition of what is taken from it while alive. He said: ﴿for indeed it﴾, meaning the swine, ﴿is an abomination (rijs)﴾, so as to convey the impurity of its very substance while it is alive. Its flesh and all its other parts are thus included by a fortiori reasoning. [Whatever shares this cause is impure. The pronoun does not return to the flesh, because its impurity is already known from its prohibition as such; if it returned to it, it would be a repetition.]

Having mentioned what is prohibited in itself, He mentioned what is prohibited due to an external cause, and so He said, emphasizing its negation by making it the very meaning for which the prohibition was issued: ﴿or a transgression (fisq)﴾, meaning, or the food is a departure from that wherein one should dwell, from the vast courts of Allah, whoever takes up residence there is secure and guided and safe from the narrowness of desire, whereas whoever goes out toward other than Him fears, strays, perishes, and is destroyed. Then He said, explaining it [advancing what falls under transgression from turning to other than Allah]: ﴿what has been dedicated to other than Allah﴾, meaning to the One to whom belongs everything, because to Him belongs all perfection, ﴿by it﴾, meaning that over it other than His name has been invoked, by slaughtering for it as an act of worship.

Then He mentioned His kindness to this Community by permitting, in a state of necessity, every prohibited thing, as a mercy from Him to them and a covering for their shortcomings. So He said: ﴿But whoever is compelled﴾, meaning, one who has come to experience hunger that he fears will destroy him. It is expressed in the passive voice because what matters is the occurrence of necessity, not that it is caused by a specific person. From this expression is derived the prohibition of what exceeds the satisfaction of the throat's hunger (p-300), because beyond that one is no longer in necessity. ﴿Neither desiring (bāghin)﴾, meaning, aggressing against others through deception, ﴿nor transgressing (ʿādin)﴾, meaning, wronging others by one's strength, nor exceeding the limit of necessity. ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, meaning the One who has been good to you by sending you and to your weak community by making its religion the upright, tolerant ḥanīfiyyah, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, meaning He erases sin when He wills, ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning He honors the sinner after forgiveness with various kinds of honors. He is therefore worthy of erasing from this one in necessity the effect of that prohibition which troubled him, and of honoring him by granting him, in his preserving himself thereby, if his intention is sound, a great reward. The verse, despite its brevity, has encompassed all prohibited foods, together with an allusion through the words rijs and fisq to all categories of prohibitions, and to the fact that committing them entails corruption and detachment from goodness, and that this is the reason for their prohibition. Al-Ustadh Abu al-Hasan al-Harrali said in his book al-ʿUrwah: The purpose of the sending down of this letter, that is, the letter of the forbidden (ḥarām), is the purification of creation from the harms to their bodies, the filth of their souls, and the ignorance of their hearts. Whatever combines these qualities is more strictly forbidden, and whatever contains some of them is forbidden in proportion to the urgency of its need for purification. Just as the conditions of the children of Adam differ according to the differences of their clay, between the wicked and the good and what lies between, so too their conditions differ regarding what renews their creation through their sustenance. Whoever nourishes his body with something manifests in his own soul the traits and attributes of that which he has been nourished by, and there results either rust upon the heart or clarity, because of its strengthening by what has been named over it of the remembrance of Allah, or of disbelief in Him (p-301) by the mention of another. The one who gathers the revelation's descent to its limit, by excepting the little from the wide expanse of the lawful, is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to an eater who eats it, except that it be carrion or blood poured forth﴾. This is for its harm to the body. ﴿Or the flesh of swine﴾, and this is for its corruption of the soul and its making it impure, as He, Exalted, said: ﴿for indeed it is an abomination or a transgression, dedicated to other than Allah﴾. And this is for its rust upon the heart. This verse is Medinan, and He established it in a Meccan surah to indicate that the prohibition was merited from the beginning of the religion, but was delayed until the time when Islam's main body gathered in Medina, in order to win over the hearts of the polytheists, to ease the burden on the weak of [the religion] who believed, and to suffice the believers with their own purity and avoidance of such things and what resembles them, through their own insight. To such an extent that al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) had prohibited wine for himself in the time of ignorance (jāhiliyyah), because he saw in it the loss of reason. How then will it be with their state after Islam! Added to these in the surah "Those who believe" was what was killed by a blow without the mention of Allah over it: the strangled, the beaten, the fallen, the gored, and what a beast of prey has eaten, except what is reached and ritually slaughtered in a manner that makes the blood flow, which causes prohibition because its spilled blood has been corrupted by something exceeding the limit of food at its beginning and by parts retained at its end, which by the blessing of the invocation of the name were rendered clean from the effect of the sudden blow that struck them. Also added to these in this surah (p-302) is the prohibition of wine for its filth, like swine, just as the dead animal was joined to carrion. And just as Allah prohibited what contains the essence of filth, namely swine, and the essence of sin, namely wine, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prohibited whatever had a share of these. He added to swine the beasts of prey, as a protection against the fury of their anger, because of the severe harm in the manifestation of anger among the servants, for it is fit only for their master. He prohibited domestic donkeys as a protection against their stupidity and their ḥirān, which is the knowledge of the natural instinct of foolishness in creation. The Prophet (ﷺ) also joined to the prohibition of wine, whose intoxication is natural, the prohibition of every intoxicant whose intoxication is manufactured. And just as Allah prohibited what deceives the servant outwardly and inwardly, He prohibited for him, in what lies between him and Himself, what cuts him off from Him, namely eating usury (ribā). [Usury] has seventy-some gates, and polytheism is like that. The one who gathers its prohibition in His saying: ﴿Those who consume usury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275], up to His saying: ﴿Allah has permitted trade and forbidden usury﴾ [al-Baqarah: 275], up to the end of its mention, encompassing what is included in it, in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume usury, doubled and redoubled﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 130], the verse, and what is joined to it in His saying: ﴿and what you give as usury﴾ [al-Rum: 39], the verse. He said: this verse is Medinan. Although I have not seen this from anyone else, it is problematic in light of His saying: ﴿And He has already explained to you what He has forbidden to you﴾ [al-An'am: 119], the verse.

(p-303) Since the prohibition of usury is between the Lord and the servant, it carries a threat, a declaration of war from Allah and His Messenger. For this reason the imams protected its means with the strictest protection. The most stringent of them in this was the scholar of Medina, to the extent that he protected against even its appearance out of confidence in the soundness of the inner heart, while acting contrary to that in the prohibitions between the servant and himself. Just as Allah prohibited usury in what lies between Him and His servant from this highest aspect, so too He prohibited the consumption of wealth by falsehood in what lies between the servant and others from the lowest aspect. The one who gathers its prohibition in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not consume one another's wealth by falsehood, nor send it to the rulers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 188], the verse, up to what is included in His saying: ﴿O you who believe, do not consume one another's wealth by falsehood, except that it be trade by mutual consent among you﴾ [al-Nisa': 29], up to what is included in His saying: ﴿And give the orphans their wealth﴾ [al-Nisa': 2], the verses concerning the wealth of orphans. Thus He prohibited it from the highest, the similar, and the lowest aspects. The prohibition is organized under three principles: the aspect of what lies between Allah and His servant, the aspect of what lies between the servant and himself, and the aspect of what lies between the servant and others. These are gathered from the whole of a verse in the Qur'an, its ḥadīths in the Sunnah, and its questions in the jurisprudence of the imams. Since it has a wide scope, there have arisen, between the clear lawful and the clear unlawful (p-304), matters that are ambiguous (mutashābihāt), which many people do not know, because they resemble the lawful in one respect and the unlawful in another. Because they fall between the two, people differ about them, and about one's honor concerning the former. Through Allah's protection of His servants from the harmful consequences of the unlawful, His name al-Ṭayyib (the Good) is realized for them. Whoever does not guard himself against His prohibitions and their ambiguities is not cured by the medicine of Allah. This is wara' (scrupulous abstention), which is the foundation of the religion. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty.

Then he said, regarding what by which the recitation of the letter of the forbidden is completed in knowledge, state, and action: Know that when a human being is a comprehensive creation, there are in him two seeds: a seed of good and a seed of evil. In proportion to his purification and his freeing himself from the crowding of the plant of the seed of evil, the seed of good grows and thrives in him. Each of the two seeds has a place of growth in his body, his soul, and his heart. The first of the letters in order is action, and the foundation for what follows it is the recitation of the letter of the forbidden, so that through it the purity of the body is achieved, which is the first to exist in a human being. Whoever is nourished on the forbidden in his childhood will not be able to avoid sins in his old age, unless Allah purifies him by what He wills, through the fire of trials in this world, through illnesses and adversities. It is thus the foundation upon which the purification of the soul from prohibitions and the purification of the heart from blindness and ignorance are built. The recitation of this letter is achieved through wara', which is the barrier against what harms the body, injures the soul, what creatures dislike (p-305), and what angers the Lord. Whoever commits any of that and does not hasten to repent of it will be punished for every verse he recited while opposing its ruling. ("Whoever does not care from which gate his provision comes, Allah will not care from which gate He admits him into the Fire.")

Since wara' is outwardly the restraint of the hand from a harmful thing, and since the limbs do not move except under the influence of the soul, wara' is not valid outwardly unless there comes to the soul an inner awe from taking that thing. Since the soul is not influenced except by the heart's insight into the harmful, just as the hand does not withdraw except when the soul is repelled by what the eye perceives as filthy, even the noble soul recoils from the forbidden, as one who is fastidious recoils from what is foul.
