Thus the devourers of the forbidden are the worms of the carrion of this world, which the people of insight find repulsive, just as they find the worms of refuse heaps repulsive.

The Forbidden is that which harms the servant in his self, like carrion. For the discerning person, it is easy to keep his hand from it, because he knows its harm to his body. The same applies to flowing blood, since it is carrion by its separation from the living body and its departure from the spirit of life that mixes with it in the veins. I say: its causation will come shortly in the Torah, in a way that implies it has a greater effect on the soul and tames it by creating flesh from what is its blood. God is the Granter of success.

Likewise, what harms the body and the mind is forbidden, such as the flesh of swine, because it is *rijs* (filth, abomination). *Rijs* is the vile moral qualities which, to intelligent people, are uglier than the vile qualities of bodies. This is because whoever nourishes his body with the flesh of an animal nourishes his soul with the animal's soul-nature and with one of its characteristics. The swine's nature gathers the vices of character: refusal, greed, deceit, boldness toward what leads to his own destruction, pursuit of corruption, and absorption in whatever is in the lowest things, the signs of which appear in its creation. It has no lifting of the head as do the long-necked animals. Likewise, what harms the body and the intellect, such as wine, with its stripping of the intellect, its splitting of the head, and its inciting of enmity and hatred in the character of the soul. For this reason it is the sum of sin. So the one who is discerning about the forbidden things shuns them, because he knows their harm and injury in the present time, and their disgrace in the day of this world, along with what he has been informed of their evil consequence on the Day of Religion. Whoever drinks wine and dies without repenting of it, it is truly incumbent upon God to give him to drink from *ṭīnat al-khabāl* (the clay of the *khabāl*), which is the residue of the people of the Fire. If someone with authority threatened the drinker in this world that he would be made to drink his own urine and excrement, he would feel such dread that it would drive him to abstain from it. When one who has insight into what harms him personally becomes discerning and shuns it, out of care for his self, it is fitting for him to commit to caring for his self against whatever reaches him as a loss from another. Thus he refrains from consuming people's property wrongfully, knowing the accountability for it in the immediate and the punishment for it in the hereafter that he has been informed of. In itself it is also harmful in the present time, by his recognizing it from the sources of the Qur'an with the light of faith (p-307) ﴿Those who consume the property of orphans unjustly only consume fire into their bellies﴾ [An-Nisa: 10], even if he does not sense it. Its interpretation is not merely the promise of the Fire, because that is informing at His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will burn in a blaze﴾ [An-Nisa: 10]. Likewise, if he shuns what harms him in himself and fears what harm reaches him from others, he is even more reluctant to approach the sanctuary of what is subject to the wrath of his Lord because of it. This applies to what is forbidden to him, as protection for the greatness of His dominion and to avoid any inequality in the matter of His mercy, as in the forbidden interest. It is also due to the harm to his present time, which he restricts with faith from the definition of his Lord. For He, may He be exalted, just as He made known that eating the property of others unjustly is fire in the belly, also made known that eating interest is madness in the intellect and corruption in the soul: ﴿Those who consume interest will not stand except as one stands whom Satan has driven to madness by touch﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 275]. And greater than this is what God has forbidden: [the animal] having been stripped of His name at the taking of its life, because it is taken from other than God. What is taken from other than God, its eating is *fisq* (transgression) and *kufr* (disbelief), because it has taken the spirit from the hand of one who does not own it. For this reason the *tasmiyah* (saying the name of God) was made obligatory in *tadhkiyah* (ritual slaughter) and made recommended in other than that. So the recitation of this letter is not valid except with the insight of the heart into it, the dread of the soul from it, and the abstinence of the hand from it. Otherwise, one is among those who recite its letters but waste its limits, concerning whom the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Many of these reciters have increased—may God not increase them!" Whoever's recitation of this letter is not valid, his recitation of any other letter is not valid either, (p-308) and his worship is not valid for him. He is the one whose prayer increases him in nothing from God except distance, and whose supplication is not accepted: "A man prolongs the journey, dishevelled and dusty, raises his hands to the sky, saying: O Lord! O Lord! While his food is forbidden, his drink is forbidden, his clothing is forbidden, and he was nourished with the forbidden. So how is he to be answered?" This is the recitation of this letter and its condition. And God is the Guardian of success.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 146:

Since His saying ﴿ṭāʿimin﴾ (eater) [Q. 6:145] is an indefinite noun in a context of negation, it encompasses every eater from among the people of our law and others, and since He, glorified is He, had forbidden to the Jews things other than those already mentioned, the comprehensiveness of His knowledge required that He say, making clear the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and refuting the Jews in their saying "Allah has not forbidden us anything; we have only forbidden on ourselves what Israel forbade on himself": ﴿And to those who were Jews﴾, that is, the Jews, ﴿We forbade﴾ by the greatness which cannot be resisted ﴿every animal with claws﴾, that is, of camels, beasts of prey and birds which strengthen themselves with their claws, which is, like the finger to a human, ﴿and of cattle and sheep﴾, that is, those which are cloven-hoofed, ﴿We forbade﴾, that is, by the greatness We have, ﴿upon them their fats, the two of them﴾, that is, the two kinds. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿except what their backs have carried﴾, that is, of the fats adhering to the back and the side from the inside of their bellies, ﴿or the entrails﴾, which are the intestines that are coiled and twisted, plural of ḥawiyya, so its pattern is faʿāʾil like safīna and safāʾin; it was also said to be the plural of ḥāwiya or ḥāwiyāʾ like qāṣiʿāʾ, ﴿or what is mixed with bone﴾, that is, [of] the fats (p-309), such as the fat of the tail, for that is not forbidden. This context, with the preposition placed first and the sentence built upon it, indicates that whatever is other than the mentioned fats of the two kinds is lawful to them.

Since it was as though it were said: Why did He forbid them these good things? It is said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the great prohibition and the great recompense [which is the prohibition of the good things], ﴿We recompensed them﴾, that is, by the greatness We have, ﴿for their rebellion﴾, that is, in their affairs in which they exceeded the limits. And in placing this verse, in which is what was forbidden to the Jews, after what precedes it, together with fulfilling the purpose of restricting the forbidden foods to this nation and others, there are two great matters. One of them is the demonstration of His ﷺ awareness of the detail of what was revealed to those before him, though he had not associated with any of their followers, nor studied with a scholar, nor learned any knowledge at all; so there is no greater proof of his truthfulness about Allah than this. The second is the preference of this nation, in that He made lawful for them the impure things in cases of necessity, out of mercy toward them, and removed their harm in that state, and He did not do with them as He did with the Jews, in that He forbade them a category of good things and did not make them lawful for them in any circumstance, as a punishment for them. In that is the most complete warning to this nation not to rebel lest they be punished as those before them were punished, as He alerted to in His saying: ﴿other than those who hunt game while you are in the state of ihram﴾ [Q. 5:1]. Thus the truthfulness became manifest and the truth became clear, and no argument remained for the captious. So it is most excellent to conclude that with His saying: ﴿And indeed, We are truthful﴾, that is, Our truthfulness is established eternally and forever, as the greatness We have requires.

Its continuation with His saying, ﴿Then if﴾, meaning: and this follows from this comprehensive and concise revelation, which indicates the truth beyond any doubt, that We say that: ﴿they deny you, then say﴾. The use of the particle of doubt (in ﴿if﴾) indicates that the situation calls for it to be considered unlikely that denial would come from them after this. ﴿Your Lord﴾, meaning: the One who is good to you by making things clear and granting respite [together with every favor], ﴿Lord of vast mercy﴾, meaning: despite His power, He has decreed that He will forbear with you by granting respite until a term that He knows.

When He informed of His mercy, He highlighted the greatness of His might, saying: ﴿And His punishment will not be turned back﴾, meaning: when He wills to take vengeance, ﴿from the guilty people﴾, meaning: those who sever what should be joined. So let no one be deceived by His granting respite for their evil deeds and their confirmed misguidance. And in [this verse there is a combination of severe warning with subtle appeal to compassion, cast in] the utmost degree of eloquence.

When this had been completed, and it was known that their undertaking to make religious rulings without any proof whatsoever, the situation required that it be said: [Indeed] everything they said about prohibition has been refuted by reason and by transmission, in a way that nullifies their polytheism. Do they have any argument left? Then He, glory be to Him, reported a doubt they would voice as an excuse for their ignorance, in a way that [by itself] suffices as evidence for the truth of what he (the Messenger) conveys of the message. It thus coincided exactly with what he had said about the people of misguidance. He said, reporting what they would say before it happened, as proof of the truthfulness of His messengers and the falsehood of the polytheists in what they opposed them on: ﴿Those who associated partners [with God] will say﴾, meaning in the future. He stated explicitly the position where a pronoun could have been used, to single them out and to rebuke them, saying: ﴿Those who associated partners [with God]﴾ (p-311), as a denial from them: ﴿Had God willed﴾, meaning the One who possesses all perfection, that we not associate [partners] and not prohibit [anything]: ﴿we would not have associated [anything]﴾, meaning with an idol or anything else; ﴿nor would our fathers﴾, meaning that the association that occurred would not have occurred; ﴿nor would we have prohibited anything﴾, meaning the things previously mentioned, such as the bahira, the sa'iba, the crops and others. That is: but He did not will abandonment, and He willed the act, so we acted in accordance with His will. He wills only the truth and wisdom, because He is capable. Had it not been a truth that He approves of, He would have prevented us from it; and since He did not prevent us from it, it is true.

Since this was a manifest obstinacy on their part after the matter had become clear through the clear proofs He established for the truthfulness of His messengers, it was as if it were said, expressing wonder at them: Has anyone other than them done the like of their deed, or said the like of what they said? It was said: Yes. ﴿Likewise﴾, meaning like that denial, far from the right course: ﴿those before them denied﴾. Since the denial was not general, he introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿before them﴾, from the earlier nations, by the arguments they raised of the sort of this dispute, in their saying that if everything happens by the will of God, then the obligation [of religious duties] is pointless, so the claims of the prophets are false. This statement by the polytheists is obstinacy after the establishment of the messages through miracles and the messengers' report that He wills a thing and punishes for it, because His dominion is complete and His possession is general, so He is not questioned about what He does. Their delusion of denial carried them on ﴿until they tasted Our might﴾, meaning Our punishment, because of Our greatness; for whoever has complete command is not questioned about what He does. So their obstinacy did not benefit them when they tasted the might; rather, the resolves of their determination dissolved, and they submitted to Us and believed in Our messengers (p-312). Their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our might. The verse is of the type of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which each of two parts omits what is mentioned in the other): it mentions polytheism first as evidence of its omission second, and denial second as evidence of its omission first. The explanation will come that it is necessary for one of the two opposing groups to be misguided, even though all is by the will of God, because there is no obstacle to a matter occurring contrary to the (divine) desire.

Since what they said was a doubt far removed from knowledge, the highest level of it being that it is among the kinds of khitaba (rhetoric), which yields only conjecture regarding the greatest questions of the science of usul (the fundamentals of religion), where reliance is not permissible except upon definitive proofs, He commanded him to say to them what would alert them to this. He said: ﴿Say﴾, meaning to these who received what Satan cast to them, as indicated in Surat al-Hajj, mocking them for their distance from knowledge and their disputation after the proofs had been established: ﴿Do you have﴾, O ignorant ones, ﴿any knowledge﴾, and he went further in questioning, saying: ﴿knowledge﴾, meaning [knowledge] that can validly be used as an argument in such a constricted situation, ﴿that you can bring forth for us﴾, meaning for me and my followers, even if it is of the kind that ought to be kept hidden and guarded, withheld from those other than its people. This is mockery of them.

Since their answer to this was silence, because they had no knowledge, He said, indicating that: ﴿You follow only﴾, meaning in this statement of yours and in most of your affairs, ﴿conjecture﴾, meaning regarding the fundamentals of your religion, where no statement is permissible except with definitive proof. ﴿And you are only﴾, meaning and you are nothing but, ﴿guessing﴾, meaning you speak at times by estimation and conjecture, and at times by pure, certain falsehood (p-313).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 149:

Since it has been established that they have no proof, and it has been confirmed that the matter belongs entirely to God, it is established that He alone possesses the clear proof. Hence He says, as a consequence of this: ﴿Say: "Then to God belongs the conclusive proof."﴾ That is, to the Supreme Deity alone is the ﴿conclusive proof﴾, namely the one that has reached the highest degrees of truth in strength, firmness, clarity, lucidity and soundness, because He encompasses all knowledge and is perfect in power, as you acknowledged when you said: ﴿"Had God willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him]"﴾ [al-An'am: 148], even though you said it by way of argument and obstinacy, and not out of religious conviction and belief. ﴿So had He willed, He would have guided you all﴾, that is, you and your opponents, ﴿all of you﴾. But He did not will that; rather, He willed the guidance of some and the misguidance of others, and so it occurred in the manner He willed. It follows, according to your claim, that both groups would be right, so that one and the same thing would be true and not true in one and the same respect, and no rational person says this. It would also follow from your position that you must befriend your adversaries and not oppose them, even if they do what they do, because it is by His will and thus part of the pleasure of God; yet you do not say this. Therefore your claim is refuted. It is thus established that He may will falsehood, since He is not questioned about what He does. He sends the Messengers to you to remove [the argument] in order to establish the proof against those whom He wills to punish, in the manner that people customarily understand among themselves; and the occurrence of a command contrary to the will is not impossible.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 150:

When the truth was confirmed, the army of falsehood was broken and crushed by the nullity of all their doubts, the proofs spoke out, and the disputant was silenced, it became clear that they have no witness for their claim, because they have no truth. It was as if it were said: "Say to them: Here I am, one whose testimony is not rejected has testified for what I have said, and the One whose commendation alone is accepted has vouched for me, through this Book, whose inability to produce anything like it is itself a witness that it is His word. So do you have any witness who would be accepted?" Since they had no witness other than their own fabricators, and since the falsifier's falsehood becomes manifest under close scrutiny, by a constant practice of God, and since it becomes evident to those who are being called as witnesses, through the confusion that appears on their faces, that they are not standing on anything, He, glorified is He, commanded him to order them to summon their witnesses, so that their disgrace would appear and their shame would become famous. So He said: ﴿Say: Bring forward﴾, that is, bring them here. It is a word of summoning in which the masculine and feminine, the singular and plural, are equal according to the Hijazis (the people of the Hijaz), ﴿your witnesses﴾.

Since it was as if it were said, "What witnesses?", He said: ﴿who testify﴾, that is, who bring about testimony that ﴿God﴾, that is, the One to whom no judgment belongs but His, ﴿has forbidden this﴾, that is, what you have mentioned before. The attribution of the witnesses to them and the description of them as ﴿who﴾ is evidence that they are known and marked for supporting their creed with falsehood. Had He said "witnesses" without attribution, it would have conveyed that what is sought is someone who testifies to the truth, and that is not the case, because the rational proof has been established that they have no argument, and that the argument belongs to God in opposition to what they claimed. So it is definitively nullified that anyone could testify to that truthfully.

Since it was as if it were said: "If they are brought forward, they cannot, if they have any intellect or any shame, speak when they hear this truth," the following was built upon it: ﴿And if﴾ they brazenly ﴿testify﴾, that is, falsely and deceitfully, to that which we have refuted by definitive proofs, ﴿then do not testify with them﴾, that is, leave them and do not submit to them, for they are in error, and their testimony rests on nothing but caprice. ﴿And do not follow the desires﴾ of [those] ... He placed the explicit noun in place of the pronoun to generalize and to tie the ruling to the attribute, indicating that what leads to denial and to every ruin is only caprice, and that whoever opposes the apparent sense of the verses is only a possessor of caprice. So He said: ﴿of those who denied﴾, that is, who committed denial ﴿Our signs﴾, that is, with respect to their manifest character and their greatness, through their attribution to Us.

When He described them with denial, He followed it with the description of not believing. By the conjunction "and" He indicated the firmness of each of the two attributes, so He said: ﴿And those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, that is, which is the abode of recompense, for if they had admitted it, they would not have dared to commit wickedness, ﴿and they ascribe equals to their Lord﴾, that is, those for whom there is no blessing and no good with them except that it comes from Him alone, ﴿they make equal﴾, that is, they make others equal to Him. And they will know when they say to their associates, while they dispute in Hell: ﴿By God, we were indeed in clear error, when we made you equal to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara' 26:97-98].

[p. 316] When he had refuted their entire religion, both its foundations and its branches, concerning the forbidding of what Allah did not forbid and the association of partners with Him, and had shown its corruption through clear proofs, it was fitting that He inform them of the true religion regarding what was forbidden by the King, to whom belong creation and command, and by no one else. Forbidding belongs to none but Him. So He said: ﴿Say: Come.﴾ That is: come to me, ascending from the depths of ignorance, blind imitation, and corrupt belief to the summit of knowledge and good deeds.

The author of al-Kashshaf said: "This is one of the specific expressions that became general, so that the lower one says it to the higher one." ﴿Recite⦆ means: I recite, from tilawa (التلاوة), which is the following of some letters by others. Since the intended audience was everyone, with recitation, [but He specifically addressed those present because they believed otherwise], and since what is forbidden is more important, He placed it first and said: ﴿what your Lord has forbidden⦆ — that is, the One who benefits you by making things lawful and unlawful — ﴿to you⦆, so that He might be displeased with it from you, and what He enjoined upon you, by way of advancing and urging, He was pleased with it for you, whether concerning foundations or branches.

Then He explained the act of reciting by forbidding association, and what follows it of the content of the command is referred to through it. So He said: ﴿Do not associate anything with Him⦆, and the verses that follow. He arranged its clauses in the finest order: He began with monotheism, in explicit disavowal of association, indicating that emptying oneself of vices precedes adorning oneself with virtues, just as preventing the illness comes before the medicine. He joined to it kindness to parents, because both belong to the category of thanking the Benefactor, and to magnify the matter of disobedience to them. Then He followed it with killing, which is the greatest of the major sins after association, and He began with killing one's children, because it is the most heinous of killing, and more heinous than killing in general [p. 317] when done out of fear of poverty. When He had enjoined the first obligation toward the first Benefactor, the One who brought existence out of nothingness, He followed it with what is owed to the first benefactor after Him, who is the cause of existence. So He said, forbidding wrongdoing in the form of a command to do good, in the most emphatic manner, because people are lax in regard to these two rights. Likewise, all the commanded matters are presented in this manner, which implies that their opposites are forbidden, so that they are commanded and their opposites are forbidden, which makes it more emphatic and weighty: ﴿And to parents⦆, that is, act toward them ﴿with kindness⦆.

When He had enjoined the cause of existence, He forbade causing non-existence and began with the gravest of it, so He said: ﴿And do not kill your children⦆. Since the prohibition was general, and since killing a child might sometimes be obligatory, He specified the reason, saying: ﴿out of poverty⦆, that is, because of a poverty existing among you. Then He gave the reason for that. And since it is apparent that poverty already exists, He placed the parents first, and said: ﴿We provide for you⦆ in the second person, that is, O poor ones. Then He conjoined the children to it, saying: ﴿and them⦆. The apparent sense of His words in al-Isra: ﴿for fear of poverty⦆ [al-Isra: 31] is that the parents are well-off but fear poverty in feeding the children. So He began with the children and said: (We provide for them), then He conjoined the parents, saying (and you). Abu Hayyan drew attention to this.

Since killing them is the most heinous of all abominations after association, He followed it with a prohibition of all abominations, which are those whose ugliness is grave and whose matter is great, with a prohibition on approaching them, let alone committing them. So He said: ﴿And do not approach the abominations⦆. Then, as an emphasis for generality, He substituted for them: ﴿what is apparent of them⦆, that is, of the abominations, ﴿and what is hidden⦆. Then He explicitly mentioned killing among them, glorifying it by specifying it after the generalization, and said: ﴿And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden⦆, that is, which the Supreme King has forbidden you to kill, ﴿except by right⦆, that is, the complete right. It is not complete unless it is as clear as the sun, with no doubt in it. Thus the killing of a child became forbidden three times. Then He emphasized what was mentioned by saying: ﴿That is what He has commanded you⦆, that is, this great matter among these mentioned things.

Since these matters are heavy upon the soul, He concluded them with what only a loving and compassionate one would say, so that the heart might accept them. So He said: ﴿He has enjoined you with this⦆, as command and prohibition. And since these matters, because of their great importance and the weight of their impact on souls, do not need further reflection, He said: ﴿that you may understand⦆, that is, that you may be hopeful of walking on the path of the wise. From the mention of the charge it is thus known that these mentioned matters are the ones enjoined, and the forbidden matters are their opposites. Its matter is thereby emphasized in two respects: the explicit enjoining of them, and the prohibition of their opposites.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 152:

Since wealth is the counterpart of the soul (rūḥ), in that the soul cannot sustain itself without it, he began the verse that follows it with wealth. And since the most weighty of these in standing and sanctity is the wealth of the orphan, because of his weakness and the paucity of his helpers, he began with it, forbidding approaching it, let alone eating or drinking it (p-319), so he said: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan﴾, that is: by any kind of approach, whether by working with it or otherwise, ﴿except in the way that is best﴾ among the courses of action, such as striving to make it grow and increase, and that this continue ﴿until he reaches his maturity﴾, which is the age at which the time of the attainment of his intellect is customarily reached and an intellect by which his sound judgment becomes manifest. Then he followed this with measures in a comprehensive manner, saying: ﴿And give full measure and weight﴾, that is: complete them, ﴿with justice﴾, because they are the arbiter in the wealth of orphans and others. And since a thing is sometimes applied to what is close to it, as in "the prayer has been established" (qad qāmati al-ṣalāh), meaning its establishment is near, and this is the time of such-and-such, and when it is very near, this possibility is removed by his saying: ﴿with justice﴾, that is, fulfilling it in a manner that is free of excess or deficiency.

Since measures scarcely ever come out equal, especially the weight, for it is the furthest of them from that, while the nearest of them is the cubit (dhir'), which falls under measuring by volume, for it is said: "he measured (kāla) the thing against the thing," meaning he compared it, he indicated that the responsible person, whose affair is founded on weakness and incapacity, is required only to exert effort. So he said: ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, in accordance with our greatness, and whatever lies beyond capacity is pardoned. Then he added a third element, justice in speech, because it is the arbiter over wealth and other things, and he placed the act before it because it indicates it, so the act was enjoined twice. So he said: ﴿And when you speak﴾, that is, in testimony, or in judgment, or in reconciling between two parties, or otherwise, ﴿be just﴾, that is, bringing speech and action into agreement.

Since souls are naturally inclined to compassion for the near of kin, he said: (p-320) ﴿And even if it be a near relative﴾, that is, the person about whom one speaks, whether for him or against him, in testimony or otherwise, ﴿and do not show partiality﴾, out of hope for his support or fear of his harm. Then he concluded with the covenant, since it encompasses all of this in speech and action, saying: ﴿And fulfill the covenant of Allah﴾, that is, of the Supreme King specifically, ﴿fulfill﴾. This includes everything that is incumbent upon a person and due to him, for Allah has not neglected anything without prior ordinance concerning it. Then he emphasized the magnitude of this with his saying: ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾, that is, the matter given care, ﴿He has enjoined you with it﴾, that is, your Lord, who is good to you.

Since these acts and words are heavy upon the soul, for justice in them runs against desires, he preceded with encouragement toward them and warning against their opposites, that whoever does any of them with another is about to have the like done to him. For this reason he urged reflection (tadhakkur) in what he enjoined, and because these matters are subtle and need further contemplation, he said: ﴿So that you may remember﴾, that is, so that you may be in a state where remembrance is attained by you, even if in a hidden manner indicated by the idgham (assimilation), regarding what your souls are inclined to, namely the love of the like of that for yourselves, so that you may judge for others by what you judge for yourselves.

When he had established these laws, he drew attention to honoring them in particular, in a way that covers everything mentioned in the surah and beyond it. So he said, linking it by conjunction to what is implied (it is coordinated with the prohibitions and the opposites of the commands, in a way that encompasses the whole Law): "And do not deviate from My way." ﴿And that﴾, i.e., "and because," according to the reading of the majority (al-Jama'ah) with the fatha, meaning: follow it for that reason. According to the reading of Ibn 'Amir and Ya'qub with the kasra, it is a new sentence (p-321) ﴿This is﴾, i.e., what I have prescribed for you, ﴿My path﴾, in the state of being ﴿straight, so follow it﴾, i.e., with the utmost of your effort, because it is what gathers the servants upon the truth in which lies every good.

Since the command to follow it implies a prohibition against anything else, he stated this explicitly to emphasize his command, so he said: ﴿And do not follow the paths﴾, i.e., those branching off from the desires that divide the servants. For this reason he said, giving the cause: ﴿so that they scatter you from His path﴾, i.e., those false paths scatter you away from ﴿His path﴾. Having praised it by commanding it and forbidding everything else, while explaining the reason for that, he reinforced its praise, so he said: ﴿That is what He has enjoined upon you﴾, i.e., this great matter of following it, ﴿that He has commanded you with﴾.

Since he had warned against slipping away from it, and since it is well known that whoever strays from the most upright way falls into ruin, and since everyone who imagines himself falling into destruction becomes fearful, he said: ﴿So that you may be God-conscious﴾, i.e., follow it and leave aside anything else, so that your condition is that of one who is hoped to fear lest he slip, stray, and perish. This is like what He, may He be glorified, praised earlier in His saying: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾ [al-An'am: 126] and ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who remember﴾ [al-An'am: 126]. He detailed the rulings mentioned here in three verses, and He concluded each verse with the injunction (wasiyyah) for this reason, so that the statement would be more emphatic and thus more likely to be accepted. He concluded each of them with what He concluded them with, because when the intellect calls to remembrance, it leads to God-consciousness (taqwa).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 154:

Since these three verses (al-An'am 6:151-153) fulfil the Ten Commandments that Allah wrote for Musa (peace be upon him) on the Tablets of the Testimony (lawhay al-shahada), at the first revelation he received at Mount Sinai (Tur Sinin), which was indicated by His words: ﴿And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers﴾ [Al-An'am: 91], and upon them He built the Tawrah (Torah), and commanded him to place them in the Ark of the Covenant (tabut al-ahd) so that they would be a witness against them and their descendants, as is mentioned in the middle of the second book (sifr) of the Tawrah, and its explanation has already passed in al-Baqarah and will come at the end of this statement, along with what it adds of rulings and excellences as Allah wills, it was fitting that the Tawrah be mentioned after them. So He said, indicating by the particle of delay (thumma) both the sequence and the magnification: ﴿Then We gave﴾, that is, by the greatness We possess which requires magnifying what came from Us, ﴿Musa the Book﴾, that is, the one indicated by His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book which Musa brought?﴾ [Al-An'am: 91]. It is, and Allah knows best, coordinated with His words: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾ [Al-An'am: 146], because after He gave Musa the Ten Signs, He appointed him to the mountain for a second appointment, and He legislated for him some rulings, commanded him to erect the Tent of Meeting (qubbat al-zaman), in which he would receive revelation and toward which they would pray, and some of its equipment, as has passed in al-Baqarah. Then, shortly after that, He mentioned the prohibition of fats (shuhum) for them, saying at the beginning of the third book, which is the Book of the Priests (sifr al-kahana), in which the matter of offerings is summarized: "And the LORD called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting, and said to him: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When any man of you brings an offering to the LORD of the livestock, of the herd or of the flock, ..." (p-٣٢٣) until he said: "And he shall offer as an offering to the LORD the fat that covers the entrails and all the fat that is on the entrails, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them and on the flanks..." until he said: "And said: The fats are the LORD's, a perpetual statute. You shall not eat any fat or any blood." Then he said: "And the LORD spoke to Moses and said to him: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: You shall not eat any fat of ox or sheep or goat, whether ram or ewe, for whoever eats the fat of an animal of which an offering by fire is made to the LORD, the person who eats it shall be cut off from his people. And you shall eat no blood, whether of bird or of animal, in any of your dwellings. Whoever eats any blood, that person shall be cut off from his people." And in the fifth book he said: "But you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out on the ground like water." Then shortly after he said: "And you may eat within your towns whatever your appetite desires... but only you must not eat the blood, for the blood is the life, so you shall not eat the life with the flesh, that it may go well with you and your children after you, when you do what is right in the sight of the LORD your God." He returned to the third book and then said: "Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting and came out and blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people, and fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat on the altar, and when all the people saw it, they shouted and fell on their faces." (p-٣٢٤) Then after that, shortly afterward, he mentioned the forbidden animals, and likewise he mentioned them in the fifth book; I have combined them, and the majority of the context is from the fifth: He said: "You shall not eat any detestable thing. These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat, the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the antelope, the wild ox and the chamois. Any animal that has divided hooves and chews the cud, you may eat. But of those that chew the cud or have divided hooves, you shall not eat the camel, the rabbit, and the coney, which chew the cud but do not have divided hooves; they are unclean for you. And the swine, because it has divided hooves but does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. You shall not eat of their flesh or touch their carcasses." And in the third book he said: "And you shall not touch their flesh, for they are unclean and forbidden to you." And in the fifth, from the translation of the Seventy: "And beware of eating any unclean thing; and what you eat from the livestock is the calf of the herd, the lamb of the sheep, the kid of the goats, or the deer, the gazelle, the roebuck, the wild goat, the antelope, the wild ox, the giraffe, and every animal that has a divided hoof, cleft into cloven hoofs and chews the cud." (p-٣٢٥) Then: "Of these you may eat, but of those that chew the cud or have divided hooves, you shall not eat the camel, the rabbit, or the jerboa, for these chew the cud but are not cloven-hoofed, and it is unlawful for you. The swine too, for its hoof is cloven and it has hooves but does not chew the cud; you shall not eat of their flesh or touch their carcasses." And in the third of them: "And the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them: Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: Of all the beasts that are on the earth, these are the animals you may eat: every animal that has a divided hoof and chews the cud. But you shall not eat of these which chew the cud or have divided hooves: the camel, the rabbit, and the swine, because they are unclean for you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, and you shall not touch their dead bodies." Then he returned to my copy, and then mentioned among birds and land animals, close to what is in our law, until he said: "You shall not eat anything unclean; rather give it to the sojourner who is within your towns, that he may eat it, or sell it to a foreigner, for you are a holy people to the LORD your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk." And in the translation of the Seventy: "You shall not boil the lamb in its mother's milk." And in the fifth book: "You may eat any clean bird, but these are the ones you shall not eat: the eagle, the vulture..." and he mentioned something similar to what we have. And in my copy in the third: "Whoever touches any of these, that is, the forbidden things, shall be unclean until evening, and whoever carries any of them shall wash his garments and be unclean until evening." End of quotation.

Al-zaby (the gazelle), with an unpointed-dotted letter and shared meaning, is known. Al-jawdhar (with a fatha on the jim, a dotted dhal and a ra): the wild cow. Al-rim (with a kasra on the undotted letter): the purely white gazelle. Al-thaytal (with two vowelled thas, with a sukun yaa between): the wild bull. Al-ayyil (with fatha on the hamza and a shadda kasra on the yaa): the deer. Al-wa'il (with fatha on the waw and kasra on the undotted letter): the mountain ram. Al-hamal (with fatha on the undotted letter): the suckling young of sheep.

As for His words, "Do not boil a kid in its mother's milk": the apparent meaning is the prohibition of eating it while it still suckles. What follows in the third book is the bulk of the Tawrah, and what is in the fifth is merely a repetition of what is in the third, for the fifth is a summary of everything preceding it of narratives and rulings with additions. Thus it is true that the giving of the Book came mostly after (p-٣٢٧) the prohibition of what was forbidden to them. It is also permissible, and this is better, that it be coordinated with an omitted element whose estimate is: "That is what He has enjoined upon you, as He enjoined upon the children of Israel in the section whose relation to the Tawrah is like the relation of Umm al-Qur'an (the Opening chapter) to the Qur'an," and that is the Ten Signs, which were the first thing Allah wrote for Musa (peace be upon him), and which are in reality the first part of the Tawrah, because they are the first of the rulings, and what precedes them is narrative. The summary of these ten [signs] is: "The LORD your God who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery and bondage; you shall have no other gods before me; you shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain; keep the Sabbath day; honour your father and your mother; you shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal; you shall not bear false witness; you shall not covet what is your neighbour's." So the meaning is: "That is what We have enjoined upon you, as We enjoined upon the children of Israel in the Ten Signs and some of what We gave Musa of the Tawrah." It is also permissible that the estimate be: because these signs are firm in all the laws, not abrogated in any nation of the nations, nor will they be abrogated; He enjoined them upon you, O children of Adam, in the earliest time, and the command to them has only increased in emphasis. ﴿Then We gave﴾, that is, by the greatness We possess, ﴿Musa the Book﴾, that is, all of it, and it contains these, in a state of ﴿being complete﴾, lacking nothing of what would benefit them, ﴿upon﴾ the manner ﴿that is best﴾, that is, He brought excellence, so He established goodness and gathered it by what He made clear of the Law and by what He protected the groups of the people of the earth through it from destruction in general, for it is narrated that Allah, exalted is He, did not destroy any people with a general destruction after the sending down of the Tawrah. ﴿And a detailed explanation of everything﴾, from the totality of that section which contains the words comprising everything needed in matters of religion and worldly life, just as the Qur'an is a detailed explanation of everything, from the seven comprehensive principles which the Umm al-Qur'an contains, which are sufficient for the welfare of both abodes. And in these two possibilities, which require that (thumma) retain its true meaning of sequence and interval, there is a sign of the signs of prophethood: namely, the awareness that the Ten Signs and the prohibition of what was forbidden to them, because of their transgression, were among the first things revealed to Musa (peace be upon him) after the drowning of Pharaoh, and that most of the Tawrah was sent down after that, and this is known only to their rabbis. ﴿And a guidance﴾, that is, an explanation, ﴿and a mercy﴾, that is, an honour for whoever accepts it and acts by it, ﴿so that they﴾, that is, the children of Israel, ﴿in the meeting with their Lord﴾, that is, the One who brought them out of Egypt from slavery and bondage with His great power and His perfect words, ﴿may believe﴾, that is, so that their state after the sending down of the Book, because of what they see of the excellence of its laws, the grandeur of its speech and the majesty of its matter, would be the state of one who is hoped to renew faith at every time in meeting his Lord, because of His power to resurrect, faith in which is the utmost of affirming the prophets, since reason alone cannot establish it, and it is only established by revelation, while reason permits it. So they should know that nothing resembles Him, just as His speech is not like any speech, so they should not seek to make a calf a goal (p-٣٢٩) whose matter is a lowing that cannot be understood and a murmuring that conveys nothing.

When he had shown that the sending down of Books is a mercy from Him, since their purpose is to guide people to their source, so that His commands are carried out and His prohibitions and warnings are heeded, he then showed that He did not single out those earlier nations with this. Rather, He sent down a Book to this Ummah and did not approve of it being like those Books. Instead, He made it the greatest of them in blessing and the clearest in guidance. So He said: ﴿And this﴾, that is, the Qur'an, ﴿is a Book﴾, that is, a great one, ﴿which We have sent down﴾, that is, by Our greatness, to you, in your tongue, as a proof against you, ﴿blessed﴾, that is, everything in it of promise and threat, of good and other things, is firmly established, with a firmness that cannot be removed, along with abundance and good.

Since this was its meaning, and it called to itself and was made beloved, He drew from it the statement: ﴿So follow it﴾, that is, so that all your affairs may be established and blessed. When He commanded following it, and a person may follow it outwardly while not doing so inwardly, He commanded the establishing of taqwa (God-consciousness, fear of God), which makes the inner self sound, in a general manner. For this reason He omitted the pronoun and said: ﴿And fear [God]﴾, that is, and in addition to that, establish taqwa, which is bringing about a protection from every thing to be feared. Indeed, the danger is severe, and safety is beyond measure. So do not depart from fear of its source with your utmost effort, for that is more fitting to bring you to complete following of it and sincerity in it. ﴿That you may receive mercy﴾, that is, so that your condition may be that of one who is hoped to be honoured with great gifts. The two verses refer to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who sent down the Book that Moses brought﴾ [al-An'am: 91], to His saying: ﴿and who guard their prayers﴾ [al-An'am: 92].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 156:

Then he explained the purpose of its revelation, which is the establishment of the conclusive proof. So he said: ﴿Lest you should say﴾ — that is, "because you [would] not say" — or "out of aversion that you should say, O community, the unlettered community: ﴿Indeed the Book was revealed﴾ — that is, the well-known divine Book — ﴿upon two groups﴾." He brought the time close and made it partial by introducing the preposition, so he said: ﴿from before us﴾ — that is, the Jews and the Christians. ﴿And indeed﴾ — that is, "and that we" — or "and that the matter" — ﴿we were, regarding their study﴾ — that is, their recitation of their Book — in a manner of repeated recitation.

Since it is the lightened form (of inna), he brought the distinguishing lam between it and the negating particle, so he said: ﴿indeed heedless﴾ — that is, we did not know its reality, and its truth was not established for us, [nor was it in our language].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 157:

﴿Or (lest) you should say﴾ — i.e., O Arabs: "We were not heedless of their study (dirasa), but rather we were aware of it. However, following the Book is only obligatory for the one to whom it was addressed, so we did not follow it. And ﴿if only that we﴾ had been qualified for what they were qualified for, until ﴿the Book had been sent down to us﴾ — i.e., its kind, or the Book that was sent down to them from our Lord — ﴿we would have been better guided than they﴾ — i.e., because of the readiness we have through abundance of intellect, sharpness of minds, soundness of thought, moderation of temperaments, and submission to the truth. For this reason he grounded these two causes in His saying: ﴿Now there has come to you﴾ — and He mentioned the verb to praise this Qur'an, to prefer it and to honor it over everything that preceded it [and to alert that the explanation of this surah comes at the end, because it is the surah of the foundations of the religion] ﴿a clear proof﴾ — i.e., an evident argument in your own tongue ﴿from your Lord﴾ — i.e., the One who does good to you — through the tongue of a man ﴿from among you﴾ whom you know to be the best of you in this respect ﴿and guidance﴾ — i.e., a great explanation for whoever reflects upon it ﴿and mercy﴾ — i.e., honor for whoever accepts it, (p-331) ﴿yet you denied it﴾.

When the argument was established against them, it was fitting for the reproach of rebuke to occur with His saying: ﴿So who﴾ — i.e., so it follows from your denial that it is said, as an explanation that you are the greatest of people in wrongdoing: who is ﴿more wrong than one who denies﴾ [i.e., who commits denial] ﴿the signs of God﴾ — i.e., the One than whom there is nothing greater, so there is nothing greater than His signs, because the effect is in proportion to the one who effects it ﴿and turns away﴾ — i.e., he turned away with an aversion by which it became as if he were in a shackle (safad) — i.e., a barrier — preventing him from readily submitting to the proof ﴿from them﴾ [after he had recognized their soundness].

Since the answer is certain — no one is more wrong than him — and the situation required anticipating what he would be recompensed with, He said: ﴿We will recompense﴾ — i.e., with a true promise that admits no breach — and He expressed explicitly what would originally have been an pronoun, to generalize and to attach the judgment to the attribute, so He said: ﴿those who turn away﴾ — i.e., who renew aversion and do not repent ﴿from Our signs﴾ — i.e., despite the greatness they possess ﴿a dreadful punishment﴾ — i.e., one that grieves their very selves ﴿for what they used to turn away﴾ — i.e., because of their aversion, which had become a habit for them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 158:

Since the worst of evils is the right of punishment, and its due is the non-acceptance of repentance, he explained it with His words, easing it for them and making it simple by stripping the verb (tajrid, using the bare form of the verb): ﴿Do they await﴾, meaning: what do these deniers await, even the least, closest and easiest waiting, ﴿except that the angels come to them﴾ [meaning: while they remain in their denial], ﴿the angels﴾, meaning: with the decisive command of their punishment (p-332), as is their custom in coming to the deniers, ﴿or your Lord comes﴾, meaning: the manifestation of the affair of Him who does good to you in the fullest manifestation, with all the signs that minds can bear, and that is the Day of Recompense, ﴿or some of the signs of your Lord come﴾. He made it indefinite to magnify and emphasise the matter, so He said: ﴿some of the signs of your Lord﴾, meaning: the portents of the Hour, in which His full manifestation and His greatest goodness towards you occur, such as the beast of the earth that distinguishes the disbeliever from the believer, and the rising of the sun from its west, which announces the closing of the door of repentance. al-Bukhari narrated in the Tafsir and others, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the sun rises from its west. When people see it, everyone on earth will believe, but that is the time when faith will not benefit a soul that did not believe before." Then he recited the verse.

Since the coming of the angels, meaning all of them, is an affair whose greatness minds cannot describe, and it brings no good news to the criminals at the sight of it, then if it came in its own form, their joints would be torn apart and their strength could not bear it, so ﴿the matter is decided, and they will not be reprieved﴾. As for the manifestation of the Lord, glorified is He, mighty is His name and exalted is His greatness, the matter is greater than any speaker's statement, whether eloquent people soften it or magnify it.

He left out what follows from it and said: ﴿on the day when some of the signs of your Lord come﴾ [meaning: are uncovered and become manifest], ﴿some of the signs of your Lord﴾, meaning: of Him who does good to you, by the coming of that as confirmation for you, and as terror and destruction for your opponents. ﴿Faith will not benefit a soul﴾, meaning: a disbelieving soul, ﴿its faith﴾, meaning: at that time, nor will a believing soul whose earning was good at that time benefit from its earlier faith before that sign [with repentance, for what comes after it is nothing]. For this reason He clarified it with His words describing a soul: ﴿had not believed﴾ (p-333), meaning: the disbelieving soul, ﴿before﴾, and He eased the matter by allowing some of the earlier time, and did not require that it be exhausted in faith, so He said: ﴿before﴾, meaning: before the sign came, in a time connected to its coming.

Since He mentioned the disbelieving soul, He followed it with the believing soul, saying, conjoining it to (had believed): ﴿or﴾ [the believing soul] who was sinful and had not ﴿earned﴾ [meaning: before] ﴿in its faith﴾, meaning: its prior faith before the sign came, ﴿any good﴾, meaning: repentance. In other words: a disbelieving soul whose renewed faith comes after the sign, which is the meaning of ﴿had not believed before﴾, or a believing soul whose earning of good comes after the sign, as long as it had not earned any good in its prior faith before the sign. The conclusion is that at that time the faith of a disbeliever is not accepted, nor the repentance of a sinner, as al-Baghawi said, because the purpose of assent and repentance is faith in the unseen, and that has passed with the compelling sign. Thus the subject of the implied verb in (earned) is omitted, and the estimate is: faith does not benefit a soul that had not believed before, or had not earned good in its faith, its faith and its earning. So faith refers to the one who did not believe, and earning refers to the one who did not earn, which is evident. The threat of faith's not benefiting at the coming of the sign is the greatest proof of what I have mentioned in this estimate. The verse is of ihtibak (a rhetorical device where one element is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa): the mention of their faith first is evidence of the omission of their earning from the second clause, and the mention of the clauses (had believed) and (had earned) second is indicative of the omission of the disbelieving and believing soul first.

Since this is a threat, as you see, terrifying, He followed it with something even more severe, to alert (p-334) that the people of faith are safe from that, with His words: ﴿Say: Wait﴾, meaning: with the utmost of your effort, O deniers, ﴿we too are waiting﴾, with our effort, and you will know to whom the final outcome belongs.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 159:

When He forbade following the (various) paths, because they are the cause of division away from the truth, and He had repeatedly, in this surah, set forth proofs, made evidences shine forth, removed doubts, and effaced the traces of suspicions, and the surah was drawing near its conclusion, and it was known with certainty that the truth, insofar as it is truth, is highly effective in destroying falsehood, how much more so when it is the speech of the King whose command is not opposed and whose will is not exceeded, the Prophet (ﷺ) became intensely eager to see the effect of that, along with his zeal for the Islam of his people, because of the compassion that Allah had instilled in him toward all creation in general and toward them in particular. That effect comes only through bringing about their guidance and erasing their misguidance. So when He, glorified is He, concluded with these two great warnings, which indicate their being veiled (from the truth), the Prophet (ﷺ) felt that what he had hoped for regarding their guidance was as if it had already been achieved. This produces a pity mixed with grief over those whose worth one does not know and whose state cannot be described. So He, glorified is He, strengthened him and consoled him with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who divided﴾, that is, after you have conveyed (the message) to them, ﴿their religion﴾, that is, by denying some of the signs of Allah, turning away from them, and believing in some of them, so they separated from it; for disbelief in part of it is disbelief in all of it. The religion is attributed to them because of the intensity of their desire for it and their fighting for it. (p-335) ﴿And they became sects﴾: each group follows and makes others follow its leader, like the Arabs who formed factions by multiplying idols, so that in every region they had one or two or more deities; and like the People of the Book, who innovated in their religion innovations that led them to declare one another disbelievers, believing in some prophets and disbelieving in others; and like the Magians, who tore their religion apart by believing that God is two: Light and Darkness, and who worshipped idols and stars, making for every star an idol through which, in their assumption, one seeks nearness to it. ﴿You are not of them﴾, that is, not responsible for their reckoning, nor for their punishment, nor for creating guidance in their hearts, ﴿in anything﴾. In this is the utmost urging toward unity and the ultimate threat against division.

. When He lightened (the burden) upon him (ﷺ) by clearing him of them, He ascribed to His Most Holy Self what befits Him in the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and power, so He said, answering one who says: "Then to whom does their affair belong?": ﴿Their affair is only with Allah﴾, that is, in all of that and in everything that concerns them, which no limit confines and no count enumerates, ﴿to Allah﴾, that is, the King to whom no one shares command with Him, so whomever He wills He guides, and whomever He wills He blinds, and whomever He wills He destroys, and whomever He wills He preserves, for He has perfect greatness.

. And since the Gathering is distant from all of that in rank and in time, such that minds cannot reach the reality of its greatness, He drew attention to this by using the particle of delay and admonition (p-336) in His saying: ﴿Then﴾, after fulfilling the terms He set for them, ﴿He will inform them﴾, that is, with a great, magnificent and thorough informing after He has gathered them to Himself in humiliation, ﴿of what they used to do﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, of those ugly deeds toward which they had the strongest motive, without hesitating to carry them out for lack of knowledge, while claiming to be religious through them. And this verse, together with what preceded of its implications, is an explanation (ta'lil) of His saying: ﴿And do not follow the (other) paths, for they will separate you from His path﴾ [al-An'am: 153].

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 160:

When He had informed that their affair is none other than His concern, it was as though it were said: "What, then, does He do with them at that time?" So He answered with His words: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed﴾, that is, from among them or from others, ﴿with the good deed﴾, that is, the complete one, by its being founded upon faith, ﴿for him﴾ there is of good deeds ﴿ten times its like﴾, out of generosity, benevolence, bounty and grace. He rewards him with this in this world or in the Hereafter. This is established for everyone, and for some it becomes clearer according to their intentions. He mentioned "ten" because it is in the sense of "good deed" (hasanah), and it is in construct with its pronoun (i.e., the number is feminine in agreement with the grammatically feminine noun it counts, and it is attached to the pronoun referring to it). When His words ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾ [al-An'am: 152], followed by His words ﴿We do not charge a soul except to its capacity﴾ [al-An'am: 152], contained an indication that equality in recompense is something before which the necks of creation are cut off, He informed that this is easy for Him, because His action is all-encompassing and His power is complete, by His words (p-337): ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed﴾, that is, whatever kind of it was from this category, ﴿he will not be recompensed except with its like﴾, that is, in both abodes, [if he is recompensed, and He pardons much].

Since equivalence does not necessarily mean being equal in every respect, even though it is apparent in this matter, especially in this expression, he stated what is its apparent meaning, because it is more pleasant to the soul and more calming to fear. So he said: ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾, that is, by its being like it in unity, even if it is greater, or of a kind more severe than its kind, and the like. Rather, equivalence exists in quantity and quality, so no one is diminished in reward nor increased in punishment.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 161:

When the preceding part (of the surah) had included the affirmation of tawhid (divine oneness) through decisive proofs, the verification of the matter of divine decree and power, and the nullification of all the religions of error, describing them by the division of their adherents, which indicates their falsehood and crookedness, and it concluded with this warning, than which there is nothing more upright or more just, He (ﷺ) was commanded to proclaim His command and to describe the religion which He had prescribed for him and guided him to, with its excellences, to make it beloved and to urge it. This is also because it is a result of this surah. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, and He emphasized it by the use of the two nuns, saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord has guided me﴾, i.e., with clarification and success, ﴿my Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to me in every good, especially this which He has revealed to me and sent down upon me, ﴿to a straight path﴾, i.e., a wide, clear way. Then He praised it by His saying: ﴿a correct religion﴾, i.e., one that reaches the utmost in moderation and uprightness, and is firm in them. This is according to the reading of Ibn Kathir, Nafi' and Abu 'Amr with a fatha on the qaf and a shadda on the ya' (kasra), and in the reading of the rest it is with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the light ya', a verbal noun meaning "standing" used as a description for the sake of emphasis. He increased its praise by His saying, admonishing them, because of their taqlid (blind imitation) of their fathers, that it is the religion of their greatest forefather: ﴿the creed of Ibrahim﴾. The millah (creed) is what the light of reason has manifested of guidance amid the darknesses of the customs of worldly affairs that people have adopted, as al-Harali stated. For this reason He said: ﴿ḥanīfan﴾, i.e., gentle, easy, pliant, receptive to uprightness, because he inclined with the proof, not dry or rigid, standing still with imitation, blind to the light of proof, as has preceded in al-Baqarah. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and he was not among the polytheists﴾, i.e., while the situation is that he was not among those who are rigid with their delusions in claiming a partner for God, while they see that it does not harm, nor benefit, nor is it fit to be a partner even for a human being, let alone for anything else in any way, who do not submit to proof nor listen to speech. So this was a praise of this religion to which he (ﷺ) was guided, and a clarification that it is the one which He, glorified is He, chose for His friend Ibrahim (peace be upon him), returning to

﴿And when Ibrahim said to his father Azar﴾ [al-An'am: 74], upon which the surah was in reality built, and to which the reins of its ends were delivered, and as an encouragement to this religion, because all the opponents cling to the skirts of Ibrahim (peace be upon him): the Arabs and the People of the Two Books by the relation of fatherhood, and the Magians by the relation of place and brotherhood. By this He indicated that Muhammad (ﷺ) understood what his forefather Ibrahim (peace be upon him) argued with his people and accepted it, so he was not attributed, like others, to rigidity or obstinacy.

Since it was as if a questioner asked: "What is this religion whose praise is repeated and to which one is called?" he answered with His saying, so that the people of faith might emulate him and adhere to everything to which he calls, in sincerity: ﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer﴾, i.e., the one which is the essence (lubab) of the religion and its purest part, ﴿and my sacrifice﴾, i.e., all my worship, including slaughtering and other things, ﴿and my living and my dying are for Allah﴾, i.e., the King, the Greatest, nothing of whose command goes beyond Him. And since He taught, by the Greatest Name, that He deserves this in His essence, He made known that He deserves it from every person for His kindness to him and His bounty upon him, so He said: ﴿Lord of the worlds﴾, the Originator, the Manager, and the Nourisher of them.

When He informed that He alone deserves worship by virtue of His essence and attributes, He informed that He alone deserves it, so He said: ﴿He has no partner﴾, meaning: so that there could be for His partner, according to your claim, some share of worship, since he would have some share of lordship (*rububiyyah*). Thereby He made clear that the direction of the Messenger (ﷺ) and of those who follow him is one, without divergence in it, namely the intention of Allah alone with sincerity (*ikhlas*), just as He alone gives life and causes death, so He should likewise be made One in worship.

When He indicated this by the proof of reason, He followed it with categorical transmitted evidence, and He said [connecting it to what is implied: "To this the proof of reason has guided me"]: ﴿And of that I have been commanded﴾, meaning: by the lofty command, from directing my affairs to Him with sincerity.

(p. 340) Since for Him, glorified is He, every thing is a sign indicating that He is One, and every thing was thus commanding monotheism by the tongue of its state or the explicit speech of its utterance, He built the verb into the passive in His saying ﴿I have been commanded﴾. That is, this religion, even had no command been revealed concerning it, was something a rational person should adopt and not turn away from, because of its great manifestness, the spread of its light, the proofs that stand upon it, and the fact that the virtuous and the excellent have walked upon following it. So how much more so when the divine commands have come forth with it and the lordly motives have called to it? ﴿And I am the first of the Muslims﴾, meaning: the first of those who submit to what the summons of Allah calls to in this religion. I have no choice at all in it; rather, I am stripped of choice in it, submitting with the utmost submission. This priority is absolute, both in time and in rank with respect to his community (ﷺ), and in rank with respect to those prophets and others who preceded him. This is also a matter of excellence in calling to something: to advance toward what one calls others to, and to love for the one addressed what one loves for oneself, so that this is more removed from suspicion and more indicative of sincere counsel, and thus more likely to secure acceptance.

When they disputed with him about associating partners with God in this surah on more than one occasion, as Abraham's people disputed with him, and the last of that was that he (ﷺ) called them to recite what God, glorified is He, had sent down to him concerning the prohibition of shirk (associating partners with God) and the explanation of His upright religion, then here He repeated their censure for division, which necessarily indicates misguidance, and the praise of the religion of the messengers, which was stated earlier to be one in which they did not differ at all. He also made the disbelievers despair of the Prophet (ﷺ) agreeing with them in any form of agreement or inclining toward them in any degree of inclination. God, glorified is He, commanded him, after it had been established at the beginning, middle and end of the surah that there is no lord other than Him, to reject those who wanted him to incline toward someone other than the One who alone gives life and causes death. So He alone has sole ownership of what lies between them and what comes after, without any doubt. Then came the severe rebuke, and He said: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to those who hope you will drive away your companions for their sake: ﴿Shall I seek other than Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all perfection, ﴿as a lord﴾ i.e., as a nurturer who manages my affairs, as you desire. ﴿Seek﴾ means I desire and want by associating partners, for absolute independence is not accepted from one who associates anything with Him. This is an allusion to them and a reminder to them. The attribution to him (ﷺ) while meaning all of creation is out of fairness in debate, for the sake of appeal. ﴿And He is﴾, i.e., while the case is that, as established by decisive proofs, fixed in sound minds and impressed upon the shining lights of thought, ﴿the Lord of all things﴾, i.e., its originator and its sustainer. Is it fitting for anyone to submit to other than his master, when that other is himself a subject of his master like him? This is what no intelligent person would accept for himself.

Since He had denounced those who incline toward others besides Him despite His general goodness and benevolence, He followed this with a warning drawn from the straight justice of His great harm, and He said: ﴿And not﴾, i.e., while the case is that ﴿every soul earns﴾, i.e., any sin, however small, together with firm resolve and strong determination that is such that action confirms it, as already passed in the verse of al-Baqarah: ﴿except against itself﴾, i.e., it is impossible that it be borne against anything other than itself, neither against itself nor against anyone else. Since it is impossible for Him, glorified is He, to hold anyone accountable for it other than the one who committed it, because He is Just and Wise, how then could I call upon another, openly or secretly? That is the greatest of sins! And to warn against hidden shirk, such as showing off, and every disobedience however small, He stripped the verb of the ifti'al (the reflexive verb form with infixed -ta-, here kasaba used in its bare form) so that it would not be supposed that it applies only to what one exerts oneself in. The context here clearly shows that kasb (earning) is restricted to sin, for it concerns calling upon other than God. The verse of al-Baqarah is for alluding to the sin that is committed only through intense desire of the soul for it, due to the soul's disposition toward deficiencies, so it does not contradict this, because what the soul earns of sins is known from there to be acquisition. Better than this is to say: since the meaning is that if I seek a lord other than Him, He would leave me to what I have entrusted to myself, and I am a human being, and a human being is disposed toward deficiencies, so I would perish, He expressed this by His words stripped of the verb for the purpose of generality: ﴿And not every soul earns﴾ by being a soul that looks at its own preciousness, turns away from its Lord, and is left to its own strength and power, ﴿except against itself﴾, and no one else bears any of its burden for it. Since it sometimes happens that one bears some of another's burdens out of help for him, He negated that with His words: ﴿And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another﴾, i.e., no bearer shall carry the sin of another, even if it were a parent or a child. ﴿And if one heavily laden calls for its load to be carried, nothing of it will be carried, even if he were a close relative﴾ [Fatir 35:18]. Given that this is the case, it is not becoming for an intelligent person to expose himself to bearing any part of the anger of this King who has no partner, and to whom is the return, however long the term may be.

Since He generalized in earning and in bearing burdens, lest a fault-finder say that this is specific to you and not to us, He generalized the return as well for the same reason. He said, threatening them after complete clarification, connecting it to what the rejection indicated of negation, as if to say: "I do not do any of that. I do not seek any lord other than my Lord at all. As for you, do what you are doing, for your Lord knows it." Then: ﴿Then﴾ [i.e., after a long respite], out of His kindness toward you, ﴿to your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who has bestowed upon you every blessing, not to anyone else, ﴿is your return﴾, i.e., by gathering, even if you live long or remain a long time, ﴿and He will inform you﴾, i.e., He will tell you with a great, magnificent and complete account.

Since it had been stated earlier that they had divided their religion, He said: ﴿of what you used to﴾, i.e., by nature and disposition. For this reason He placed the prepositional phrase first, to convey emphasis on it, because of the strength of their motive toward it without compulsion, heedlessness or forgetfulness. So He said: ﴿concerning it you differed﴾, i.e., with a messenger and others. He will repay you for all of that according to what you deserve, and your situation is worthy that your punishment be severe, because you denied His blessing. Abu Hayyan said: al-Naqqash (d. 351 AH) related that it was reported that the disbelievers said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Return, O Muhammad, to our religion, worship our gods, and leave what you are upon, and we will guarantee for you everything you need in your worldly life and your afterlife." So this verse was revealed. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 6, verse 165:

When he had mentioned that He is the One who benefits every thing through His lordship, and concluded with the warning of the gathering (al-hashr), he followed this with a reminder of their being singled out for benefaction. He said, linking it to ﴿And He is the Lord of every thing﴾ [al-An'am: 164], seeking their favour toward Him by reminding them of His blessing: ﴿And He﴾, that is, not other than Him, ﴿is the One who made you﴾, that is, O humankind, ﴿successors (khala'if) on the earth﴾, that is, you act in it as a successor does, empowered to do whatever you wish. It is also permissible that by this the Arabs be meant, and the apparent sense of the speech is that by "the earth" is meant the Arabian Peninsula where they were, while its inner meaning is the good tidings of the elevation of their religion, Islam, over every religion, and their dominion over most of the people of the earth in these times and over all the people of the earth at the end of time. ﴿And He raised some of you﴾ in the ranks of intellect, knowledge, religion, wealth, rank, physical strength and moral strength, ﴿above others in degrees﴾, that is, although you are all from a single soul. Perhaps the lowly person is more intelligent than the exalted one, yet his intelligence did not benefit him. This clearly indicates that all of that is the act of the One, the Subduer, not from incapacity, ignorance or miserliness. Then he explained this by His saying: ﴿that He may try you﴾, that is, He acts toward you as one who tests, in order to establish the proof against you, while He is more knowing of you than you are yourselves, ﴿in what He has given you﴾. Thus He observes whether the mighty shows mercy to the lowly, whether the poor is content with His meagre gift, whether the strong gives thanks, and whether the weak is patient!

When he had mentioned the superiority of some of them over others, and since it is in human nature to be arrogant, he followed this with a warning to the wrongdoer and an appeal to the penitent, by what indicates, through His own exalted station and great power, the weakness of the one on high among them and his inability to punish the one below him, since there may be an intercessor or helper standing between them, and by what he needs of preparing the means, warning against transgression and disobedience. He said, addressing the most perfect of creation to comfort his heart, informing him that his Lord had nurtured him in the most beautiful upbringing and had disciplined him in the best discipline: ﴿Indeed, your Lord﴾, that is, the One who does good to you, ﴿is swift in punishment﴾, that is, toward whoever He wishes to punish among those who deny His blessing, because nothing stands between Him and the one He wants to punish, and He does not need to bring forth the instruments of punishment; rather, whatever He wills is present with Him, ready.

﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Ya-Sin: 82]. In this there is a severe threat to whoever does not take heed.

When He had threatened and frightened, He gave hope to whoever wished to repent and sought to win him over, so He said: ﴿And indeed, He is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾, informing that He, despite His complete power over them and their immersion in what necessitates destruction, is abundant in forgiveness toward them and great in mercy. ﴿Had Allah taken people to account for their wrongdoing, He would not have left upon it a single creature﴾ [al-Nahl: 61], urging the exalted to pardon the lowly. The emphasis of the second clause without the first is in view of His saying: ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ [al-An'am: 12], and the hadith "My mercy precedes My wrath." This is because it is within the context of disciplining this community and reminding them of the favour bestowed upon them by making them successors. It will come in al-A'raf with the emphasis on both, because it is in the narration of what befell the Children of Israel of their hastening into disbelief, their rushing to it, and their deserving punishment for that. This came in the manner of a resumptive sentence (isti'naf), on the presumption that someone said: "Then the exalted would hasten to punish the lowly!" So it was answered that Allah is above all, and He is swifter in punishment, for He is able to empower the lowly, or one lower than him, over the exalted, so that he destroys him.

Then, after this intimidation, He encouraged pardon, for He, despite being independent of all, let down the skirt of His forgiveness and mercy by granting the disobedient respite and accepting the little of acts of obedience, by having created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light as benefits for them, yet they, with Him, ascribe equals! Had it not been for His forgiveness and mercy, His punishment would have hastened upon whoever set up another as equal to Him, and He would have dropped the heavens upon them and sunk the earths beneath them, the earths in which He bestowed upon them the favour of succession, and removed the light from them and perpetuated the darkness. Thus He concluded the surah with that with which He began it: for His saying ﴿And He it is who made you successors on the earth﴾ is what is meant by His saying ﴿He it is who created you from clay﴾ [al-An'am: 2], and His saying ﴿Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, when He is the Lord of every thing?﴾ [al-An'am: 164] is the meaning of His saying ﴿created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 1]. And Allah is the Granter of success.
